Quick Start

### Build, preview, deploy Run the documentation pipeline from the repository root.

make serve PORT=8001
make deploy

Pipeline

omp skills: the pstack skills inside every seat
docs.text: omp 18.11.3 (@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent, installed under ~/.local/lib/node_modules/@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent; paths below are relative to it) loads the skills under ~/.agents/skills into every seat. This page names the setting that pins that, where the skills come from, how to prove what a seat loads, and how a seat's own skill coexists with the pstack set. Facts marked "measured" come from the U10 dry run of 2026-10-23 under a scratch HOME.

docs.title: The key
docs.text:
skills.customDirectories in ~/.omp/agent/config.yml.

  • omp registers it at src/extensibility/settings.ts:65-69 (type array, default empty) and reads it in loadSkills at src/extensibility/skills.ts:471-480: each entry goes through expandTilde, is scanned one level deep for */SKILL.md, and is admitted under the provider id custom at level user with requireDescription: true.
  • The manifest home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml holds the list as omp.skills_directories (default ~/.agents/skills, the same root as skills.canonical_dir). scripts/generate-agent-configs.py validates it (~/ or absolute, no shell characters) and renders home/.chezmoitemplates/omp-config-managed.yml; make render-check fails when the template is stale.
  • home/dot_omp/private_agent/modify_private_config.yml merges modelRoles.default, skills.customDirectories, the top-level extensions list (docs/pi-claude-bridge.md, "Plain launch") and disabledProviders (the manifest's omp.disabled_providers, the same list the seat overlays carry; it keeps the retired openai-codex route unselectable on a plain launch too) into the live file and keeps every other key omp wrote. It writes the directories with ~ expanded to $HOME, because omp skill list resolves a non-absolute entry against the inspected directory before omp expands ~ (src/cli/skill-list.ts:58-64); measured, ~/.agents/skills lists nothing through that command while the absolute path lists the skills. A second apply is a no-op (tests/unit/test_omp_config_merge.py).
  • The merge reaches the default profile only. A seat started with omp --profile <name> reads ~/.omp/profiles/<name>/agent/config.yml instead (pi-utils src/dirs.ts:312-315), so a named profile gets the key, and its model route, from the per-role overlay below.

docs.title: Per-role overlays
docs.text:
~/.agents/omp/profiles/<role>.yml, one file per key of omp.roles in the manifest (orchestrator: deep, worker: standard, audit: audit, review: review, security: security). Each holds modelRoles.default from the mapped profile's omp.model and skills.customDirectories from omp.skills_directories; the seat launcher passes the role's file as a second --config beside the policy overlay (home/dot_agents/omp/policies/<role>.yml), so a named profile gets its model route and skill roots without a hand edit of ~/.omp/profiles/<role>/agent/config.yml.

  • scripts/generate-agent-configs.py renders them as home/dot_agents/omp/profiles/<role>.yml.tmpl; make render-check fails when a file is stale, and the generator fails when omp.roles is missing, names an unknown profile, or carries a role name that is not launcher-safe. tests/unit/test_generate_agent_configs.py holds the cases and checks that every policy file has an overlay.
  • The committed file is a chezmoi template so that the deployed file carries the absolute home ({{ .chezmoi.homeDir }}/.agents/skills) while the repository stays machine-independent. The absolute form is needed because omp expands ~ in skills.customDirectories only on the session route (loadSkills, src/extensibility/skills.ts:471-473); omp skill list resolves a non-absolute entry against the inspected directory first (src/cli/skill-list.ts:58-64), and measured, the ~ form lists nothing there. modelRoles.default is a plain string copied from the layer (src/config/model-settings.ts:109, src/config/settings.ts:1626-1638) and gets no path handling.
  • Each overlay also carries setupVersion: 2 and startup.setupWizard: false. A seat profile has no ~/.omp/profiles/<role>/agent/config.yml, so setupVersion reads its schema default 0 (src/modes/settings.ts:28), the cold-launch gate sees it below CURRENT_SETUP_VERSION 2 (src/main.ts:668-671, pi-tui src/setup/setup-version.ts:11) and runs the first-run wizard over the pane (measured 2026-10-23 on the worker and orchestrator seats: Setup step 1 of 5 / Sign in to your providers, where a keypress starts a provider login). startup.setupWizard: false (src/modes/settings.ts:1085-1095) empties the scene list (pi-tui src/setup/wizard.ts:52), and setupVersion: 2 keeps the gate from importing the wizard at all (src/main.ts:669-672).
  • An overlay wins over the profile's own config.yml key by key: runtime override → config overlay → project → global → schema default (src/config/settings.ts:879). --config and PI_CONFIG_FILES feed the same list (src/config/settings.ts:674-676) and the same strict loader, which refuses a missing file (Config overlay not found) or a non-mapping (src/config/settings.ts:2506-2528).
  • The listing and read-back commands take the overlay through PI_CONFIG_FILES only: omp skill list (src/cli/skill-list.ts:47) and omp config get (src/cli/config-cli.ts:164) call Settings.init without the parsed --config list, which an interactive or -p session passes (src/main.ts:1886). Measured, omp --profile u14test --config <overlay> --no-extensions skill list --json returns {"skills":[],"warnings":[]} under a profile that turns the agents provider off, while the same overlay through PI_CONFIG_FILES lists the skills.

Dry run of 2026-10-23, omp 18.11.3, wrapper HOME=$TMPDIR/u14-home, cwd an empty directory, ~/.omp/profiles/u14test/agent/config.yml = skills: {enableAgentsUser: false} (so only the overlay can supply the skills), ~/.agents/skills/{sharpen,unslop} linked from the pstack tree, overlay = the worker template rendered by chezmoi execute-template under the same HOME.

command result omp --profile u14test --no-extensions skill list --json {"skills":[],"warnings":[]} PI_CONFIG_FILES=<overlay> omp --profile u14test --no-extensions skill list --json sharpen and unslop, "source":"custom:user", "warnings":[] PI_CONFIG_FILES=<overlay with ~/.agents/skills> omp … skill list --json {"skills":[],"warnings":[]} PI_CONFIG_FILES=<missing file> omp … skill list --json skill list: Config overlay not found: <path> PI_CONFIG_FILES=<overlay> omp --profile u14test config get modelRoles --json "value": {"default": "claude-bridge/claude-opus-5-5"} omp --profile u14test config get modelRoles --json "value": {}

docs.title: The directory
docs.text:
~/.agents/skills (manifest skills.canonical_dir). omp scans it on two routes:

  • The agents provider (src/discovery/agents.ts:30 and :124-127, loader :158-174) scans ~/.agent/skills and ~/.agents/skills at the user level and .agent/skills and .agents/skills on the walk up from the project. Its user level is on by default: skills.enableAgentsUser defaults to true (src/extensibility/settings.ts:57, gate at src/extensibility/skills.ts:322), and .agents is not a foreign provider, so enabledProviders does not apply to it (src/capability/index.ts:363-373; upstream docs/skills.md, "Source toggles and filtering"). enabledProviders opts the foreign user roots in (~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.cursor; default off), but the agent-plugins provider, which reads the Claude Code marketplace registry under ~/.claude and refused pstack's plugin copy with 56 warnings, is not one of them: the seat overlays switch it off with disabledProviders: [agent-plugins] (omp.disabled_providers in the manifest, regime-cutover U22).
  • skills.customDirectories, the key above. It pins the root against a seat setting that turns the provider off (skills.enableAgentsUser: false, or disabledProviders naming agents).

With both routes on, each skill is listed once with no warning. Measured: source is agents:user, because the provider copy is admitted first and the custom copy of the same real path is skipped (src/extensibility/skills.ts:466-467).

docs.title: The instrument
docs.text:
omp skill list [dir] [--json] (src/cli/skill-list.ts:94-123) discovers skills for a directory exactly as a session would (:27-29) and prints one name<TAB>description row per skill, or the full result with --json. The --mode json session route of the pilot facts shows the same set through the system prompt, at the cost of a model turn; the listing command needs none.

Dry run of 2026-10-23, omp 18.11.3, wrapper HOME=$TMPDIR/u10-home, ~/.agents/skills/{sharpen,unslop} linked from the pstack tree, cwd an empty directory. Each row is the full stdout of omp skill list --json.

~/.omp/agent/config.yml result absent sharpen and unslop, "source":"agents:user", "warnings":[] skills: {enableAgentsUser: false} {"skills":[],"warnings":[]} the row above, then the modify script merged the rendered key (customDirectories: [/…/u10-home/.agents/skills]) sharpen and unslop, "source":"custom:user", "warnings":[] skills: {customDirectories: [/…/u10-home/.agents/skills]} (the deployed state) sharpen and unslop, "source":"agents:user", "warnings":[]

Both skills list with "hide":true: their front matter sets disable-model-invocation: true, which omp maps to hide (src/extensibility/skills.ts:463). A hidden skill is left out of the system prompt's <skills> listing and stays reachable through /skill:<name> and skill://<name> (:37-42). 56 of the 57 skills in pstack 0.15.30 set that flag.

docs.title: The pin
docs.text:
assets.pstack in home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml: pin is a commit of cursor/plugins and sha256 the digest of GitHub's source archive of that commit (https://github.com/cursor/plugins/archive/<pin>.tar.gz). Two chezmoi externals in home/.chezmoitemplates/chezmoiexternal.d/common.yaml.tmpl read both values from the manifest (include + fromYaml, so the pin lives in one place) and extract harness/pstack/claude-code/skills/* into ~/.agents/skills and harness/pstack/claude-code/docs/** into ~/.agents/docs at every chezmoi apply, which make update runs. harness/pstack/claude-code is the Claude Code build of the plugin, the tree the cursor-plugins marketplace entry points at, so a seat reads the same bytes as the Claude Code plugin install; the docs land beside the skills because every skill's first paragraph links ../../docs/harness/claude-code.md. No installer step, clone or receipt exists. chezmoi checks the download against sha256 and fetches the archive again only when the URL, that is the pin, changes, since refreshPeriod stays at its default of zero (chezmoi reference, .chezmoiexternal format: checksum.sha256, stripComponents, include, exact, refreshPeriod); chezmoi status reports drift in the deployed files.

Measured 2026-10-23 under HOME=$TMPDIR/u10b-home with the rendered externals pointed at the downloaded archive (tests/unit/test_pstack_asset.py repeats the run with a fixture archive): chezmoi apply placed the 57 skill directories beside a source skill, ~/.agents/docs/harness/claude-code.md included; a second apply changed nothing; omp --no-session skill list --json from an empty directory listed 58 skills with "warnings":[], poteto-mode among them with "hide":true. A pstack skill named like a skill under home/dot_agents/skills makes chezmoi refuse the whole apply (inconsistent state, both sources named) instead of overwriting either copy; the test also keeps the two name sets disjoint. make doctor runs scripts/update-agent-assets.sh check_pstack, which fails when poteto-mode/SKILL.md or the adapter file is missing or when omp skill list does not name poteto-mode. A skill upstream drops stays deployed until a .chezmoiremove entry removes it, because ~/.agents/skills is not an exact directory (other installers own siblings there); ~/.agents/docs is exact.

docs.title: A seat's skill beside the pstack skills
docs.text:
A seat's own skill (the planned hcom-worker, for example) is one more <name>/SKILL.md under the same ~/.agents/skills root, or under the project's .agents/skills, and needs no further setting. omp resolves the two sets by name (src/extensibility/skills.ts:120-139; upstream docs/skills.md, "Collision and duplicate handling"):

  • Different names coexist. This is the normal case: pstack names are principle-*, correct, sharpen, unslop and so on; a seat skill carries the seat's name.
  • The same name with identical content is loaded once.
  • The same name with different content keeps the bare name for the higher-precedence copy (a custom-directory skill outranks a provider skill; otherwise the first admitted) and namespaces the other as <namespace>/<name> with a warning in the listing. Rename the seat skill rather than rely on that.
  • A seat skill the model should pick up on its own must not set disable-model-invocation: true; the pstack skills set it and are invoked by name, which is how poteto-mode addresses them.

docs.title: openai-siwc: omp provider for Sign in with ChatGPT
docs.text:
Design for the omp 18.11.3 extension at home/dot_agents/omp/extensions/openai-siwc/. It gives the audit-side omp profiles ChatGPT plan inference through OpenAI's official Sign in with ChatGPT (SIWC) route, which omp does not ship (issue can1357/oh-my-pi#13974, facts §3). The package loads in omp 18.11.3 and registers the provider; it has not yet run a real login or completion (gate G2). The points that still need a real-endpoint measurement carry TODO(gate G2) and are listed under open questions.

Sources: .orchestration/validation/025-v13-facts-20261023.md (facts §3, §3b, §4), .orchestration/validation/025-pilot-facts.md #S0, the probe .orchestration/validation/025-pilot-s0-siwc-probe.py, red-team row R12R-07, the installed omp source under ~/.local/lib/node_modules/@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent (paths below are relative to it), and upstream docs/extensions.md and docs/provider-compat-reference.md (main, fetched 2026-10-23).

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
omp's built-in openai-responses transport already streams the Responses API, parses SSE, retries, and surfaces response.completed. The SIWC preview accepts a narrower request than omp builds. Measured against omp's real builder with a fake HTTP layer (the test tests/requests.test.ts), a provider named openai-siwc on https://api.openai.com/v1 sends prompt_cache_retention: "24h", max_output_tokens, and the system prompt as an input item with role: "developer". The preview rejects all three, and it needs store: false, stream: true, and full history instead of previous_response_id.

Login is the other gap. SIWC registers each host dynamically: the first authorize request uses client_id=dynamic_agent_client plus ext_agent_host_id, and the callback returns the issued client_id that every later exchange and refresh must use. pi-ai's OAuthCallbackFlow cannot carry that value, because its callback handler keeps only code and state (node_modules/@oh-my-pi/pi-ai/src/registry/oauth/callback-server.ts:560-576).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
The operator installs the package once and logs in once per profile:

omp --profile audit -e ~/.agents/omp/extensions/openai-siwc
/login openai-siwc
/model openai-siwc/gpt-6.1-sol

What the extension does at load:

export default function openaiSiwc(pi: ExtensionAPI): void {
  pi.registerProvider("openai-siwc", {
    baseUrl: "https://api.openai.com/v1",
    api: "openai-responses",
    compat: SIWC_COMPAT,
    oauth: createSiwcOAuth({
      agentDir: pi.pi.getAgentDir(),
      agentName: "omp-dotfiles",
    }),
    models: MODELS,
  });
  pi.on("before_provider_request", (event, ctx) =>
    ctx.model?.provider === "openai-siwc"
      ? rewriteResponsesRequest(event.payload)
      : undefined,
  );
}

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
Module Owns src/index.ts The registerProvider call, the static model rows, and the before_provider_request hook. src/oauth.ts The oauth block: authorize URL, PKCE, loopback receiver, code exchange, refresh, scope and nonce checks. src/requests.ts SIWC_COMPAT and rewriteResponsesRequest, the only place that knows the preview's request rules. src/store.ts The per-profile registration record: its path, validation, and atomic 0600 write. It is the record's single writer, called by oauth.ts.

The package has no runtime dependencies. It imports omp only as types (import type), which Bun erases.

docs.title: Registration record
docs.text:
One JSON file per omp profile at <agentDir>/openai-siwc/registration.json, where agentDir is getAgentDir() and therefore follows --profile (pilot facts #B3):

interface Registration {
  hostId: `urn:uuid:${string}`; // uuid4; a bare uuid was refused (pilot facts #S0 run 1)
  clientId?: string; // issued by the registration callback (prefix "oaiapp" measured)
  accountId?: string; // from the id_token account claim, when present
}

The record holds no secret. clientId is a public client identifier, and tokens never enter this file. Load rejects a malformed record instead of re-registering over it.

docs.title: OAuthCredentials mapping
docs.text:
Tokens live in omp's own credential store, <agentDir>/agent.db, which omp creates with directory mode 0700 and file mode 0600 (node_modules/@oh-my-pi/pi-ai/src/auth/sqlite-credential-store.ts:587-594).

OAuthCredentials field Source access access_token; getApiKey returns it and omp sends it as the bearer. refresh refresh_token, replaced on every refresh. expires now + expires_in × 1000; expires_in measured as 3600. accountId id_token claim https://api.openai.com/auth → chatgpt_account_id (TODO(gate G2)). email id_token claim email. issued client_id Not in OAuthCredentials, which has no field for it; kept in the registration record.

docs.title: Login flow
docs.text:
1. Load the registration record. When none exists, create one with a fresh urn:uuid: host id and save it before opening the browser, so a retried first login reuses the same host id.
  2. Create a PKCE S256 pair, a fresh state, and a fresh OIDC nonce.
  3. Bind the loopback receiver on 127.0.0.1 (never localhost), port 1455 when free, otherwise a random port. The redirect URI is http://127.0.0.1:<port>/auth/callback.
  4. Build the authorize URL on https://auth.openai.com/api/accounts/authorize with response_type=code, the scopes openid profile email offline_access resource.invoke chatgpt.tokens.use.direct, resource=https://api.openai.com/v1, the PKCE challenge, state, nonce, and ext_agent_host_id. A first login sends client_id=dynamic_agent_client and agent_name_hint=omp-dotfiles. A later login sends the saved client_id and no name hint.
  5. Hand the URL to omp through callbacks.onAuth; omp opens the system browser.
  6. The receiver answers only GET /auth/callback. A callback whose state is not ours gets a 400 page and is ignored, because any local process can send one. A callback with our state and error ends the login. A callback with our state and code resolves it. The wait honours callbacks.signal and a 5-minute timeout.
  7. Save the callback's client_id into the record when it differs from the saved one. The server is authoritative, and saving before the exchange keeps a failed exchange from causing a second registration.
  8. Exchange the code at https://auth.openai.com/api/accounts/oauth/token, form-encoded, with grant_type=authorization_code, the issued client_id, code, code_verifier, the same redirect_uri, and the same resource. No client secret.
  9. Refuse the grant unless its scope contains chatgpt.tokens.use.direct. A valid ID token alone does not authorize plan usage (sign-in page, facts §4). Refuse an id_token whose nonce differs from ours.

docs.title: Refresh
docs.text: The access token lives 1 hour; the refresh token lives 30 days and rotates on every refresh (token reference, facts §4). refreshToken posts grant_type=refresh_token with the saved client_id, the stored refresh_token, and resource. It returns the replacement refresh token and keeps the old one only when a response omits it. Without a saved client_id it fails with an instruction to run /login openai-siwc. When a refresh response carries scope, the plan scope is checked again; an absent scope is accepted on refresh only (TODO(gate G2)).

docs.title: Request rewrite
docs.text:
Two layers, both on omp's own transport. SIWC_COMPAT stops omp from building most rejected shapes. rewriteResponsesRequest runs on every payload through before_provider_request, which omp passes to the transport as onPayload (src/sdk.ts:4345-4346), and the transport calls it for the first request and for both retry paths (node_modules/@oh-my-pi/pi-ai/src/providers/openai-responses.ts:852-859, :1008, :1055). Line references below are in node_modules/@oh-my-pi/pi-ai/src/providers/.

omp-emitted field or item Where omp emits it Handling role: "developer" system items in input openai-responses.ts:1640, when supportsDeveloperRole resolves true Compat supportsDeveloperRole: false sends the system prompt as instructions (:1660). The rewrite folds any remaining system or developer message item into instructions, which also covers the Juice item (:1779-1782). prompt_cache_retention: "24h" openai-responses.ts:1663 Compat supportsLongPromptCacheRetention: false; the rewrite deletes the field. max_output_tokens openai-responses.ts:1677, openai-shared.ts:4082 The rewrite deletes it. No compat key turns it off, and omitMaxOutputTokens is not accepted on an extension model row. temperature, top_p openai-shared.ts:4091-4092, only when sampling params are supported The rewrite deletes them. store openai-responses.ts:1671, true only with compat.storeResponses (:548) The rewrite forces store: false. previous_response_id with delta-only input openai-responses.ts:567 (PI_OPENAI_STATEFUL), :836 forces store: true Compat statefulResponses: false turns chaining off. PI_OPENAI_STATEFUL outranks compat, so the extension refuses to load when it is truthy (src/index.ts). The rewrite still throws on the field, but that only reports: omp's runner catches a hook throw and sends the unrewritten payload (src/extensibility/extensions/runner.ts:1590-1591, :1627-1632, :2121-2131). configuration_update input items Stable-effort policy (supportsConfigurationUpdate, provider-compat-reference) Compat supportsConfigurationUpdate: false. Other preview-rejected fields Not emitted by the 18.11.3 builder for this provider The rewrite deletes background, conversation, max_tool_calls, metadata, moderation, multi_agent, prompt, safety_identifier, top_logprobs, truncation, user in case a hook or a later omp adds them. prompt_cache_key, include, reasoning, stream_options Emitted (measured in the test's captured body) Kept. The preview does not list them as rejected. TODO(gate G2): confirm on the real endpoint.

stream: true is forced too. The rewrite copies the payload and never mutates omp's object.

docs.title: Error mapping
docs.text:
OpenAI's SIWC docs (https://developers.openai.com/siwc/llms-full.txt, "Errors and recovery", Structured Responses errors, read 2026-10-25) give each code its status and recovery. subscription_sharing_user_not_eligible (403) means "ChatGPT plan usage is unavailable for the selected user, workspace, or policy"; do not repeat the request. subscription_sharing_usage_limit_exceeded (429) says to "Pause new requests that use the user's ChatGPT plan" and warns "Do not assume the entire plan is empty or infer a reset time from this code alone; an app-specific limit can also apply". subscription_sharing_usage_unavailable (503) means "Usage availability could not be checked. Preserve credentials and retry later with bounded backoff"; it is not a spent or unavailable plan. The extension adds no error code of its own: omp's classifier already handles all three, and tests/requests.test.ts proves it through omp's real transport with fake 403, 429 and 503 bodies.

Code Fake response What omp 18.11.3 does omp hook subscription_sharing_user_not_eligible HTTP 403 One request, then an error event naming the code. AIError.retriable is false, so the session does not retry the turn. isTransientStatus excludes 403 (pi-ai/src/error/retryable.ts:20-22); isProviderRetryableError treats every 4xx but 408/429 as terminal (:44-49). subscription_sharing_usage_limit_exceeded HTTP 429 Classified Flag.UsageLimit (the code matches usage.?limit, pi-ai/src/error/rate-limit.ts:337), so isProviderRetryableError is false (retryable.ts:46) and the session hands it to omp's usage-limit recovery (wait for a reset within retry.maxDelayMs, or rotate to a sibling credential). The transport still sends 6 requests first. none reachable, see below subscription_sharing_usage_unavailable HTTP 503 A transient failure: the transport sends 6 requests, then an error event naming the code, and isProviderRetryableError is true, so the session may retry the turn. This matches the docs' bounded backoff; credentials are kept. none needed

The transport retry is the gap. postOpenAIStream sends through fetchWithRetry with 6 attempts (pi-ai/src/utils/openai-http.ts:33, :100-117), which retries every 429 unless the response carries a retry hint above 60 s or a proxy concurrency marker (pi-utils/src/fetch-retry.ts:375-382). The only caller gate, shouldRetryResponse, is built from omp-internal state (openai-responses.ts:903-905), and the fetch override reaches the transport only through SimpleStreamOptions.fetch (pi-ai/src/types.ts:716-723), which the session never sets for a built-in api. A before_provider_request hook sees only the payload, and after_provider_response fires only after a 2xx (openai-responses.ts:914, after postOpenAIStream has thrown on any other status). So on the built-in openai-responses transport no extension hook stops those 5 resends. With omp's default backoff they take about 15 s and spend nothing, because the server refuses each one. The custom-api candidate below would own the fetch; it is not taken, because it renames the session's model.api and so silently changes every omp branch keyed on "openai-responses" (src/utils/tool-choice.ts:17-23, src/tools/think.ts:31-36, src/session/agent-session.ts:11043, :11090-11094, src/sdk.ts:1610-1612). The test pins the 6 requests, so an omp release that adds a gate fails it.

Operating rules that follow from the docs and the SIWC Terms (https://openai.com/policies/sign-in-with-chatgpt-terms/, read 2026-10-25):

  • On subscription_sharing_usage_limit_exceeded, stop sending new requests on the profile and read ChatGPT Settings > Usage, under App limits (help article https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001542). Do not probe the route to learn whether the limit has reset: the article says "An app can reach its own limit even when your ChatGPT plan still has usage available" and "Signing in again or repeatedly retrying does not restore your usage".
  • Keep one SIWC account per omp profile. omp's usage-limit recovery can rotate to a sibling credential of the same provider, and the Terms (§4) forbid enabling "Creating multiple accounts, splitting usage, rotating accounts, or otherwise bypassing usage limits". A second account stored under the same profile would let omp do exactly that.

docs.title: Synthesis decision
docs.text: The architect skill's single-runner form was used, with the arena skipped by the brief. Two whole shapes were sketched. The base is the payload-hook shape (built-in openai-responses transport, compat, and a before_provider_request rewrite). The rejected candidate registered a custom api with streamSimple, wrapping pi-ai's streamSimple with its own fetch. It would own error mapping at the HTTP layer, but built-in api ids are reserved (node_modules/@oh-my-pi/pi-ai/src/api-registry.ts:65-69), so it needs a new api id and must re-target each model to openai-responses before delegating, which ties the extension to omp's internal model shape. U3b confirmed it is the only shape that reaches the transport's 429 retry, and kept it rejected: renaming the session's model.api changes more omp behaviour than five refused resends cost (Error mapping above).

docs.title: Tradeoffs accepted
docs.text:
• We accept depending on before_provider_request reaching every request in exchange for reusing omp's transport, SSE parsing, and retries unchanged. Upstream documents that transports must invoke onPayload and that devin-agent does not; openai-responses does.
  • We accept a hand-written loopback receiver of about 40 lines in exchange for capturing the issued client_id, which OAuthCallbackFlow drops.
  • We accept static model rows in exchange for no discovery call, since GET /v1/models returned no entries on this route.
  • We accept one registration per profile, so three audit profiles mean three agent entries in the ChatGPT account (red-team R12R-06 proposed one shared record). The brief fixes the record per profile.

docs.title: Threat table
docs.text: Asset or boundary Threat Control Test Token store Another local user reads access or refresh tokens. Tokens stay in omp's agent.db (dir 0700, file 0600, sqlite-credential-store.ts:587-594). The extension writes no token anywhere. tests/oauth.test.ts: tokens only in returned credentials. Registration record Tampering or a half-written file causes a re-registration. Atomic write (temp file, rename) with 0600 file and 0700 directory; strict validation on load and save. tests/store.test.ts: modes 0600 and 0700, bare uuid refused. Loopback port Another process holds 1455 or listens on ::1. Bind 127.0.0.1 only, as the docs require; fall back to a random port, which the docs allow. tests/oauth.test.ts loopback test (skipped where binding is refused). Redirect validation A forged local request injects a code (login CSRF). Only GET /auth/callback; state must match; a foreign state is ignored, not fatal; the first accepted callback settles the wait; PKCE S256 binds the code to this process; id_token nonce must match when present. tests/oauth.test.ts: foreign state ignored, PKCE checked by the fake. Grant scope An identity-only grant is used for inference. Login refuses a grant without chatgpt.tokens.use.direct. tests/oauth.test.ts: scope refusal. Log redaction Tokens or codes reach logs or error messages. The extension logs nothing. Token errors carry only the OAuth error and error_description, capped at 200 characters; request bodies are never echoed. The callback page shows no parameters. Review only. Hosts Traffic leaves the two named hosts. Constants only: auth.openai.com for authorize and token, api.openai.com for inference. No discovery or telemetry call. tests/fake-auth-server.ts asserts both URLs.

docs.title: Open questions and risks
docs.text:
• Does a later sign-in with the issued client_id accept ext_agent_host_id? Default: send it, because the sign-in page marks it required. G2's second login per profile measures it.
  • Does a refresh response carry scope, and does the SIWC id_token carry the Codex account claim? Defaults: accept an absent scope on refresh; leave accountId empty when the claim is absent.
  • Is gpt-6-astra served on this route? Assumption (【仮定】): yes. It ships as a static row next to the measured gpt-6.1-sol, both text-only, with the limits of omp's openai/<id> catalog rows. fetchDynamicModels is not registered, because GET /v1/models returned no entries (#S0).
  • What HTTP status carries each subscription error? Default: rely on omp's classifier, which handles a 403 and a 429 as the table above shows.
  • Should three profiles share one registration (R12R-06)? Default: one per profile, as the brief specifies.
  • Are prompt_cache_key, include, reasoning and stream_options accepted? Default: keep them.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Gate G2: the operator runs /login openai-siwc and one -p turn in each audit-side profile (audit, audit-r2, security), as the package README lists, which answers the first four questions.

docs.title: The orchestrator seat: stop gate, skill and doctor wiring
docs.text: Plan 025 W6b (U9). The orchestrator seat is the omp process that scripts/orchestrator/hcom-seat orchestrator starts in the repository checkout. This page covers the three pieces that make it able to run the program loop: the session_stop gate that keeps it from ending a turn while it owes the bus a reply, the hcom-orchestration skill that is its playbook, and the make doctor line that proves the bridge it talks through still loads. omp paths below are relative to ~/.local/lib/node_modules/@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent (omp 18.11.3); facts marked measured come from the U9 scratch runs of 2026-10-23 under HOME=$TMPDIR/u9-home.

docs.title: The stop gate
docs.text: home/dot_agents/omp/hooks/stop-gate.ts, applied to ~/.agents/omp/hooks/stop-gate.ts. It is an omp extension loaded with -e ~/.agents/omp/hooks: a configured directory without a package.json manifest or an index.ts is scanned one level deep for .ts files (src/extensibility/extensions/directory-resolution.ts:101-140, called from loader.ts:652), so the tests/ directory beside it is not loaded. hcom-seat passes -e ~/.agents/omp/hooks on every launch, whatever the role or --ext (U33c). Before U33c no seat loaded it: on 2026-10-24 the orchestrator, audit and worker seats ran omp with -e for the pi-claude-bridge, the openai-siwc extension and hcom's own hcom.ts only (ps, pids 42205, 8361 and 5621), so the gate described here never ran in an hcom seat until then.

docs.title: The event
docs.text:
omp fires session_stop when a main-agent turn is about to settle (src/extensibility/shared-events.ts:109-119, "handlers may request one continuation turn"); an extension subscribes with pi.on("session_stop", …) (src/extensibility/extensions/types.ts:1661). This is omp's native blocking stop hook, so no fallback is needed:

  • A handler result {decision: "block", reason} makes the runner return at once (src/extensibility/extensions/runner.ts:1689-1692) and the session queue a hidden continuation turn whose content is reason (src/session/agent-session.ts:5196-5198, :5291-5301). The model sees the reason as context and gets another turn.
  • event.stop_hook_active is true while a continuation the gate asked for is settling (agent-session.ts:5264, set at :5290).
  • A block is exempt from the continuation cap (agent-session.ts:5276), so a gate that blocked every settle could loop for as long as a RESULT never arrives. The gate therefore blocks the first settle and answers {continue: true, reason} while stop_hook_active is set, which the cap SESSION_STOP_CONTINUATION_CAP = 8 bounds (agent-session.ts:470, :5276-5283). After one block and eight continuations omp ends the turn with the warning still printed.
  • Subagents never see the event (agent-session.ts:5254), so the gate applies to the seat's own turns only.

docs.title: The rule
docs.text:
The gate reads the thread's rows since the seat started, ~/.local/bin/common/bus-history.sh <team> --limit 100000 --since <seat start>, and keeps the newest row per task_id among the rows that move a task. The script keeps the newest --limit rows (default 200), so the gate asks for far more than a program writes and treats a full window as unreadable (a warning, the turn ends unchecked) rather than as proof of no debt:

Row, by kind (an older sender's AGMSG- prefix is ignored) and sender Effect on its task_id TASK from the seat open: awaiting RESULT RESULT from a seat the seat's TASK under that id went to (its to column) open: owes a VERDICT, MERGED or HOLD line VERDICT, MERGED or HOLD from the seat closed anything else (PING, every PONG, status=question included, another seat's TASK, MERGED or HOLD, a RESULT on a task the seat did not send to its author, a VERDICT from any other seat, …) no effect; the previous moving row keeps the state

The line kinds are the first word of a bus line: TASK, RESULT, VERDICT, PONG, MERGED and HOLD (plus PING, which moves nothing). A seat that still writes the retired AGMSG- prefix (AGMSG-TASK and so on) is read the same, because the gate strips the prefix before it looks the kind up (U35). There is no audit seat on the bus: every audit is one fresh omp-run.sh --role audit run that the orchestrator starts and reads (the hcom-orchestration skill, step 4), so its verdict reaches the bus only as the orchestrator's own VERDICT line, and another seat's VERDICT closes nothing, on an -audit id or any other (U58).

Every seat loads the gate and shares the thread, so a row from another seat opens a debt only on a task this seat sent to that very seat (U33c): a worker seat never owes anything for a peer's RESULT, and the orchestrator owes a verdict on the RESULTs of the TASKs it sent.

One message lists the open items with their row ids and the ways out: answer them, wait with hcom listen, or send HOLD v1 task_id=<id> note=<why>, the auditable override that the skill names. OMP_STOP_GATE_ALLOW_OPEN=1 ends the turn with the warning instead of the block.

docs.title: The seat's environment
docs.text:
Variable Meaning Set by HCOM_DIR the program's private bus store, read by bus-history.sh the environment when set; else hcom-seat derives ~/.local/state/hcom/<slug> from the checkout (regime-env, U33) and exports it; hcom passes it to the seat HCOM_TEAM the thread every TASK line of the program names hcom does not pass it into the pane it launches (measured in the U33 pilot), so hcom-seat passes the team it was given, explicit or derived, as --hcom-team <team>; the gate reads that flag, else HCOM_TEAM, never a team derived from the cwd, and exports the result as HCOM_TEAM into the seat at session start (U33c) HCOM_NAME the seat's own hcom name; absent, hcom list self name hcom, when it exports it; else the command (hcom list --help) OMP_STOP_GATE_ALLOW_OPEN 1 ends the turn with the warning the operator, never the seat

<slug> is the main checkout's basename, lower-cased, [^a-z0-9_-] as -, at most 40 characters (README.md, "Run a program in another repository"). Without a team (no --hcom-team and no HCOM_TEAM, or one outside the team grammar) or a seat name the gate is inert and says so at every stop; a bus-history.sh failure ends the turn with the failure in the warning. Both are visible, never silent (M-20261023-01). In print mode (omp -p, omp-run.sh) there is no UI, so the warning goes to stderr, which omp-run.sh holds and replays; interactively it is ctx.ui.notify(…, "warning").

docs.title: Measured
docs.text:
• bun test home/dot_agents/omp/hooks/tests/stop-gate.test.ts: 7 tests, 25 assertions, pass (U9c run, 2026-10-23). They cover the open and closed transitions above, the three VERDICTs that settle nothing, the exact message, the block on the first settle and the capped continuation on the next, OMP_STOP_GATE_ALLOW_OPEN, the inert case, and the bus-history.sh argv (<team> --since <ISO second>Z).
  • U33c, 2026-10-24: bun test home/dot_agents/omp/hooks/tests/stop-gate.test.ts, 11 pass, adding the flag over HCOM_TEAM over nothing (a regime-env beside the installed bus-history.sh is never consulted), the team grammar, and a peer's RESULT that opens nothing. Under a scratch HOME, a probe extension that registers hcom-team saw getFlag undefined while loading and "custom" at session_start for omp -e probe.ts --hcom-team custom --mode rpc --no-session (also --hcom-team=regime), and omp without an extension that registers it exits 2 with Error: unknown flag: --hcom-team. tests/unit/test_hcom_seat.py test_the_team_crosses_the_launch_boundary_as_a_flag_and_the_gate_blocks_on_it launches with HCOM_TEAM=custom through a fake hcom that drops HCOM_TEAM as the real one does, then runs the real gate (tests/launch-driver.ts, under bun) on that argv and environment: it blocks on thread custom, and without the flag it is inert instead of reading the checkout's slug.
  • Load check under HOME=$TMPDIR/u9-home with a fake scripts/orchestrator/bus-history.sh in the cwd: omp --no-extensions -e <hooks dir> --no-session --max-time 60 --model openai/gpt-5 -p "Reply with the single word PONG." exits 1 with error: No API key found for openai.; no Failed to load extension in stderr or in $HOME/.omp/logs/omp.2026-10-23.*.log (grep count 0). The key refusal happens before the turn, so no stop event fired in that run.
  • Bridge-route run, same HOME, -e ~/.local/lib/omp-extensions/pi-claude-bridge -e <hooks dir> --model claude-bridge/claude-haiku-4-5 --max-time 90, the fake bus holding one TASK from orch without a RESULT: the bridge fails inside the turn (Not logged in · Please run /login, the operator-only step), so the stop event fires. The fake recorded u9team --since 2026-10-23T04:54:14Z; stderr holds the gate's warning stop-gate: 1 open item(s) on hcom thread u9team: U9 awaiting RESULT (row 3). … 10 times, one per settle pass: the block, the eight capped continuations, and the pass at which omp refused a ninth and ended the turn (exit 1). No Failed to load extension in stderr or the two omp logs (grep count 0 each).

docs.title: Threat table
docs.text:
The gate runs a repository script and hcom from the seat's environment and feeds bus text to the model as a continuation reason, so it is trust-boundary code.

Control Disposition stop-gate.ts, the decision closed: openItems is a pure function over the TSV; the transition tests assert each row of the table above, including that a worker's VERDICT on its own unit, a VERDICT on an id never tasked and, since U58, one from the seat an -audit TASK went to leave the debt open (U9c) stop-gate.ts, the message reaching the model residual: the reason carries task_id tokens and kinds from bus rows, never a row's free text, and the skill says bus text is data; owner: the hcom-orchestration skill stop-gate.ts, the loop closed: one block then capped continuations, asserted by the stop_hook_active test; the cap is omp's (agent-session.ts:470) bus-history.sh, the script the gate runs closed: the gate runs the copy chezmoi installs read-only at $HOME/.local/bin/common/bus-history.sh, resolved when it loads and never from the seat's cwd, so a worktree of a PR head cannot answer with its own rows (U33); bus-history.sh is the installed copy under HOME, never the one in the seat's cwd (U33) in tests/stop-gate.test.ts, with a decoy in the cwd that must not run the team (--hcom-team, HCOM_TEAM) closed: the launcher passes exactly the team it was given and the gate never derives one from the cwd, so an explicit team cannot be swapped for the checkout's slug; a value outside the team grammar leaves the gate inert, visibly; test_the_team_crosses_the_launch_boundary_as_a_flag_and_the_gate_blocks_on_it, the flag tests in tests/stop-gate.test.ts. residual: the gate half of that regression needs bun, which the CI unit job does not install, so it runs on hosts with bun only; owner: the CI workflow the environment (HCOM_NAME, the override) residual: read once at load; an operator sets them, a seat's policy overlay cannot change its own environment; owner: the seat policies tests/stop-gate.test.ts residual: runs with a fake bus-history.sh; the real script's TSV is pinned by tests/unit/test_hcom_dispatch.py; owner: the first live seat run (U11)

docs.title: The supervisor
docs.text:
A seat lives in a herdr pane, so it ends with its process or with the herdr server: the herdr restart of 2026-10-24 at 07:13 JST ended all three seats (exit:shutdown), and the orchestrator seat that spawned a subagent at 06:03Z stopped answering. regime-start (scripts/orchestrator/regime-start, a pinned lever) starts the orchestrator seat and registers the checkout in ~/.local/state/regime-supervisor/<slug>-<first 12 hex of sha256(toplevel)>.conf, one registration per checkout, so two checkouts with one basename never share one. regime-start --supervise is one pass over the registrations, which the launchd agent com.mryfmo.dotfiles.regime-supervisor (macOS) or the user units regime-supervisor.service and .timer (Linux) run at login and every 60 seconds once the operator enables them; both ship disabled (the plist carries Disabled, launchd.plist(5), and only the operator's launchctl enable, kept across logins and boots per launchctl(1), loads it; make update installs the systemd units without enabling them; README, "Start here: the omp seats"). The pass relaunches a registered orchestrator that is not alive, unless the newest stop event hcom recorded for the last seat (hcom list --stopped <base name>, the (latest) line) is killed by:cli, an hcom kill, which ends the supervision like regime-stop does. A failed launch waits 60 seconds, doubling by saturation to 30 minutes, and the failure counter stops at 9999. regime-start, the pass and regime-stop (which is regime-start --stop) take one host lock: the kernel's flock(2) on ~/.local/state/regime-supervisor/supervisor.lock, held through a descriptor the script keeps open (perl takes it, because macOS ships no flock command). Start and stop wait for it, and a pass that finds it held skips. The kernel releases it only when its last holder exits or dies, so it is never taken over by age or by a pid, no other process can release it, and the file is never removed. A launch runs in subshells that keep the descriptor until the launch and its wait return, so killing regime-start cannot let a stop in while a launch is in flight; hcom-seat and every hcom call get the descriptor closed, so a seat never holds the lock after its launch (measured on this host on 2026-10-24: after regime-start returned, lsof showed no process with the lock open, the seat included, and regime-stop took it at once). So a stop that arrives during a relaunch runs after it and stops the seat it launched. A registration must hold each of its eight keys exactly once (toplevel, hcom_dir, hcom_team, program, seat, base, fails, next), its seat must be orchestrator-<base>, its file name must be the one its own toplevel derives, and a store with an origin file must name that toplevel; one that breaks any of these is skipped and logged and never launched, rewritten or stopped from. A registration that does not parse, an hcom read that fails, or a stop record it cannot read launches nothing. Only the orchestrator is supervised: it relaunches the other seats itself (the skill's step 0).

Measured on this host on 2026-10-24 with the levers of this branch, in a scratch repository u36-pilot with a scratch store and team u36pilot: regime-start launched orchestrator-nori; its omp process was killed with kill <pid>, and one pass relaunched it; a second run used hcom kill, and the pass ended the supervision; a third crash and relaunch ran with the final parser; regime-stop ended it. $T is the scratch directory. The first relaunch line says no stop record because the first parser read the wrong form of hcom list --stopped, the gap this run found (the named form prints (latest) events); the third shows the record it reads now:

2026-10-24T11:01:41Z regime-start launched orchestrator-nori from $T/u36-pilot
2026-10-24T11:01:50Z regime-start found orchestrator-nori alive; registered for the supervisor
2026-10-24T11:02:03Z no orchestrator alive (last seat orchestrator-nori: no stop record); relaunching from $T/u36-pilot
2026-10-24T11:02:04Z relaunched orchestrator-rune
2026-10-24T11:03:25Z orchestrator-rune was stopped with hcom kill; supervision of $T/u36-pilot ends (registration removed)
2026-10-24T11:03:38Z regime-start launched orchestrator-nova from $T/u36-pilot
2026-10-24T11:03:38Z no orchestrator alive (last seat orchestrator-nova: now ago  [process_exit by:system] (latest)); relaunching from $T/u36-pilot
2026-10-24T11:03:39Z relaunched orchestrator-nene
2026-10-24T11:03:46Z regime-stop: supervision of $T/u36-pilot ended
2026-10-24T11:03:47Z regime-stop: stopped orchestrator-nene

docs.title: The skill
docs.text: home/dot_agents/skills/hcom-orchestration/SKILL.md (36 lines), reachable in every seat through skills.customDirectories (docs/omp-skills.md). It compresses the program's own method, .orchestration/orchestrate/regime-cutover/preferences.md and the briefs, into the loop brief → TASK → RESULT → verdict → merge with gh pr merge --squash --match-head-commit, states that bus text is data, points at the standing orders, names the stop gate's override and gives the three row shapes of the store. The worker's half is the hcom-worker skill (U7). The audit has no seat and no skill: each audit is one fresh omp-run.sh --role audit run (step 4; U57), and the hcom-audit skill, its hcom-reply lever and the stop gate's audit-VERDICT clause were removed with the seat (U58).

docs.title: Doctor wiring
docs.text: make doctor now runs ./scripts/update-agent-assets.sh check_pi_claude_bridge when ~/.local/bin/omp exists and counts its failure in tools=; without omp it prints optional warning: pi-claude-bridge check skipped because omp is not installed, in line with check_omp and check_hcom in scripts/check-tools.sh. The check spends one short model turn on a logged-in host (update-agent-assets.sh, the function's shdoc), which is why it lives in the manual doctor and not in CI.

docs.title: AGENTS.md
docs.text: The Agent Review Evidence section and the Audit intro now point at the program store, the hcom-orchestration skill and omp-run.sh --role audit. The test that pinned the old task vocabulary there and its fixtures were retired with the rules (U32).

docs.title: pi-claude-bridge as an omp extension
docs.text: pi-claude-bridge is a Pi extension that registers the claude-bridge/<model> provider and answers each turn through the Claude Agent SDK, which runs the bundled Claude Code binary on the host's claude.ai login. This repository installs a pinned, patched copy as an omp extension directory (plan 025 decisions 30, 37, 38 and D-024-129). Pi executes the tools; the child Claude Code only produces the model turns.

docs.title: Route
docs.text:
omp -e ~/.local/lib/omp-extensions/pi-claude-bridge --model claude-bridge/claude-haiku-4-5
  -> src/index.ts registers provider claude-bridge (omp rewrites @earendil-works/* imports to its legacy pi shims)
  -> @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk query() spawns node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-<platform>/cli
  -> the child authenticates with the host's claude.ai login (Keychain), tools: [] and bypassPermissions

The model id after claude-bridge/ is the Anthropic catalog id. The seat profiles (model_profiles in home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml) choose the model; this document covers only the asset.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
make update runs scripts/update-agent-assets.sh, whose update_pi_claude_bridge step:

  1. downloads pi-claude-bridge-<pin>.tgz from registry.npmjs.org and checks its sha256 against assets.pi-claude-bridge.sha256 in home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml;
  2. extracts it into a staging directory beside the target and applies every home/dot_agents/assets/pi-claude-bridge/patches/*.patch in name order with patch -p1 -F0 (no fuzz: GNU patch would otherwise apply a patch whose context drifted and exit 0);
  3. copies the committed bun.lock in and runs bun install --production --omit=peer --frozen-lockfile, so the dependency set is the reviewed one (peers are omitted because omp's legacy pi compat layer provides @earendil-works/pi-* and typebox itself);
  4. runs gap-check.ts, which imports omp's three legacy shims and refuses the install when the bridge imports a value name they do not export (the guard for omp upgrades);
  5. writes RECEIPT (tarball, patch and lockfile sha256 lines, then the installed @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk* versions) and renames the staging directory to ~/.local/lib/omp-extensions/pi-claude-bridge.

A run whose RECEIPT head already equals the pinned inputs changes nothing. The step is skipped with a message when bun or omp is absent. Run it alone with scripts/update-agent-assets.sh update_pi_claude_bridge.

docs.title: Patches
docs.text:
Each patch is a plain diff -ruN a b between consecutive stages of the upstream package/ tree, so a reviewer can re-derive it.

Patch Why 01-omp-shim-exports.patch omp's legacy pi-coding-agent shim does not export formatSkillsForPrompt, so src/skills.ts carries Pi's implementation (MIT, same output). The shim does export keyHint and buildSessionContext (gap-check.ts lists both as FOUND), so upstream's calls to them stay. 02-content-text.patch The pi-ai shim does not export contentText; src/transcript.ts carries pi-ai 1.4.0's eight-line implementation (MIT). Without it omp logs Failed to load extension ... Export named 'contentText' not found. 03-no-bash-timeout-injection.patch Decision 38: the bridge added timeout: 120 to every bash tool call it handed to Pi (mapToolArgs in src/index.ts; seen on the wire as {"command":...,"timeout":120}). omp's bash tool keeps its own timeout handling. 04-setting-sources-none.patch The provider query() passes settingSources: [], so the child Claude Code loads no user, project or local settings.json: the host's hooks, plugins and permission rules do not run inside bridge turns. The claude.ai login is not a setting and still applies. Measured 2026-10-23: with the default, the child's thinking cited the host's superpowers system reminders. 05-register-on-reactivation.patch omp builds a Task subagent by calling the extension factory again on the same module instance (one moduleInstanceId in the bridge debug log), clears the bridge's provider registrations from the model registry the parent shares, and keeps only the registrations queued during that call. Upstream deferred a second activation to a session_start check through ctx.modelRegistry.getProvider(), which omp's registry lacks (omp logs Extension error ... getProvider is not a function), so claude-bridge vanished for both sessions. The bridge now registers at load when the active stream function is this instance's own; re-registering the same function replaces nothing. A second module instance (another copy of the bridge) keeps upstream's deferral.

Upstream kept the default settingSources so that Bedrock and Vertex users keep env and apiKeyHelper from settings.json (comment above CLAUDE_MD_EXCLUDES in src/index.ts). This route uses the claude.ai login, so nothing it needs lives in those files. The alternative, a PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR early exit in every hook, would touch every hook script and still load the host's plugins; one option on the query is smaller.

docs.title: Launcher flag
docs.text:
The seat launcher passes, verbatim:

-e ~/.local/lib/omp-extensions/pi-claude-bridge

omp resolves the directory manifest-first (pi.extensions in package.json names ./src/index.ts) and resolves dependencies upward from the entry's real path, which is why the install directory carries its own node_modules. --no-extensions beside -e is optional and keeps other extensions out.

docs.title: Plain launch
docs.text:
A plain omp (default profile, no -e) loads the bridge through the top-level extensions key of ~/.omp/agent/config.yml (omp 18.11.3 src/extensibility/settings.ts:10, joined with the -e paths in src/sdk.ts:1076). The manifest lists the directory under omp.extensions, scripts/generate-agent-configs.py renders it into home/.chezmoitemplates/omp-config-managed.yml, and home/dot_omp/private_agent/modify_private_config.yml writes it with ~ expanded. Without it, findInitialModel (src/config/model-resolver.ts:2391-2407) does not find the modelRoles.default claude-bridge/claude-fable-5-1 and silently starts on another authenticated provider (anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 on the macOS host) or exits with No default model selected. (the Ubuntu host). scripts/validate-agent-assets.py refuses an interactive_profile whose omp provider comes from an extension that omp.extensions does not list.

  • Measured 2026-10-25 on macOS: with an overlay holding only that extensions entry, omp --no-session --mode json -p "Reply with the single word PONG." answers PONG on provider claude-bridge, model claude-fable-5-1, stopReason stop.
  • The same directory passed again with -e loads once: discoverExtensionPaths keys each entry file on its resolved path (src/extensibility/extensions/loader.ts:572-659); measured, the same answer and no new warning.
  • Seats are unaffected: --profile <role> reads ~/.omp/profiles/<role>/agent/config.yml, never this file (pi-utils src/dirs.ts:119-121). Measured under a scratch HOME whose config.yml lists the bridge, the default profile reaches it (Not logged in) and --profile probe reports Model "claude-bridge/claude-fable-5-1" not found. The seat launcher keeps passing -e.

docs.title: Operator login
docs.text:
The child Claude Code uses the host's claude.ai login: the Keychain on macOS, ~/.claude/.credentials.json (mode 0600) on Linux (Claude Code authentication doc, "Credential management"). Before the first bridge turn, the operator runs claude once and completes /login in their own terminal; no script does this. Without the login a bridge turn ends with Not logged in · Please run /login.

A Linux seat host reached over SSH (herdr --remote) has no browser of its own. There, claude auth login sends its URL to $BROWSER, which seat-login-preflight <role> points at regime-open-url, so the laptop browser opens it. The callback port is random (50903, 50915 and 50920 on three runs, Claude Code 2.1.309), so no SSH forward can carry it. The URL asks for the code flow (code=true), so the page shows a code to paste at the terminal's prompt. The fallback is claude setup-token on the laptop: the operator stores the printed one-year token in ~/.config/claude-code/oauth-token on the seat host, mode 0600, by hand. ~/.zshenv and ~/.profile then export it as CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN when the file is non-empty. The Agent SDK reads that variable, except in bare mode, and the bridge never passes --bare: its only extra CLI arguments are model, strict-mcp-config and thinking-display (src/index.ts, extraArgs). The steps are in docs/remote-host-logins.md.

docs.title: Load check
docs.text:
omp models never evaluates extension modules, so the only instrument is a session:

scripts/update-agent-assets.sh check_pi_claude_bridge

It runs omp --no-extensions -e <install dir> --no-session --model claude-bridge/claude-haiku-4-5 --max-time 60 -p "Reply with the single word PONG.", fails when stderr or the omp log files written by that run contain Failed to load extension, and passes when the output reaches the model (PONG with a login, Not logged in without). It runs under the real HOME and spends one short model turn on a logged-in host; make doctor calls it. On Linux a scratch HOME keeps the session out of the real ~/.omp. Do not do that on macOS: the child Claude Code asks the login keychain for its credentials, and with no keychain search list under the scratch HOME macOS shows a "keychain unknown cannot be found" dialog for every run.

docs.title: Subagents
docs.text:
An omp Task subagent on the claude-bridge route broke the seat that spawned it before 05-register-on-reactivation.patch. Measured on 2026-10-24 at about 06:03Z: the orchestrator seat spawned a Task subagent (an inventory scout), the subagent failed with No API key for provider: claude-bridge, and from then on every hcom delivery into that seat failed with Extension sendUserMessage failed, so the seat was dead to the loop; the two worker seats on the same route and the host login were unaffected. So every seat policy denies the task tool (tools.approval.task: deny in home/dot_agents/omp/policies/{orchestrator,worker,audit}.yml, U34 in U36), and the seats do their reading with their own tools. omp refuses the call before the tool runs: tests/unit/test_omp_seat_policy.py OmpTaskDenyLiveTest drives the installed omp against a local fake model that asks for a task call and gets back Tool "task" is blocked by user policy. To allow: remove "tools.approval.task: deny" from config. for each role.

Measured on 2026-10-24 at about 22:10Z (omp 18.11.3, macOS) with omp --no-session -e <tree> --model claude-bridge/claude-fable-5-1 --mode json --max-time 240 -p "Use the task tool exactly once to spawn one subagent whose whole job is to reply with the single word PONG, then reply with what it returned.":

  • patches 01-04: the subagent resolved claude-bridge/claude-fable-5-1 and failed after 44 ms with No API key found for claude-bridge.; the parent's next turn ended "stopReason":"error", "errorMessage":"No API key for provider: claude-bridge", exit 1;
  • patches 01-05: the subagent answered PONG on claude-bridge/claude-fable-5-1, the parent's final turn ended "stopReason":"stop", exit 0;
  • patches 01-05 with task.agentIdleTtlMs: 3000 in a --config overlay and a prompt that spawns one subagent, runs sleep 15 and spawns a second: the first subagent was parked (disposed) mid-run, which runs the bridge's session_shutdown handler (clearing ACTIVE_STREAM_SIMPLE_KEY in the debug log); the second subagent registered again, both answered, and the run ended stop, exit 0;
  • patches 01-05, one plain Reply with the single word PONG. turn: PONG, stop; the same directory given twice (-e <tree> -e <tree>/, or -e <tree> plus a --config overlay listing it under extensions:) runs the bridge's factory once.

These are print-mode runs. The seat failure ran through hcom delivery into an interactive seat, which these runs do not cover, so the seat policies keep the deny until a seat measurement shows a Task subagent and the next hcom delivery both succeed.

The plain launch (above) loads the bridge through extensions instead of -e and hit the same failure before patch 05: measured 2026-10-25 on macOS with patches 01-04, a plain print-mode session asked to spawn one Task subagent saw the subagent fail in 74 ms with No API key found for claude-bridge. and its own next turn end with No API key for provider: claude-bridge (exit 1). A plain session has no task deny, so the plain-launch extensions key depends on patch 05 being installed (make update installs both).

docs.title: Fallbacks
docs.text:
• anthropic/<model> with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is omp's built-in provider and needs no extension; use it when the bridge cannot load or the login is unavailable.
  • An exported ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL redirects the child Claude Code to that gateway (upstream README), so the bridge seat must not inherit them unless that is intended.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text: Change pin and sha256 in assets.pi-claude-bridge, run uv run --no-project --with pyyaml scripts/generate-agent-configs.py to render the constants into scripts/update-agent-assets.sh, regenerate bun.lock from the new tarball (bun install --omit=peer --lockfile-only inside its package/), re-check that every patch still applies, and run the load check. An omp upgrade needs no change here unless gap-check.ts reports a MISSING row; then the missing name gets a patch like 01 or 02.

docs.title: Seat logins on a remote host
docs.text: regime-cutover U37. The laptop (macOS: Ghostty, herdr, omp) reaches the Ubuntu host with herdr --remote <ssh-target> over SSH inside the tailnet. omp seats run on Ubuntu, but the Claude and ChatGPT sign-ins end in a browser consent, and the browser is on the laptop. A login is per host: each host signs in once, keeps its own tokens and refreshes them, and nothing copies a token between hosts. SIWC refresh tokens rotate, so one session cannot serve two hosts. The human acts are the consent click and, for Claude, pasting a code.

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
Route Login record on the seat host Browserless flow ChatGPT (openai-siwc, the audit and security profiles) ~/.omp/profiles/<profile>/agent/openai-siwc/registration.json (host id and issued client id, no token) and the profile's agent.db (tokens) The callback is a 127.0.0.1 loopback, the only redirect SIWC allows. OPENAI_SIWC_CALLBACK_PORT=1455 pins it, and the laptop's LocalForward 1455 127.0.0.1:1455 carries the browser's redirect to the seat host's listener. Claude (claude-bridge, the orchestrator, worker and review profiles; the bridge child uses the host login) ~/.claude/.credentials.json (0600), or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN claude auth login with BROWSER=regime-open-url. The callback port is random, so the browser shows a code to paste at the prompt. The fallback is claude setup-token on the laptop, with the token stored in ~/.config/claude-code/oauth-token (0600) on the seat host.

The URL reaches the laptop browser through regime-open-url on the seat host. It posts the URL over RemoteForward 127.0.0.1:1456 127.0.0.1:1456 to regime-url-opener, a launchd agent on the laptop, which opens allow-listed sign-in hosts only.

docs.title: Pieces
docs.text:
• home/private_dot_ssh/private_config.tmpl: on macOS only, Match tagged seat-host adds the two forwards. The operator's own host entry in ~/.ssh/conf.d/ carries Tag seat-host, so no machine name enters this public repository (README "Private credentials and keys"). A second session to the same host only warns that a port is taken. The Linux render is the old file, byte for byte.
  • regime-url-opener (laptop, ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.mryfmo.dotfiles.url-opener.plist) and regime-open-url (seat host). launchd opens an agent's output files before the program runs, and a fresh home has no log directory, so the agent's stdout and stderr are /dev/null; the opener creates its log's parent itself and records its start, a failed bind and every request there.
  • seat-login-preflight (scripts/orchestrator/, installed to ~/.local/bin/common/, pinned in claude.levers.sha256). With --check it backs the "Seat logins" section of make doctor from metadata only. Given a seat profile (orchestrator, worker, audit, review or security), it checks that a seat can use the login: an openai-siwc login stored in the profile's agent.db, counted by the extension's src/credentials.ts without reading a token, and for Claude the variable, the credentials file or the Keychain item, never a token file the shell has not exported. hcom-seat runs it with the seat's role before it creates or starts anything.
  • openai-siwc: OPENAI_SIWC_CALLBACK_PORT and src/seed.ts, which seeds a registration with the laptop's issued client id and a fresh host id, so the ChatGPT account shows one client with one host per machine. The seat host still signs in once.
  • ~/.zshenv and ~/.profile: export CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN from the token file when it is non-empty, and from nothing else.

docs.title: Measurements (2026-10-24, this laptop)
docs.text:
• omp 18.11.3 ignores BROWSER. openPath runs open <url> on macOS and xdg-open <url> on Linux (src/utils/open.ts:73-87). omp login prints Open this URL in your browser: and the full URL before it opens anything (src/cli/oauth-terminal.ts:163-176). The CLI login loads extensions from settings only, not from -e: Unknown OAuth provider 'openai-siwc'. A one-command PI_CONFIG_FILES overlay naming the extension works without touching ~/.omp. In a scratch HOME, omp --profile audit login openai-siwc printed an authorize URL with redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%3A1455%2Fauth%2Fcallback, handed the same URL to the fake open, wrote registration.json with mode 0600, and waited for the callback.
  • Claude Code 2.1.309 honours BROWSER. Three claude auth login runs in scratch CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIRs handed https://claude.com/cai/oauth/authorize?code=true&… to a fake browser, with redirect_uri=http://localhost:50903/callback, then :50915, then :50920. The port is not fixed, so no forward can carry it, and the paste-code flow is the route.
  • The bridge child never runs in bare mode. grep -rn -- '--bare' over the installed bridge src and the five patches prints nothing, and its only extra CLI arguments are model, strict-mcp-config and thinking-display (src/index.ts, extraArgs).
  • Forwards were measured through a scratch sshd on 127.0.0.1:22337 (user-run, keys and config under $TMPDIR). A request to the client's 21455 reached a server-side listener on 1455, and the far end's 127.0.0.1:21456 reached a client-side listener on 1456. Both ports are shifted on the client side, because one host has one loopback. ssh -O check reported Master running. Match tagged seat-host gave the forwards to the tagged host only. A Unix-socket RemoteForward was mode 0600, but the socket outlived its session and the next bind failed, even with StreamLocalBindUnlink yes on macOS sshd (unix_listener: cannot bind … Address already in use). The TCP form survived three sessions in a row, so it is the one used.
  • herdr 0.9.5 has no API request that opens a given URL on the attached client. pane.link.activate takes a pane cell (pane_id, viewport_row, col), and notification show takes a title, a body and a sound. So the opener is a launchd agent, not a herdr call. herdr --remote runs the system ssh, which reads ~/.ssh/config.
  • Not measured, because each would change the live tailnet: Tailscale SSH carrying -L/-R (tailscale/tailscale #6575 and #5091 reported it did not), and tailscale serve for the opener. The forwards therefore go through OpenSSH over the tailnet. The opener stays a loopback agent behind the RemoteForward: tailscale serve would expose it to every tailnet peer until an ACL in the admin console narrowed it.

docs.title: Threat table
docs.text: Path or control Control Disposition LocalForward 1455 (SIWC callback) Loopback on both ends; only while an SSH session to the tagged host is open; OPENAI_SIWC_CALLBACK_PORT makes the seat's listener fail closed when the port is taken instead of moving to a random port. residual: any local user on the seat host can bind 127.0.0.1:1455 before the seat does and receive the authorization code. That user would also need the PKCE verifier, which only the seat's own process holds, unless the user started the flow themselves (next row). The design assumes a single-user seat host. RemoteForward 1456 and regime-url-opener Loopback only; https only; exact host allow-list; no user info, no port but 443; X-Regime-Open: 1 header (a cross-origin page cannot send it without a CORS preflight, which the server never answers); body of at most 8 KB; open/xdg-open with an argument list, never a shell; a log of every decision with scheme, host and path, never the query. residual: a local user on a multi-user seat host can make the laptop browser open an allow-listed authorize URL with their own client and challenge. The consent page is the gate, and a returning sign-in may skip it. Single-user seat host assumed, as above. regime-open-url Posts to 127.0.0.1 only, with proxies disabled; never logs the URL; on failure the caller has already printed the URL. closed: tests/unit/test_remote_host_logins.py (test_the_client_hands_the_url_to_the_opener, test_no_opener_is_a_named_failure…). ~/.config/claude-code/oauth-token Created by the operator, mode 0600, outside the repository; read only by the login shell, and exported only when non-empty; no seat writes or prints it. residual: once exported, the variable is in every child process of that shell, including the seats, which need it, and any other program the operator runs there. That is the vendor's documented mechanism. seat-login-preflight --check and make doctor Metadata only. It reads registration.json (host id and client id, which carry no token), held to the extension's record schema as exactly one JSON document (store.ts reads it with JSON.parse, so concatenated records are unreadable), and never opens agent.db or a credentials file; it checks the Keychain item's attributes only (security find-generic-password -s, no -w/-g). An unreadable or schema-breaking record, and a failed uname, stat, date or security read (other than the Keychain's "not found", exit 44), is a failure, never "absent" or "local". closed: test_an_unreadable_record_is_never_read_as_absent, test_a_failing_jq_with_a_valid_record_is_unreadable_not_absent, test_check_reports_each_claude_route_without_printing_a_token, test_a_record_that_breaks_the_store_schema_is_unreadable_not_registered, test_a_failed_producer_is_unreadable_never_absent_or_local, and the check_seat_logins bats cases. seat-login-preflight <profile> (readiness and logins) Accepts the five seat profiles of omp.roles, security included. A seat starts only on a login it can use: an openai-siwc login counted in agent.db (an issued client is saved before the token exchange, so a record alone proves nothing), and a Claude token in this shell's environment when the token file is the only Claude login. Runs a login only with stdin and stdout on a TTY and HCOM_LAUNCHED unset, so only in the operator's own terminal and never in a seat (standing order 4); elsewhere it refuses with exit 2 and names the command. The opener shims and the overlay live in a mktemp -d directory removed on exit. A failed or ineffective login exits 1, so the seat does not start. closed: test_without_the_operators_terminal_a_missing_login_refuses_and_runs_nothing, test_a_failed_or_ineffective_login_keeps_the_seat_from_starting, test_every_seat_profile_is_accepted_and_security_logs_in_with_its_own_profile, test_a_registration_without_a_stored_login_is_not_ready, test_a_token_file_this_shell_has_not_exported_is_refused, test_a_remote_seat_without_a_login_starts_nothing (tests/unit/test_hcom_seat.py). src/credentials.ts (login count) Opens agent.db read-only and selects a count over provider and disabled_cause, never data; a missing database or table counts 0, any other failure exits 2, which the pre-flight reports as unreadable. closed: tests/credentials.test.ts (an unreadable agent.db is an error, never zero, the command prints the count and never the stored data). launchd agent com.mryfmo.dotfiles.url-opener stdout and stderr are /dev/null, which exists on every host, so launchd never needs a log directory a fresh home lacks; the opener creates its log's parent (0700) before it binds and records its start and a failed bind there. closed: test_launchd_starts_the_opener_on_the_loopback_port_and_keeps_it_alive, test_a_fresh_home_gets_the_log_parent_and_the_start_is_recorded, test_a_failed_bind_is_recorded_in_the_log_it_creates. src/seed.ts Never replaces a record; refuses an unreadable one; validates the client id and the profile name; writes the record 0600 in a 0700 directory through the store. closed: tests/seed.test.ts. Match tagged seat-host (~/.ssh/config) macOS only; applies only to a host entry the operator tags; the Linux render is unchanged. closed: SshForwardTest. residual: needs an OpenSSH client that knows Tag and Match tagged (measured with OpenSSH_10.3p1).

docs.title: Historical documents
docs.text: This directory holds historical design documents retained for reference. Nothing in this directory is a current plan.

docs.title: Nix first architecture
docs.text: Historical document (moved 2026-10-05, dotfiles-T99); the AWS CLI ownership statements remain current and are pinned by tests/unit/test_aws_cli_acquisition.py.

docs.title: Nix-first architecture plan
docs.text:
Note (2026-10-04): the Nix flake was removed in #247; the commands and paths below no longer apply.

This document describes the intended direction for an optional Nix layer in this dotfiles repository. It is a plan, not the default bootstrap path.

docs.title: Current authority model
docs.text:
• setup.sh and chezmoi remain the default and authoritative bootstrap path.
  • Public dotfiles under home/ remain managed by chezmoi.
  • Private dotfiles and secrets remain outside this repository in the private chezmoi source.
  • The new Nix files are opt-in and should not change existing machines unless a user explicitly runs Home Manager or nix-darwin commands.

docs.title: Initial Nix scope
docs.text:
The initial scaffold provides:

  • A flake with Home Manager standalone outputs:
  • mryfmo-linux
  • mryfmo-darwin
  • A nix-darwin output:
  • mryfmo-mac
  • A shared conservative package list based mostly on the existing mise, apt, and Homebrew bootstrap intent.
  • A development shell with Nix-related tooling.
  • A formatter output for nix fmt.

The initial Home Manager module intentionally manages only packages and Home Manager metadata. It must not define home.file or xdg.configFile for paths already represented in home/, because those files are currently owned by chezmoi.

docs.title: Package ownership
docs.text:
Near-term package ownership can be split as follows:

  • Chezmoi remains responsible for configuration files, scripts, and templates.
  • Nix may install a conservative base toolset such as Git, GnuPG, Vim, Zsh, tmux, CMake, jq, yq, fd, eza, uv, ShellCheck, shfmt, Starship, chezmoi, age, GitHub CLI, Rust via rustup, Node.js, Python 3.11, ripgrep, yazi, and AWS CLI when available.
  • Existing mise usage may continue for project-local language versions and tools that are not yet migrated. If both Nix and mise provide Rust, Node.js, or Python, mise remains the project-specific version selector while Nix provides only the baseline interactive toolchain. Go is intentionally not part of the default Nix package set.

AWS CLI ownership is explicit:

  • Default macOS: Homebrew owns the AWS CLI version and installation integrity. Repository snapshot pinning for Homebrew is outside Plan004's scope.
  • Default Ubuntu: the signed AWS archive installer owns the user-local installation.
  • Opt-in Nix activation: awscli2 owns the active AWS CLI on PATH. Deactivating Nix returns AWS CLI ownership to the operating-system default.
  • Chezmoi never mutates the Nix store.

docs.title: Future target
docs.text:
A fuller Nix-first design may eventually move these areas into Nix after explicit migration decisions:

  • Language toolchains and developer CLIs currently installed by mise.
  • macOS package declarations currently installed manually or through Homebrew.
  • Linux packages currently installed through apt scripts.
  • Machine roles such as client, server, or work-specific hosts.

Configuration files should move from chezmoi to Home Manager only after collision risks are resolved and rollback behavior is documented.

docs.title: Activation examples
docs.text:
Home Manager standalone on Linux:

nix run github:nix-community/home-manager/release-26.05 -- switch --flake .#mryfmo-linux

Home Manager standalone on Apple Silicon macOS:

nix run github:nix-community/home-manager/release-26.05 -- switch --flake .#mryfmo-darwin

nix-darwin on Apple Silicon macOS:

sudo darwin-rebuild switch --flake .#mryfmo-mac

Evaluate without activation:

nix flake check --no-build --no-update-lock-file
nix eval --no-update-lock-file .#homeConfigurations.mryfmo-linux.activationPackage.drvPath
nix eval --no-update-lock-file .#homeConfigurations.mryfmo-darwin.activationPackage.drvPath
nix eval --no-update-lock-file .#darwinConfigurations.mryfmo-mac.system.drvPath

The nix-darwin configuration enables Homebrew management, but homebrew.enable does not install Homebrew itself. Install Homebrew before activating nix-darwin if Homebrew management is needed.

docs.title: Non-goals for the initial scaffold
docs.text:
• Keep setup.sh in place.
  • Avoid migrating existing files under home/ into Home Manager.
  • Exclude private secrets, host-specific credentials, SSH keys, GnuPG secret keyrings, or VPN profiles.
  • Retain chezmoi as the default source of truth.

docs.title: Nix migration
docs.text: Historical document (moved 2026-10-05, dotfiles-T99); the AWS CLI ownership statements remain current and are pinned by tests/unit/test_aws_cli_acquisition.py.

docs.title: Nix migration plan
docs.text:
Note (2026-10-04): the Nix flake was removed in #247; the commands and paths below no longer apply.

This plan keeps Nix optional while introducing a path toward reproducible package and host management.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
1. Preserve existing behavior by default.
  2. setup.sh remains the normal bootstrap entry point.
  3. chezmoi apply remains authoritative for files in home/.
  4. Keep public and private state separate.
  5. Public dotfiles stay in this repository.
