  6. Private files and secrets stay in the private chezmoi source or on the target host.
  7. Avoid file ownership collisions.
  8. Do not add Home Manager home.file or xdg.configFile entries for existing chezmoi-managed paths until they are deliberately migrated.
  9. Make every migration reversible.
  10. Document the owner of each migrated package or config path.
  11. Prefer small changes that can be rolled back independently.

docs.title: Phase 0: Opt-in scaffold
docs.text:
Status: initial implementation.

  • Add flake.nix.
  • Add a shared package module at nix/shared/packages.nix.
  • Add a minimal Home Manager module at nix/home-manager/default.nix.
  • Add a minimal nix-darwin module at nix/nix-darwin/default.nix.
  • Add documentation describing architecture and migration rules.

Validation target:

nix fmt --no-update-lock-file
nix flake show --no-update-lock-file
nix flake check --no-build --no-update-lock-file

If Nix is unavailable on a machine, CI evaluates every declared output on Linux and macOS. Never hand-edit flake.lock; regenerate it with nix flake lock.

AWS CLI follows the ownership boundary in the architecture plan: Homebrew owns the default macOS installation, the signed user-local installer owns the default Ubuntu installation, and opt-in Nix activation puts Nix awscli2 first on PATH. Deactivating Nix restores the operating-system default, and chezmoi never mutates the Nix store. Homebrew repository snapshot pinning remains outside Plan004's scope.

docs.title: Phase 1: Package-only adoption
docs.text:
Goal: use Nix to install common packages without changing dotfile ownership.

Candidate packages:

  • Core: git, gnupg, vim, zsh, tmux, cmake
  • CLI data tools: jq, yq
  • Search and listing tools: fd, eza, ripgrep
  • Development helpers: uv, shellcheck, shfmt, starship, chezmoi, age, gh
  • Language runtimes: rustup, nodejs, python311
  • Optional tools: yazi, awscli2 when available

Acceptance criteria:

  • Home Manager standalone activation does not overwrite existing dotfiles.
  • nix-darwin activation does not assume Homebrew is already installed beyond documented behavior.
  • Existing chezmoi commands continue to work before and after Nix activation.

docs.title: Phase 2: Host roles and package ownership
docs.text:
Goal: make package sets explicit by host or role.

Possible role modules:

  • common
  • linux-client
  • linux-server
  • darwin-client
  • work

Each role should document whether a package is owned by Nix, mise, apt, Homebrew, or another installer.

docs.title: Phase 3: Selective config migration
docs.text:
Goal: migrate selected dotfile paths to Home Manager only when there is a clear benefit.

Before migrating a path:

  1. Identify the current chezmoi source path under home/.
  2. Confirm whether private chezmoi overlays or templates affect the same target path.
  3. Remove or disable the chezmoi source for that path in the same change that adds Home Manager ownership.
  4. Document rollback steps.

Paths that should not be migrated early:

  • SSH private material
  • GnuPG secret keyrings
  • VPN credentials
  • Any host-specific or work-specific secret

docs.title: Phase 4: Optional Nix-first bootstrap
docs.text:
Goal: provide a Nix-first bootstrap path for users who explicitly choose it.

This should remain separate from setup.sh unless the repository owner decides to change the default bootstrap model. A future bootstrap may install Nix, activate Home Manager or nix-darwin, and then run chezmoi for public and private dotfiles.

docs.title: Rollback notes
docs.text:
Home Manager standalone rollback is generally handled with Home Manager generations. nix-darwin rollback is handled with system generations. Package-only changes should be low risk, but any future file ownership migration must include explicit rollback instructions because ownership collisions can block activation or overwrite expected state.

Useful rollback entry points:

home-manager generations
home-manager switch --rollback
sudo darwin-rebuild --rollback

For flake input regressions, revert the Git commit that changed flake.nix or flake.lock, then re-run the relevant Home Manager or nix-darwin switch command.

#!/bin/bash

# @file home/dot_claude/hooks/executable_enforce-uv.sh
# @brief Block direct Python and pip commands in favor of `uv`.
# @description
#   Emit PreToolUse permissionDecision deny for direct `pip` or `python` usage;
#   other input exits successfully without output. Contract verified 2026-10-05.
# @see https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#pretooluse-decision-control

# @description Encode the denial reason from stdin using the current hook contract.
# @stdout PreToolUse deny JSON with the original multiline reason.
function deny_command() {
    jq -Rsc '{hookSpecificOutput: {hookEventName: "PreToolUse", permissionDecision: "deny", permissionDecisionReason: rtrimstr("\n")}}'
}

# @description Emit the `uv` replacement message for `pip install`.
# @arg $1 string Parsed `pip` subcommand beginning with `install`.
function handle_pip_install() {
    local pip_cmd="$1"
    local packages
    packages=$(echo "$pip_cmd" | sed 's/install//' | sed 's/--[^ ]*//g' | xargs)

    # -r requirements.txt
    if [[ "$pip_cmd" =~ -r\ .*\.txt ]]; then
        local req_file
        req_file=$(echo "$pip_cmd" | sed -n 's/.*-r \([^ ]*\).*/\1/p')
        deny_command <<- EOF
        📋 requirements.txtからインストール:

        ✅ 推奨方法:
        uv add -r $req_file

        これにより:
        • requirements.txt内のすべての依存関係をpyproject.tomlに追加
        • uv.lockファイルを自動生成/更新
        • 仮想環境を自動的に同期

        💡 制約ファイルがある場合:
        uv add -r $req_file -c constraints.txt

        📌 注意: この方法が最も確実で、バージョン指定も正しく処理されます
        EOF
        exit 0
    fi

    # 開発依存関係
    if [[ "$pip_cmd" =~ --dev ]] || [[ "$pip_cmd" =~ -e ]]; then
        deny_command <<- EOF
        🔧 開発依存関係をインストール:

        uv add --dev $packages

        編集可能インストール: uv add -e .
        EOF
        exit 0
    fi

    # 通常のインストール
    deny_command <<- EOF
    📦 パッケージをインストール:

    uv add $packages

    💾 'uv add' はpyproject.tomlに依存関係を保存します
    🔒 uv.lockで再現可能な環境を保証

    💡 特殊なケース:
    • URLからのインストール: パッケージを手動でダウンロードしてから追加
    • 開発版: uv add --dev $packages
    • ローカルパッケージ: uv add -e ./path/to/package
    EOF
    exit 0
}

# @description Emit the `uv remove` replacement message for `pip uninstall`.
# @arg $1 string Parsed `pip` subcommand beginning with `uninstall`.
function handle_pip_uninstall() {
    local pip_cmd="$1"
    local packages
    packages=$(echo "$pip_cmd" | sed 's/uninstall//' | sed 's/-y//g' | xargs)
    deny_command <<- EOF
    🗑️ パッケージを削除:

    uv remove $packages

    ✨ 依存関係も自動的にクリーンアップされます
    EOF
    exit 0
}

# @description Explain the `uv` alternatives for `pip list` and `pip freeze`.
function handle_pip_list() {
    deny_command <<- 'EOF'
    📊 パッケージ一覧を確認:

    • プロジェクト依存関係: cat pyproject.toml
    • ロックファイル詳細: cat uv.lock
    • インストール済み一覧: uv tree
    • requirements.txt形式でエクスポート: uv export --format requirements-txt

    💡 'uv tree'はプロジェクトの依存関係ツリーを表示します
    EOF
    exit 0
}

# @description Fall back to a generic `uv` recommendation for other pip commands.
# @arg $1 string Parsed `pip` subcommand.
function handle_pip_other() {
    local pip_cmd="$1"
    deny_command <<- EOF
    🔀 pipコマンドをuvで実行:

    uv $pip_cmd

    💡 パッケージのインストール/削除には 'uv add/remove' を使用してください
    EOF
    exit 0
}

# @description Handle `python -m pip ...` by mapping it to the right `uv` advice.
# @arg $1 string Parsed module arguments after `python -m pip`.
function handle_python_m_pip() {
    local pip_cmd="$1"

    # Parse pip install commands
    if [[ "$pip_cmd" =~ ^install ]]; then
        local packages
        packages=$(echo "$pip_cmd" | sed 's/install//' | sed 's/--[^ ]*//g' | xargs)
        if [[ "$pip_cmd" =~ -r\ .*\.txt ]]; then
            local req_file
            req_file=$(echo "$pip_cmd" | sed -n 's/.*-r \([^ ]*\).*/\1/p')
            deny_command <<- EOF
            📋 requirements.txtからインストール:

            ✅ 推奨方法:
            uv add -r $req_file

            💡 これによりすべての依存関係がpyproject.tomlに追加されます
            EOF
        else
            deny_command <<- EOF
            📦 パッケージをインストール:

            uv add $packages

            💡 'uv add' はpyproject.tomlに依存関係を保存します
            EOF
        fi
    else
        deny_command <<- EOF
        🔀 pipコマンドをuvで実行:

        uv $pip_cmd

        💡 パッケージ管理には 'uv add/remove' を使用してください
        EOF
    fi
    exit 0
}

# @description Rewrite `python -m module` invocations to `uv run`.
# @arg $1 string Module invocation after `python -m`.
function handle_python_m_module() {
    local module="$1"
    deny_command <<- EOF
    uvでモジュールを実行:

    uv run python -m $module

    🔄 uvは自動的に環境を同期してから実行します。
    EOF
    exit 0
}

# @description Rewrite direct Python execution to `uv run`.
# @arg $1 string Original Python arguments.
function handle_python_run() {
    local args="$1"
    deny_command <<- EOF
    uvでPythonを実行:

    uv run $args

    ✅ 仮想環境のアクティベーションは不要です！
    EOF
    exit 0
}

# @description Read hook input JSON, classify the command, and emit a decision.
function main() {
    local input
    input=$(cat)

    # Validate input
    if [ -z "$input" ]; then
        exit 0
    fi

    # Extract fields with error handling
    local tool_name
    tool_name=$(echo "$input" | jq -r '.tool_name' 2> /dev/null || echo "")
    local command
    command=$(echo "$input" | jq -r '.tool_input.command // ""' 2> /dev/null || echo "")

    # ===== pip関連コマンド =====
    if [[ "$tool_name" == "Bash" ]]; then
        case "$command" in
        pip\ * | pip3\ *)
            # pipコマンドの詳細な解析
            local pip_cmd
            pip_cmd=$(echo "$command" | sed -E 's/^pip[0-9]? *//' | xargs)

            case "$pip_cmd" in
            install\ *)
                handle_pip_install "$pip_cmd"
                ;;
            uninstall\ *)
                handle_pip_uninstall "$pip_cmd"
                ;;
            list* | freeze*)
                handle_pip_list
                ;;
            *)
                handle_pip_other "$pip_cmd"
                ;;
            esac
            ;;

        # ===== 直接的なPython実行の処理 =====
        python* | py\ *)
            # 通常のuvへの変換
            local args
            args=$(echo "$command" | sed -E 's/^python[0-9]? //' | xargs)

            # -m オプションの特別処理
            if [[ "$args" =~ ^-m ]]; then
                local module
                module=${args/-m /}

                case "$module" in
                pip\ *)
                    local pip_cmd
                    pip_cmd=${module/pip /}
                    handle_python_m_pip "$pip_cmd"
                    ;;
                *)
                    handle_python_m_module "$module"
                    ;;
                esac
            fi

            # 基本的なPython実行
            handle_python_run "$args"
            ;;
        esac
    fi

    exit 0
}

main

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Format files reported by Claude Code hook JSON input.

The hook reads the complete JSON event from stdin, extracts every edited file path
from common Write/Edit/MultiEdit payload shapes, filters by suffix, and runs the
formatter for that suffix without going through a shell. ruff and prettier come
from PATH: their versions are pinned in the mise config, and ruff.toml and
.prettierignore keep vendored and record paths untouched.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shlex
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

PYTHON_COMMANDS = [
    ["ruff", "format"],
]
MARKDOWN_COMMANDS = [
    ["prettier", "--write"],
]


def collect_paths(value: Any) -> set[Path]:
    paths: set[Path] = set()
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        for key, item in value.items():
            if key in {"file_path", "path"} and isinstance(item, str):
                paths.add(Path(item))
            else:
                paths.update(collect_paths(item))
    elif isinstance(value, list):
        for item in value:
            paths.update(collect_paths(item))
    return paths


def repository_root(path: Path) -> Path:
    """The git work tree containing path, else its directory: where the formatter configs live."""
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(path.parent), "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=False
        )
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return path.parent
    root = result.stdout.rstrip("\n")
    return Path(root) if result.returncode == 0 and root else path.parent


def run_commands(commands: list[list[str]], files: list[Path]) -> int:
    status = 0
    # Run from each file's repository root: prettier reads .prettierignore from
    # its working directory, and the session's directory may be another tree.
    by_root: dict[Path, list[str]] = {}
    for path in files:
        resolved = path.resolve()
        by_root.setdefault(repository_root(resolved), []).append(str(resolved))
    for root, file_args in sorted(by_root.items()):
        for command in commands:
            config = root / "ruff.toml"
            if command[0] == "ruff" and config.is_file():
                # Pin the root config: ruff otherwise picks each file's nearest
                # pyproject.toml (vendor/compactiondb) and skips the root exclusions.
                command = [*command, "--config", str(config)]
            try:
                result = subprocess.run(command + file_args, cwd=root, check=False)
            except FileNotFoundError:
                # make update installs every declared mise tool, so a missing formatter means that step was skipped or failed.
                print(
                    f"{command[0]} is not installed; run `make update` (it installs every declared mise tool)",
                    file=sys.stderr,
                )
                status = max(status, 1)
                continue
            status = max(status, result.returncode)
    return status


def main() -> int:
    raw = sys.stdin.read()
    if not raw.strip():
        return 0
    try:
        payload = json.loads(raw)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as error:
        print(f"failed to parse Claude hook input: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 0

    paths = sorted(path for path in collect_paths(payload.get("tool_input", payload)) if path.exists())
    python_files = [path for path in paths if path.suffix == ".py"]
    markdown_files = [path for path in paths if path.suffix == ".md"]

    status = 0
    status = max(status, run_commands(PYTHON_COMMANDS, python_files))
    status = max(status, run_commands(MARKDOWN_COMMANDS, markdown_files))
    return status


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/bin/bash

# @file home/dot_claude/hooks/executable_project-map-reload.sh
# @brief Reload the visible project map after a Claude file edit.
# @description
#   Pass CDP on both calls to avoid terminal-browser issue 60.
#   Pin tab selection and guard reloads against navigation away from a project map.
#   Match the event file path before choosing an existing map tab.
#   Canonicalize event paths and file URLs with the installed isolated Python stdlib.
#   Reject encoded URL separators before decoding them into filesystem paths.
#   Bind the reload guard to the canonical-matched URL, encoded as a JSON string.
#   Open a separate right split using half the width when the parsed listing yields no map tab.
#   shortcut: rejected map metadata or racing writes can open another pane; tighten selection in the hook follow-up.
# @exitcode 0 Always, including unavailable tools or browsers.

# @description Return the physical absolute path of a local path or file URL.
# @arg $1 path Event path or file URL, including home and relative forms.
# @stdout Canonical path.
canonical_path() {
    python3 -I -S -c '
import os
import sys
from urllib.parse import unquote, urlsplit

path = sys.argv[1]
if path.startswith("file://"):
    url = urlsplit(path)
    if url.netloc not in ("", "localhost") or "%2f" in url.path.lower():
        sys.exit(1)
    path = unquote(url.path, errors="strict")
if path == "~" or path.startswith("~/"):
    path = os.path.expanduser("~") + path[1:]
print(os.path.realpath(path))
' "$1" 2>/dev/null
}

file_path=$(jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // empty' 2>/dev/null) || exit 0
[[ -n "$file_path" ]] || exit 0
event_path=$(canonical_path "$file_path") || exit 0
[[ "$event_path" == */.project-map/index.html ]] || exit 0

listing=$(terminal-browser ls --all --json 2>/dev/null) || exit 0
candidates=$(jq -c '
    [.browsers[]? | .cdpPort as $port
     | select($port | type == "number")
     | select($port >= 1 and $port <= 65535 and $port == ($port | floor))
     | .tabs[]?
     | select(.url | strings | startswith("file://"))
     | select(.targetId | strings | test("^[A-Fa-f0-9]{32}\\z"))
     | [$port, .targetId, .url]][]
' <<< "$listing" 2>/dev/null) || exit 0
selection=""
while IFS= read -r candidate; do
    [[ -n "$candidate" ]] || continue
    tab_path=$(canonical_path "$(jq -r '.[2]' <<< "$candidate")") || continue
    [[ "$tab_path" == "$event_path" ]] || continue
    selection=$(jq -r '.[0:2] | @tsv' <<< "$candidate")
    selected_url=$(jq -c '.[2]' <<< "$candidate")
    break
done <<< "$candidates"
if [[ -z "$selection" ]]; then
    terminal-browser open "$file_path" --split right --size 0.5 --no-merge >/dev/null 2>&1
    exit 0
fi
IFS=$'\t' read -r port target_id <<< "$selection"

agent="${TERMINAL_BROWSER_AGENT:-$HOME/.local/share/terminal-browser/app/agent-browser/bin/agent-browser}"
"$agent" --cdp "$port" --session project-map-reload --pin-tab tab "$target_id" >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
"$agent" --cdp "$port" --session project-map-reload --pin-tab eval "if (location.href === new URL($selected_url).href) location.reload()" >/dev/null 2>&1
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# Shared shell aliases used across machines.
# These aliases wrap common repository and local workflow commands.

# Use eza for ls command. In eza 0.23.5 `--icons` takes an optional WHEN value,
# so the bare flag swallows the first path argument and `ls dir` fails.
alias ls="eza --long --group --header --binary --time-style=long-iso --icons=auto"

# Alias for private chezmoi configuration
# ref. https://www.chezmoi.io/user-guide/frequently-asked-questions/design/#can-chezmoi-support-multiple-sources-or-multiple-source-states
alias chezmoi-private="chezmoi --source ~/.local/share/chezmoi-private --config ~/.config/chezmoi-private/chezmoi.yaml"

# Alias to checkout the default branch in git
alias gm='git checkout $(git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD | sed "s@^refs/remotes/origin/@@")'

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Approximate session staleness from public managed-asset mtimes.

This command never reads undocumented harness or session state. It compares a
caller-provided session epoch with public plugin-cache directories, managed
asset roots, and rendered settings. Detection is intentionally approximate.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import fcntl
import hashlib
import json
import math
import os
import re
import signal
import sys
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterator

WALL_LIMIT_S = 5
MAX_SCAN_ENTRIES = 10_000
MAX_HOOK_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 64 * 1024
MAX_STATE_FILES = 1_000
MAX_OUTPUT_LINES = 5
STATE_MAX_AGE_S = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60
EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES = {
    ".git",
    ".pytest_cache",
    ".ruff_cache",
    ".venv",
    "__pycache__",
    "health",
    "spool",
    "state",
}
MANAGED_ROOTS = (
    ("compactiondb", Path(".agents/compactiondb")),
    ("skills", Path(".agents/skills")),
    ("plugins", Path(".agents/plugins")),
)

Update = tuple[float, str, Path]


class QuietParser(argparse.ArgumentParser):
    def error(self, message: str) -> None:
        raise ValueError(message)


def version_key(version: str) -> tuple[tuple[int, int | str], ...]:
    return tuple(
        (0, int(token)) if token.isdigit() else (1, token.lower())
        for token in re.split(r"(\d+)", version)
    )


def display_path(path: Path, home: Path) -> str:
    try:
        return "~/" + str(path.relative_to(home))
    except ValueError:
        return str(path)


def excluded(path: Path, home: Path) -> bool:
    relative = path.relative_to(home)
    if any(part in EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES for part in relative.parts):
        return True
    if ".sqlite" in path.name.lower():
        return True
    parts = relative.parts
    return (
        len(parts) >= 4
        and parts[:3] == (".agents", "skills", "agmsg")
        and (parts[3] in {"db", "run", "teams"} or parts[3].startswith("db-"))
    )


def scan_files(root: Path, home: Path, deadline: float) -> Iterator[tuple[Path, float]]:
    if not root.is_dir():
        return
    pending = [root]
    scanned = 0
    while pending:
        if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
            raise TimeoutError("managed asset scan exceeded 5 seconds")
        directory = pending.pop()
        with os.scandir(directory) as entries:
            for entry in entries:
                scanned += 1
                # ponytail: bounded scan favors hook latency; raise only if 10k entries miss real updates.
                if scanned > MAX_SCAN_ENTRIES:
                    return
                path = Path(entry.path)
                if excluded(path, home):
                    continue
                if entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False):
                    pending.append(path)
                elif entry.is_file(follow_symlinks=False) or entry.is_symlink():
                    yield path, entry.stat(follow_symlinks=False).st_mtime


def plugin_cache_updates(
    home: Path, since: float | None, deadline: float
) -> list[Update]:
    cache = home / ".claude/plugins/cache"
    if not cache.is_dir():
        return []
    updates: list[Update] = []
    scanned = 0
    for marketplace in os.scandir(cache):
        if not marketplace.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False):
            continue
        for plugin in os.scandir(marketplace.path):
            if not plugin.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False):
                continue
            versions: list[tuple[str, float, Path]] = []
            for version in os.scandir(plugin.path):
                scanned += 1
                if scanned > MAX_SCAN_ENTRIES or time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                    raise TimeoutError("plugin cache scan exceeded its bound")
                if version.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False):
                    stat_result = version.stat(follow_symlinks=False)
                    versions.append(
                        (version.name, stat_result.st_mtime, Path(version.path))
                    )
            if since is None:
                updates.extend(
                    (mtime, f"claude-plugin:{marketplace.name}/{plugin.name}", path)
                    for _, mtime, path in versions
                )
                continue
            highest = max(versions, key=lambda item: version_key(item[0]), default=None)
            older = [item for item in versions if item[1] <= since]
            baseline = max(older, key=lambda item: version_key(item[0]), default=None)
            if (
                highest
                and highest[1] > since
                and (
                    baseline is None
                    or version_key(highest[0]) > version_key(baseline[0])
                )
            ):
                updates.append(
                    (
                        highest[1],
                        f"claude-plugin:{marketplace.name}/{plugin.name}",
                        highest[2],
                    )
                )
    return updates


def collect_updates(home: Path, since: float | None, deadline: float) -> list[Update]:
    updates = plugin_cache_updates(home, since, deadline)
    for label, relative_root in MANAGED_ROOTS:
        for path, mtime in scan_files(home / relative_root, home, deadline):
            if since is None or mtime > since:
                updates.append((mtime, label, path))
    settings = [("claude-settings", home / ".claude/settings.json")]
    codex_root = home / ".codex"
    if codex_root.is_dir():
        settings.extend(("codex-settings", path) for path in codex_root.glob("*.toml"))
    for label, path in settings:
        if path.is_file():
            mtime = path.stat().st_mtime
            if since is None or mtime > since:
                updates.append((mtime, label, path))
    return updates


def prune_state_files(state_dir: Path, deadline: float) -> None:
    cutoff = time.time() - STATE_MAX_AGE_S
    try:
        with os.scandir(state_dir) as entries:
            for index, entry in enumerate(entries):
                if index >= MAX_STATE_FILES or time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                    return
                try:
                    if (
                        entry.is_file(follow_symlinks=False)
                        and entry.stat(follow_symlinks=False).st_mtime < cutoff
                    ):
                        os.unlink(entry.path)
                except OSError:
                    pass
    except OSError:
        pass


def run_hook(home: Path, deadline: float) -> int:
    try:
        raw_payload = sys.stdin.read(MAX_HOOK_PAYLOAD_BYTES + 1)
        if len(raw_payload) > MAX_HOOK_PAYLOAD_BYTES:
            return 0
        payload = json.loads(raw_payload)
        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
            return 0
        session_id = payload.get("session_id")
        source = payload.get("source")
        if (
            not isinstance(session_id, str)
            or not session_id
            or (source is not None and not isinstance(source, str))
        ):
            return 0

        state_dir = home / ".local/state/agent-staleness"
        state_dir.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        state_dir.chmod(0o700)
        prune_state_files(state_dir, deadline)
        state_file = (
            state_dir / f"{hashlib.sha256(session_id.encode()).hexdigest()}.epoch"
        )
        flags = os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | getattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW", 0)
        descriptor = os.open(state_file, flags, 0o600)
        os.fchmod(descriptor, 0o600)
        with os.fdopen(descriptor, "r+") as baseline_file:
            fcntl.flock(baseline_file, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
            baseline = baseline_file.read().strip()
            if not baseline:
                baseline_file.write(f"{time.time()}\n")
                baseline_file.flush()
                return 0
        return run(["check", "--since", baseline], home, deadline)
    except Exception:
        return 0


def run(argv: list[str], home: Path, deadline: float) -> int:
    if not argv:
        updates = sorted(collect_updates(home, None, deadline), reverse=True)[:10]
        for mtime, label, path in updates:
            timestamp = (
                datetime.fromtimestamp(mtime, timezone.utc)
                .isoformat()
                .replace("+00:00", "Z")
            )
            print(f"{timestamp} {label} {display_path(path, home)}")
        return 0

    if argv[0] == "hook":
        return run_hook(home, deadline) if len(argv) == 1 else 0

    parser = QuietParser(description=__doc__)
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    check = subparsers.add_parser("check")
    check.add_argument("--since", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    since = float(args.since)
    if not math.isfinite(since) or since < 0:
        raise ValueError("--since must be a finite non-negative epoch")

    latest_by_label: dict[str, Update] = {}
    for update in collect_updates(home, since, deadline):
        current = latest_by_label.get(update[1])
        if current is None or update[0] > current[0]:
            latest_by_label[update[1]] = update
    for _mtime, label, path in sorted(latest_by_label.values(), reverse=True)[
        :MAX_OUTPUT_LINES
    ]:
        print(f"restart recommended: {label} ({display_path(path, home)})")
    return 0


def guarded_main(argv: list[str] | None = None, *, home: Path | None = None) -> int:
    arguments = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
    target_home = (
        Path(os.environ.get("HOME", str(Path.home()))) if home is None else home
    )
    previous_handler = signal.getsignal(signal.SIGALRM)

    def timeout_handler(_signum: int, _frame: object) -> None:
        raise TimeoutError("wall limit exceeded")

    signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, timeout_handler)
    signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, WALL_LIMIT_S)
    try:
        return run(arguments, target_home, time.monotonic() + WALL_LIMIT_S)
    except Exception as error:
        print(f"agent-session-staleness: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 0
    finally:
        signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, 0)
        signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, previous_handler)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(guarded_main())

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file bus-history.sh
# @brief Print a team's hcom bus history as TSV rows the records can paste.
# @description
#   Plan 025 W2b (C-1). Reads `hcom events --type message --thread <team> --full
#   --last <limit> [--after <since>]` (`hcom events --help`; hcom 0.7.30 and 0.7.31,
#   measured 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-24; at v0.7.30 src/commands/events.rs:33 last,
#   :39 full; `--last` is `ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT n`, events.rs:185, so the newest
#   rows) and prints one row per message,
#   ascending by id: `id<TAB>at<TAB>from<TAB>to<TAB>kind<TAB>body`. `at` is hcom's
#   `ts` as printed, `to` the delivered_to names joined with commas (`-` when
#   none), `kind` the first word of the text, and `body` the text with backslash,
#   tab, CR and LF escaped as `\\`, `\t`, `\r` and `\n`, so every row is one line
#   of five tabs. `--kind` keeps only the rows whose kind equals it. Never writes:
#   the store `$HCOM_DIR/hcom.db` must already exist, because `hcom events`
#   creates one on first use (observed with 0.7.30 and 0.7.31).
# @arg $1 string Team, the hcom thread (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`).
# @option --limit <n> Newest rows to read (default 200, a positive integer).
# @option --since <ts> Only rows after this time, hcom's `--after` (`YYYY-MM-DD[THH:MM:SS[Z]]`).
# @option --kind <kind> Only rows of this kind, the first word of the line (e.g. RESULT).
# @env HCOM_DIR The private hcom store directory; default: the store derived from the checkout (regime-env).
# @stdout TSV rows `id<TAB>at<TAB>from<TAB>to<TAB>kind<TAB>body`, possibly none.
# @exitcode 0 Printed.
# @exitcode 1 Usage error, store absent, or hcom failed (its error on stderr).
# @example
#   HCOM_DIR=/path/to/.hcom scripts/orchestrator/bus-history.sh dotfiles --limit 50 --kind RESULT
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
# @set LEVER_DIR The physical directory of this file, where the sourced regime-env helper sits (U33).
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    # shellcheck disable=SC2034 # read by the levers that source regime-env from this directory
    LEVER_DIR=${dir}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

usage='usage: bus-history.sh <team> [--limit <n>] [--since <ts>] [--kind <kind>]'
(($# >= 1)) || {
    echo "${usage}" >&2
    exit 1
}
team=$1
shift
limit=200 since='' kind=''
while (($#)); do
    (($# >= 2)) || {
        echo "${usage}" >&2
        exit 1
    }
    case $1 in
    --limit) limit=$2 ;;
    --since) since=$2 ;;
    --kind) kind=$2 ;;
    *)
        echo "${usage}" >&2
        exit 1
        ;;
    esac
    shift 2
done
[[ ${team} =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$ ]] || {
    echo "bus-history: team '${team}' is outside ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}\$" >&2
    exit 1
}
[[ ${limit} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || {
    echo 'bus-history: --limit must be a positive integer' >&2
    exit 1
}
# The store is HCOM_DIR when set, else the one derived from this checkout (regime-env, regime-cutover U33); a
# derived store that does not exist yet is refused like an explicit one, because `hcom events` would create it.
[[ -r ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env ]] || {
    echo "bus-history: refused: regime-env unreadable beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env" >&2
    exit 1
}
# shellcheck source=scripts/orchestrator/regime-env
. "${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env"
regime_env bus-history || exit 1
[[ -n ${HCOM_DIR:-} && -f ${HCOM_DIR:-}/hcom.db ]] || {
    echo "bus-history: store absent: \${HCOM_DIR}/hcom.db (HCOM_DIR=${HCOM_DIR:-unset})" >&2
    exit 1
}

query=(events --type message --thread "${team}" --full --last "${limit}")
[[ -z ${since} ]] || query+=(--after "${since}")
rows=$(hcom "${query[@]}") || exit 1
jq -rn --arg kind "${kind}" '
  def kind_of: [splits("[ \t]+") | select(. != "")][0] // "-";
  def escaped: gsub("\\\\"; "\\\\") | gsub("\t"; "\\t") | gsub("\r"; "\\r") | gsub("\n"; "\\n");
  [inputs | select(.type == "message")] | sort_by(.id)[]
  | select($kind == "" or (.data.text | kind_of) == $kind)
  | [(.id | tostring), .ts, (.data.from // "-"),
     ((.data.delivered_to // []) | if length == 0 then "-" else join(",") end),
     (.data.text | kind_of), (.data.text | escaped)]
  | join("\t")' <<< "${rows}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_cdgwq
# @brief Change into a repository path selected from `gwq`.
# @description
#   Uses `gwq list --json` and `fzf` to select a known repository path, then
#   changes the current shell into that directory.
# @example
#   cdgwq

# @description Fuzzy-select a `gwq` workspace path and `cd` into it.
function cdgwq() {
    # Require a Git worktree before reading `gwq` workspaces.
    if ! git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree &> /dev/null; then
        echo "Not inside a git repository."
        return 1
    fi
    local workspaces paths moveto
    if ! workspaces=$(gwq list --json); then
        echo "gwq list failed." >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if ! paths=$(jq -r '.[].path' <<< "$workspaces"); then
        echo "Cannot read the gwq workspace list." >&2
        return 1
    fi
    moveto=$(fzf <<< "$paths") || return 1
    cd -- "$moveto" || return 1
}

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    cdgwq
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_cdw
# @brief Change into the most recent `gwq` workspace.
# @description
#   Selects the newest path returned by `gwq list --json` and changes the
#   current shell into that repository.
# @example
#   cdw

# @description Jump to the newest `gwq` workspace path.
function cdw() {
    # Require a Git worktree before reading `gwq` workspaces.
    if ! git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree &> /dev/null; then
        echo "Not inside a git repository."
        return 1
    fi

    local workspaces moveto
    if ! workspaces=$(gwq list --json); then
        echo "gwq list failed." >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if ! moveto=$(jq -r 'max_by(.created_at) | .path' <<< "$workspaces"); then
        echo "Cannot read the gwq workspace list." >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if [ -z "$moveto" ]; then
        echo "No recent gwq found."
        return 1
    fi
    cd -- "$moveto" || return 1
}

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    cdw
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_chezmoi-cd
# @brief Change into the active chezmoi source directory.
# @description
#   Resolves `chezmoi source-path` and changes the current shell into that
#   repository checkout.
# @example
#   chezmoi-cd

# @description Change into the current chezmoi source path.
chezmoi-cd() {
    local source_path
    source_path=$(chezmoi source-path) || return
    cd -- "$source_path" || return
}

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    chezmoi-cd
fi

docs.text: Codex notify passes the JSON payload as the first argument; Codex command hooks (PreCompact, PostCompact, SessionEnd) deliver it on stdin. Either way the payload is ingested with --no-maintenance, which skips the SessionEnd retention pass, and the CLI gets 2 seconds, so the SessionEnd hook returns within Codex's 3-second limit; retention stays on the explicit prune command and on Claude Code's own SessionEnd hook. Failures print one stderr line and exit 0 so Codex is never blocked. Python runs isolated (-I), so a module committed in the session's working directory (for example a json.py in an untrusted repository) cannot shadow the standard library. Lookup walks from the session cwd to the nearest Git root (a .git directory or worktree gitfile), selecting the nearest opted-in project. Outside Git, only cwd is checked. The receiver's walk and vendor no-follow directory construction close pre-construction races; a same-user process swapping a storage path after construction remains outside this protection because later I/O, including SQLite, reopens paths by name.

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_contextdb-codex-notify
# @brief Ingest a Codex notification or hook event into an opted-in project's CompactionDB.
# @description
#   Codex `notify` passes the JSON payload as the first argument; Codex command
#   hooks (PreCompact, PostCompact, SessionEnd) deliver it on stdin. Either way
#   the payload is ingested with `--no-maintenance`, which skips the SessionEnd
#   retention pass, and the CLI gets 2 seconds, so the SessionEnd hook returns
#   within Codex's 3-second limit; retention stays on the explicit `prune`
#   command and on Claude Code's own SessionEnd hook. Failures print one stderr
#   line and exit 0 so Codex is never blocked. Python runs isolated (`-I`), so a
#   module committed in the session's working directory (for example a
#   `json.py` in an untrusted repository) cannot shadow the standard library.
#   Lookup walks from the session cwd to the nearest Git root (a .git directory
#   or worktree gitfile), selecting the nearest opted-in project. Outside Git,
#   only cwd is checked. The receiver's walk and vendor no-follow directory
#   construction close pre-construction races; a same-user process swapping a
#   storage path after construction remains outside this protection because
#   later I/O, including SQLite, reopens paths by name.
# @arg $1 string Optional JSON payload; read from stdin when absent.

if ! command -v python3 > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf '%s\n' 'contextdb-codex-notify: ingest failed' >&2
    exit 0
fi

payload="${1:-$(cat)}"

if ! python3 -I - "${payload}" 2> /dev/null << 'PY'
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

try:
    payload = sys.argv[1]
    event = json.loads(payload)
    if not isinstance(event, dict):
        raise ValueError("notify payload must be an object")
    cwd = event.get("cwd")
    if cwd is not None and not isinstance(cwd, str):
        raise ValueError("notify cwd must be a string")
    project_dir = (Path(cwd) if cwd else Path.cwd()).resolve()
    ancestors = (project_dir, *project_dir.parents)
    boundary = next((p for p in ancestors if os.path.lexists(p / ".git")), project_dir)
    for candidate in ancestors:
        if (candidate / ".claude" / "contextdb").is_dir():
            project_dir = candidate
            break
        if candidate == boundary:
            break
    opt_in = project_dir / ".claude" / "contextdb"
    cli = Path.home() / ".agents" / "compactiondb" / ".claude" / "hooks" / "contextdb_cli.py"
    # Only a real directory inside the project opts in: a repository could point
    # .claude or .claude/contextdb elsewhere with a symlink, and the CLI would
    # then create its state there.
    if not opt_in.is_dir() or opt_in.resolve() != opt_in or not cli.is_file():
        raise SystemExit(0)
    # The CLI creates, chmods and writes under this tree, so a symlink at any
    # depth would send its writes outside the project: refuse every symlink,
    # and require each storage directory to be a real directory or absent.
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(opt_in, followlinks=False):
        for name in dirs + files:
            if os.path.islink(os.path.join(root, name)):
                raise ValueError(f"{os.path.join(root, name)} must not be a symlink")
    for child in ("state", "spool", "spool/incoming", "spool/quarantine", "health"):
        storage = opt_in / child
        if storage.exists() and not storage.is_dir():
            raise ValueError(f"{storage} must be a directory")
    subprocess.run(
        [
            sys.executable,
            str(cli),
            "--project-root",
            str(project_dir),
            "ingest",
            "--ingested-from",
            "codex",
            "--no-maintenance",
        ],
        input=payload,
        text=True,
        stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        timeout=2,
        check=True,
        cwd=project_dir,
    )
except Exception:
    raise SystemExit(1)
PY
then
    printf '%s\n' 'contextdb-codex-notify: ingest failed' >&2
fi

exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_dev
# @brief Change into a repository selected from `ghq`.
# @description
#   Lets the user choose a repository path from `ghq` and changes into it.
# @example
#   dev

# @description Fuzzy-select a repository path from `ghq`.
function ghq-path() {
    local repositories selected_path
    if ! repositories=$(ghq list --full-path); then
        echo "ghq list failed." >&2
        return 1
    fi
    selected_path=$(fzf <<< "$repositories") || return 1
    [[ -n $selected_path ]] || return 1
    printf '%s\n' "$selected_path"
}

# @description Change into a selected `ghq` repository.
function dev() {
    local moveto
    moveto=$(ghq-path) || return 0
    cd -- "$moveto" || exit 1
}

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    dev
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_fgc
# @brief Fuzzy-pick and checkout a local Git branch.
# @description
#   Lists local branches, selects one with `fzf`, and checks it out.
# @example
#   fgc

# @description Checkout a branch selected from the local branch list.
function fgc() {
    local branches branch
    if ! branches=$(git for-each-ref refs/heads/ --format='%(refname:short)'); then
        echo "Cannot list the local branches." >&2
        return 1
    fi
    branch=$(fzf <<< "$branches") || return 1
    git checkout "$branch"
}

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    fgc
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_git-delete-merged-branches
# @brief Delete local branches already merged through squash-and-merge.
# @description
#   Detects the repository default branch, compares local branches against it,
#   and removes branches whose tree has already been integrated upstream.
# @example
#   git-delete-merged-branches

# @description Check whether the current directory is inside a Git repository.
function is_inside_git_repository() {
    git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree > /dev/null 2>&1
}

# @description Detect the default branch name from the `origin` remote.
# @exitcode 1 When `git remote show origin` fails or names no HEAD branch.
function get_default_branch() {
    local remote_info default_branch

    remote_info=$(LC_ALL=C git remote show origin) || return 1
    default_branch=$(sed -n '/HEAD branch/s/.*: //p' <<< "${remote_info}") || return 1
    [[ -n ${default_branch} ]] || return 1
    echo -n "${default_branch}"
}

# @description Delete local branches whose content is already on the default branch.
# @exitcode 1 When the default branch, the branch list or a branch's squash check cannot be read; nothing more is deleted.
function git-delete-merged-branches() {
    # delete all git branches which have been "squash and merge" via GitHub
    # ref. https://stackoverflow.com/questions/43489303/how-can-i-delete-all-git-branches-which-have-been-squash-and-merge-via-github

    if ! is_inside_git_repository; then
        return 0
    fi

    local default_branch branches branch merge_base tree squashed cherry
    if ! default_branch=$(get_default_branch); then
        echo "git-delete-merged-branches: cannot read the HEAD branch of origin; nothing deleted" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    git checkout -q "${default_branch}" || return 1
    if ! branches=$(git for-each-ref refs/heads/ "--format=%(refname:short)"); then
        echo "git-delete-merged-branches: cannot list the local branches; nothing deleted" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    while read -r branch; do
        [[ -n ${branch} ]] || continue
        # No common ancestor: the branch was never forked from the default branch.
        merge_base=$(git merge-base "${default_branch}" "${branch}") || continue
        if ! tree=$(git rev-parse "${branch}^{tree}") ||
            ! squashed=$(git commit-tree "${tree}" -p "${merge_base}" -m _) ||
            ! cherry=$(git cherry "${default_branch}" "${squashed}"); then
            echo "git-delete-merged-branches: cannot check whether ${branch} was squash-merged; stopping" >&2
            return 1
        fi
        if [[ ${cherry} == "-"* ]]; then
            git branch -D "${branch}"
        fi
    done <<< "${branches}"
}

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    git-delete-merged-branches
fi

docs.text: Plan 025 W2b (C-1). Keeps agmsg-dispatch's argument form so every caller keeps its call: the words after the pane are joined with spaces into one line, which reaches hcom as one argument after -- (hcom send --help: "Everything after -- is the message"). The send is hcom send @<to> --thread <team> --from <from> --json -- <line> (hcom 0.7.30 and 0.7.31, measured 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-24; the send.rs and events.rs lines are at v0.7.30): @<to> is the seat's exact hcom name (send --help "Target matching"; a name hcom does not know fails with its "No active agent" error), --thread <team> seeds the team thread the seat answers in with hcom send --thread <team> -- <line> and no target (src/commands/send.rs:300 refuses a thread without members, so the TASK carries the mention), --from <from> is the external sender identity (send.rs:96; the row's from, send.rs:403) and --json prints {"delivered_to": [...], "event_id": N} on stdout (send.rs:1135). hcom's own error stays on stderr and its exit status is passed through. The event id is then read back with hcom events --type message --thread <team> --sql "id = N" --full (src/commands/events.rs:45 sql, :39 full), so the receipt names a row the bus holds, the one bus-history.sh prints: id=<N> at=<hcom ts> to=<to> kind=<first word of the line>. The pane argument is accepted and unused: hcom delivers to a bound seat itself (hcom list --help: "[OMP] hcom-launched, automatic delivery"), so there is no wake. The store is $HCOM_DIR/hcom.db (hcom start --help: "Prefix all hcom commands with: HCOM_DIR=..."); an unset HCOM_DIR or an absent store is refused before any hcom call, because hcom creates a store on first use and the seats' launch owns that.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file hcom-dispatch
# @brief Send one protocol line from one seat to another over hcom and print a durable receipt.
# @description
#   Plan 025 W2b (C-1). Keeps agmsg-dispatch's argument form so every caller keeps
#   its call: the words after the pane are joined with spaces into one line, which
#   reaches hcom as one argument after `--` (`hcom send --help`: "Everything after
#   -- is the message"). The send is
#   `hcom send @<to> --thread <team> --from <from> --json -- <line>` (hcom 0.7.30 and 0.7.31,
#   measured 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-24; the send.rs and events.rs lines are at v0.7.30):
#   `@<to>` is the seat's exact hcom name (send --help "Target matching"; a name
#   hcom does not know fails with its "No active agent" error), `--thread <team>`
#   seeds the team thread the seat answers in with `hcom send --thread <team> --
#   <line>` and no target (src/commands/send.rs:300 refuses a thread without
#   members, so the TASK carries the mention), `--from <from>` is the external
#   sender identity (send.rs:96; the row's `from`, send.rs:403) and `--json` prints
#   `{"delivered_to": [...], "event_id": N}` on stdout (send.rs:1135). hcom's own
#   error stays on stderr and its exit status is passed through. The event id is
#   then read back with `hcom events --type message --thread <team> --sql "id = N"
#   --full` (src/commands/events.rs:45 sql, :39 full), so the receipt names a row
#   the bus holds, the one bus-history.sh prints:
#   `id=<N> at=<hcom ts> to=<to> kind=<first word of the line>`.
#   The pane argument is accepted and unused: hcom delivers to a bound seat itself
#   (`hcom list --help`: "[OMP] hcom-launched, automatic delivery"), so there is no
#   wake. The store is `$HCOM_DIR/hcom.db` (`hcom start --help`: "Prefix all hcom
#   commands with: HCOM_DIR=..."); an unset HCOM_DIR or an absent store is refused
#   before any hcom call, because hcom creates a store on first use and the seats'
#   launch owns that.
# @arg $1 string Team, the hcom thread (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`).
# @arg $2 string Sender seat, same grammar.
# @arg $3 string Recipient seat, its exact hcom name, same grammar.
# @arg $4 string Pane or seat label, accepted for agmsg-dispatch's form, unused.
# @arg $@ string Message words, joined with spaces into one line.
# @env HCOM_DIR The private hcom store directory; default: the store derived from the checkout (regime-env).
# @stdout One receipt line `id=<event id> at=<ts> to=<to> kind=<kind>`.
# @exitcode 0 Sent and found in the bus.
# @exitcode 1 Usage, grammar, empty line, store absent, or the sent id was not found.
# @exitcode * hcom's own status when the send fails (its error on stderr).
# @example
#   HCOM_DIR=/path/to/.hcom hcom-dispatch dotfiles orch u5team-nemo w1:p2 'TASK v1 task_id=T1 ...'
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
# @set LEVER_DIR The physical directory of this file, where the sourced regime-env helper sits (U33).
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    # shellcheck disable=SC2034 # read by the levers that source regime-env from this directory
    LEVER_DIR=${dir}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

(($# >= 5)) || {
    echo 'usage: hcom-dispatch <team> <from> <to> <pane> <line...>' >&2
    exit 1
}
team=$1 from=$2 to=$3
shift 4
line=$*
for identifier in "${team}" "${from}" "${to}"; do
    [[ ${identifier} =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$ ]] || {
        echo "hcom-dispatch: identifier '${identifier}' is outside ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}\$" >&2
        exit 1
    }
done
[[ -n ${line} ]] || {
    echo 'hcom-dispatch: empty line' >&2
    exit 1
}
# The store is HCOM_DIR when set, else the one derived from this checkout (regime-env, regime-cutover U33); a
# derived store that does not exist yet is refused like an explicit one, because `hcom events` would create it.
[[ -r ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env ]] || {
    echo "hcom-dispatch: refused: regime-env unreadable beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env" >&2
    exit 1
}
# shellcheck source=scripts/orchestrator/regime-env
. "${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env"
regime_env hcom-dispatch || exit 1
[[ -n ${HCOM_DIR:-} && -f ${HCOM_DIR:-}/hcom.db ]] || {
    echo "hcom-dispatch: store absent: \${HCOM_DIR}/hcom.db (HCOM_DIR=${HCOM_DIR:-unset})" >&2
    exit 1
}

receipt=$(hcom send "@${to}" --thread "${team}" --from "${from}" --json -- "${line}")
id=$(jq -r '.event_id' <<< "${receipt}" 2> /dev/null) || id=
[[ ${id} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || {
    echo "hcom-dispatch: no event_id in the hcom receipt: ${receipt}" >&2
    exit 1
}
row=$(hcom events --type message --thread "${team}" --sql "id = ${id}" --full)
[[ -n ${row} ]] || {
    echo "hcom-dispatch: sent event ${id} was not found in thread ${team}" >&2
    exit 1
}
jq -r --arg to "${to}" '
  def kind_of: [splits("[ \t]+") | select(. != "")][0] // "-";
  "id=\(.id) at=\(.ts) to=\($to) kind=\(.data.text | kind_of)"' <<< "${row}"

docs.title: home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_hcom-seat
docs.text: Plan 025 W5b (U7), the minimal form before X. A seat is one omp process that hcom omp starts in a herdr pane (hcom omp --help: hcom [N] omp [args...], --tag <name>, --dir <path>, --terminal <preset>; hcom gives the seat HCOM_LAUNCHED=1, HCOM_TAG and HCOM_DIR). For <role> the launch line is hcom omp --tag <name> --dir <dir> --terminal herdr --go -- --profile <role> --config ~/.agents/omp/policies/<role>.yml --config ~/.agents/omp/profiles/<role>.yml -e <ext>...; hcom drops the -- and forwards what follows to omp verbatim (hcom 0.7.30 and 0.7.31, measured 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-24; extract_launch_flags, src/commands/launch.rs:572-581 at v0.7.30). --go is hcom's launch gate: inside an AI tool, hcom without it prints == LAUNCH PREVIEW == / Add --go to proceed. and starts nothing (launch.rs:48,388-389, measured on the real host 2026-10-23), and extract_launch_flags consumes it only before the -- (launch.rs:650-652). The profile equals the role. A named profile reads its own ~/.omp/profiles/<role>/agent/config.yml (pi-utils src/dirs.ts:312-315, U10), so the manifest's modelRoles.default and skills.customDirectories reach the seat only through the second overlay, rendered per role (U14); the first overlay owns the approval mode (U6). Both are required. The extensions default to the pi-claude-bridge, which the role's model route needs, plus the openai-siwc when it is present; --ext replaces that list. There is no audit seat: every audit is one fresh omp-run.sh --role audit run (regime-cutover U57, U58). The stop gate's directory ~/.agents/omp/hooks is loaded on every launch, whatever --ext says, and the launch line ends with --hcom-team <HCOM_TEAM>: hcom passes HCOM_DIR into the pane but not HCOM_TEAM, so the flag, which the gate registers, carries exactly the team this launch was given, an explicit one included (regime-cutover U33c; omp refuses the flag when no loaded extension registers it, so a launch without the gate fails instead of running unguarded). Every directory, a default, --ext or the gate's, must resolve to an entry of claude.levers.extensions in the manifest the self-check reads (regime-cutover U31), else the launch is refused. The orchestrator sits in the repository this command runs in; every other role gets the worktree <seats-root>/<name>, which is created detached from origin/main (HEAD in a repository without it) when absent and reused when it is a worktree of this repository (any other directory at that path is refused). HCOM_DIR, HCOM_TEAM and the seats root come from the environment or --seats-root when set, else from the checkout through the sourced regime-env helper (regime-cutover U33: ~/.local/state/hcom/<slug>, <slug>, ~/.local/state/omp-seats/<slug>), and are exported to the seat. Every input is checked before anything is created or started: an unknown role, a name or team outside ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$, a store regime-env refuses, hcom absent from PATH, an absent policy or profile overlay or extension directory, or a cwd outside a git checkout is exit 2 with the reason. --dry-run prints the launch line, and the derived environment on stderr, and creates and starts nothing. Otherwise hcom's own exit status is returned (hcom omp --help: 0 ready, 1 launch failed, 2 still launching or blocked on user attention).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file hcom-seat
# @brief Start one omp seat for a role in a herdr pane through `hcom omp`, with its profile, policy overlay and extensions wired in.
# @description
#   Plan 025 W5b (U7), the minimal form before X. A seat is one omp process that
#   `hcom omp` starts in a herdr pane (`hcom omp --help`: `hcom [N] omp [args...]`,
#   `--tag <name>`, `--dir <path>`, `--terminal <preset>`; hcom gives the seat
#   HCOM_LAUNCHED=1, HCOM_TAG and HCOM_DIR). For `<role>` the launch line is
#   `hcom omp --tag <name> --dir <dir> --terminal herdr --go -- --profile <role>
#   --config ~/.agents/omp/policies/<role>.yml --config ~/.agents/omp/profiles/<role>.yml
#   -e <ext>...`; hcom drops the `--` and forwards what follows to omp verbatim
#   (hcom 0.7.30 and 0.7.31, measured 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-24; `extract_launch_flags`,
#   `src/commands/launch.rs:572-581` at v0.7.30). `--go`
#   is hcom's launch gate: inside an AI tool, hcom without it prints `== LAUNCH
#   PREVIEW == / Add --go to proceed.` and starts nothing (`launch.rs:48,388-389`,
#   measured on the real host 2026-10-23), and `extract_launch_flags` consumes it
#   only before the `--` (`launch.rs:650-652`). The profile equals the role. A
#   named profile reads its own `~/.omp/profiles/<role>/agent/config.yml`
#   (pi-utils `src/dirs.ts:312-315`, U10),
#   so the manifest's `modelRoles.default` and `skills.customDirectories` reach the
#   seat only through the second overlay, rendered per role (U14); the first overlay
#   owns the approval mode (U6). Both are required. The extensions default to the
#   pi-claude-bridge, which the role's model route needs, plus the openai-siwc when it
#   is present; `--ext` replaces that list. There is no audit seat: every audit is one
#   fresh `omp-run.sh --role audit` run (regime-cutover U57, U58). The stop gate's directory
#   `~/.agents/omp/hooks` is loaded on every launch, whatever `--ext` says, and the
#   launch line ends with `--hcom-team <HCOM_TEAM>`: hcom passes HCOM_DIR into the
#   pane but not HCOM_TEAM, so the flag, which the gate registers, carries exactly the
#   team this launch was given, an explicit one included (regime-cutover U33c; omp
#   refuses the flag when no loaded extension registers it, so a launch without the
#   gate fails instead of running unguarded). Every directory, a default, `--ext` or
#   the gate's, must resolve to an entry of `claude.levers.extensions` in the manifest
#   the self-check reads (regime-cutover U31), else the launch is refused. The
#   orchestrator sits in the repository
#   this command runs in; every other role gets the worktree `<seats-root>/<name>`,
#   which is created detached from `origin/main` (HEAD in a repository without it)
#   when absent and reused when it is a worktree of this repository (any other
#   directory at that path is refused). HCOM_DIR, HCOM_TEAM and the seats root come
#   from the environment or `--seats-root` when set, else from the checkout through
#   the sourced regime-env helper (regime-cutover U33: `~/.local/state/hcom/<slug>`,
#   `<slug>`, `~/.local/state/omp-seats/<slug>`), and are exported to the seat.
#   Every input is checked before anything is created or started: an unknown role,
#   a name or team outside `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`, a store regime-env refuses, hcom absent from
#   PATH, an absent policy or profile overlay or extension directory, or a cwd outside a git checkout
#   is exit 2 with the reason. `--dry-run` prints the launch line, and the derived
#   environment on stderr, and creates and starts nothing. Otherwise hcom's own exit status is returned (`hcom omp --help`:
#   0 ready, 1 launch failed, 2 still launching or blocked on user attention).
# @arg $1 string Role: orchestrator or worker.
# @option --name <name> Seat name, passed as the hcom tag (default: the role; `<role>-<n>` for a second seat of a role).
# @option --seats-root <dir> Parent of the seat worktrees (default: ~/.local/state/omp-seats/<slug>, regime-env).
# @option --ext <dir> Extension directory in claude.levers.extensions, repeatable; replaces the role's default list.
# @option --dry-run Print the launch line and exit 0 without creating a worktree or starting hcom.
# @env HCOM_DIR The program's private hcom store (default: ~/.local/state/hcom/<slug>, regime-env).
# @env HCOM_TEAM The team thread (default: the repository slug, regime-env); passed to the seat as --hcom-team.
# @stdout The launch line with --dry-run, else hcom's output.
# @exitcode 0 Dry run printed, or hcom reports the seat ready.
# @exitcode 2 A refusal, before anything is created or started.
# @exitcode * hcom's own status otherwise.
# @example
#   HCOM_DIR=/path/to/.hcom scripts/orchestrator/hcom-seat worker --name worker-2 --dry-run
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
# @set LEVER_DIR The physical directory of this file, where the sourced regime-env helper sits (U33).
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    # shellcheck disable=SC2034 # read by the levers that source regime-env from this directory
    LEVER_DIR=${dir}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

usage='usage: hcom-seat <orchestrator|worker> [--name <name>] [--seats-root <dir>] [--ext <dir>]... [--dry-run]'
refuse() {
    echo "hcom-seat: $*" >&2
    exit 2
}

(($# >= 1)) || refuse "${usage}"
role=$1
shift
name=${role} seats_root='' dry_run=0 user_exts=()
while (($#)); do
    case $1 in
    --dry-run) dry_run=1 ;;
    --name | --seats-root | --ext)
        (($# >= 2)) || refuse "${usage}"
        case $1 in
        --name) name=$2 ;;
        --seats-root) seats_root=$2 ;;
        --ext) user_exts+=("$2") ;;
        esac
        shift
        ;;
    *) refuse "${usage}" ;;
    esac
    shift
done

bridge=${HOME}/.local/lib/omp-extensions/pi-claude-bridge
siwc=${HOME}/.agents/omp/extensions/openai-siwc
gate=${HOME}/.agents/omp/hooks
# The extension the role's model route needs first, the optional one second.
case ${role} in
orchestrator | worker) exts=("${bridge}" "${siwc}") ;;
*) refuse "unknown role '${role}'; expected orchestrator or worker" ;;
esac
[[ ${name} =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$ ]] || refuse "name '${name}' is outside ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}\$"
# HCOM_DIR, HCOM_TEAM and the seats root come from the environment when set, else from this checkout (regime-env,
# regime-cutover U33). hcom passes HCOM_DIR into the seat but not HCOM_TEAM, so the team rides --hcom-team below.
[[ -r ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env ]] || refuse "regime-env unreadable beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env"
# shellcheck source=scripts/orchestrator/regime-env
. "${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env"
regime_env hcom-seat || exit 2
command -v hcom > /dev/null || refuse 'hcom not found on PATH'
[[ ${HCOM_TEAM:-} =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$ ]] || refuse "team '${HCOM_TEAM:-}' is outside ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}\$"
policy=${HOME}/.agents/omp/policies/${role}.yml
profile=${HOME}/.agents/omp/profiles/${role}.yml
[[ -f ${policy} ]] || refuse "policy overlay absent: ${policy}"
[[ -f ${profile} ]] || refuse "profile overlay absent: ${profile}"
if ((${#user_exts[@]})); then
    exts=("${user_exts[@]}")
elif [[ ! -d ${exts[1]} ]]; then
    exts=("${exts[0]}")
fi
# The stop gate rides every launch, after the route's extensions; --ext never drops it (U33c).
exts+=("${gate}")
# The extension allow-list (regime-cutover U31): claude.levers.extensions in the manifest the self-check read, so the
# installed copy reads it from ~/.agents, outside every sandbox write root. A read failure is a refusal, not an empty list.
allowed=$(awk '
    /^  levers:$/ { levers = 1; next }
    levers && /^  [^ ]/ { levers = 0 }
    levers && /^    extensions:$/ { list = 1; next }
    list && /^      - / { sub(/^      - /, ""); print; next }
    list { list = 0 }
' "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || refuse "cannot read the extension allow-list in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}"
[[ -n ${allowed} ]] || refuse "no extension allow-list (claude.levers.extensions) in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}"
# The launch passes the canonical allow-list entry (`pwd -P` of the listed path), never the caller's spelling: a
# symlink the caller controls could be swapped between this check and omp resolving `-e`.
checked=()
for ext in "${exts[@]}"; do
    [[ -d ${ext} ]] || refuse "extension directory absent: ${ext}"
    real=$(cd "${ext}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve extension directory: ${ext}"
    listed=''
    while IFS= read -r entry; do
        entry=${entry/#\~/${HOME}}
        # An entry that is absent or cannot be resolved lists nothing, so the extension stays refused.
        [[ -d ${entry} ]] || continue
        entry_real=$(cd "${entry}" && pwd -P) || continue
        if [[ ${entry_real} == "${real}" ]]; then listed=${entry_real}; fi # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
    done <<< "${allowed}"
    [[ -n ${listed} ]] || refuse "extension directory is not in the allow-list (claude.levers.extensions): ${ext}"
    checked+=("${listed}")
done
exts=("${checked[@]}")
repo=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2> /dev/null) || refuse 'run hcom-seat inside the repository checkout'
common=$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir) || refuse "cannot read the git common directory of ${repo}"
seats_root=${seats_root:-${REGIME_SEATS_ROOT:-}}
[[ -n ${seats_root} ]] || refuse 'no seats root: pass --seats-root or run inside a checkout'
case ${role} in
orchestrator) dir=${repo} ;;
*) dir=${seats_root}/${name} ;;
esac

argv=(hcom omp --tag "${name}" --dir "${dir}" --terminal herdr --go -- --profile "${role}" --config "${policy}" --config "${profile}")
for ext in "${exts[@]}"; do
    argv+=(-e "${ext}")
done
argv+=(--hcom-team "${HCOM_TEAM}")
if ((dry_run)); then
    printf '%q ' "${argv[@]}"
    echo
    echo "hcom-seat: environment HCOM_DIR=${HCOM_DIR} HCOM_TEAM=${HCOM_TEAM:-}" >&2
    exit 0
fi
# U37: a remote seat host needs this host's own login first (seat-login-preflight beside this file).
"${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}/seat-login-preflight" "${role}" || exit $?
if [[ ! -e ${dir} ]]; then
    # A repository without a remote (a fresh project) seats its worktrees at HEAD instead of origin/main. Only a
    # genuinely absent ref means that: a ref that is broken or names no commit, or a failed git, is a refusal.
    origin_main=$(git -C "${repo}" for-each-ref --format='%(objecttype)' refs/remotes/origin/main 2>&1) ||
        refuse "cannot inspect refs/remotes/origin/main in ${repo}: ${origin_main}"
    case ${origin_main} in
    commit) base=origin/main ;;
    '')
        base=HEAD
        echo "hcom-seat: origin/main is absent in ${repo}; the seat worktree starts at HEAD" >&2
        ;;
    *) refuse "refs/remotes/origin/main in ${repo} does not resolve to a commit: ${origin_main}" ;;
    esac
    git -C "${repo}" worktree add --detach "${dir}" "${base}"
elif ! seat_common=$(git -C "${dir}" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2> /dev/null) ||
    ! [[ -d ${dir} && ${seat_common} -ef ${common} ]]; then
    # A stale or foreign directory at the seat path would seat omp in the wrong tree.
    refuse "seat directory exists and is not a worktree of ${repo}: ${dir}"
fi
exec "${argv[@]}"
