<pre><code>#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file herdr-agents
# @brief Retire the agmsg regime from a checkout.
# @description
#   Retire mode (--retire-agmsg, run by `make update` before `chezmoi apply`)
#   turns the checkout's agmsg wiring off and also removes the pre-push stub
#   that earlier versions wrote for the retired main-push guard; the GitHub
#   ruleset on `main` is the boundary. The Herdr layout, attach, worker and
#   audit modes were agmsg seat tooling and are gone (regime-cutover U26).
# @option --retire-agmsg Remove agmsg hooks and leave agmsg teams without changing Herdr panes: in DIR, or without DIR in every registered clone of this repo
# @arg DIR Optional directory to retire. Without it, every registered clone of this repository and the current directory.

set -euo pipefail

# @description Print usage information.
function usage() {
    cat << 'USAGE'
Usage: herdr-agents --retire-agmsg [DIR]

Retire mode turns the agmsg regime off for DIR (E1 of plan 025): it removes
every agmsg hook from DIR/.claude/settings.local.json with delivery.sh set off,
makes each claude-code agmsg identity registered at DIR leave its team, and
prints one line per action, or `agmsg already retired for DIR` when there was
nothing to do. Without DIR it first visits every project the agmsg team store
registers whose root commits and origin owner/repo match the current
directory's, retiring each the same way, then retires the current directory; a
registered project of another repository is printed as skipped with its team
and path and left untouched. It also removes the pre-push stub that earlier versions wrote
for the retired main-push guard (any other pre-push hook is left alone); the
GitHub ruleset on main is the boundary.
USAGE
}

# @description Remove the pre-push stub that earlier `--bootstrap-agmsg` runs
#   wrote for the retired main-push guard, and its decision log. The GitHub
#   ruleset on `main` is the boundary now, and with the guard mode gone the
#   stub would refuse every push to `main`. The hook is resolved the way the
#   installer placed it (`git rev-parse --git-path hooks`, which honours
#   core.hooksPath) and only inside the common git dir, where alone the
#   installer wrote. Only a hook whose content is exactly that stub (git blob
#   af94a0b5…, the one fixed body every install wrote) is removed. An edited
#   copy that kept the stub's header is left unchanged with a notice, and any
#   other pre-push hook is left alone.
# @arg $1 workdir Repository path.
function remove_retired_pre_push_stub() {
    local workdir="$1" common_dir hook blob header
    local stub_blob=af94a0b55e08a02423f72f3d4f713a4a804d905e

    common_dir="$(git -C "${workdir}" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2> /dev/null)" || return 0
    hook="$(git -C "${workdir}" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path hooks 2> /dev/null)/pre-push" || return 0
    # The installer never wrote outside the common git dir (a core.hooksPath
    # elsewhere was left alone), so a hook there is not ours to remove.
    [[ ${hook} == "${common_dir}"/* && -f ${hook} ]] || return 0
    if ! blob="$(git -C "${workdir}" hash-object --no-filters -- "${hook}")"; then
        printf 'herdr-agents: cannot hash %s, so whether it is the retired main-push guard stub is unknown; nothing removed\n' "${hook}" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    if [[ ${blob} == "${stub_blob}" ]]; then
        rm -f -- "${hook}" "${common_dir}/orch-push-main.log"
        printf 'herdr-agents: removed the retired main-push guard stub at %s; the GitHub ruleset on main is the boundary.\n' "${hook}" >&2
        return 0
    fi
    if ! header="$(sed -n 2p "${hook}")"; then
        printf 'herdr-agents: cannot read %s, so whether it is an edited main-push guard stub is unknown\n' "${hook}" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    if [[ ${header} == "# herdr-agents main-push guard:"* ]]; then
        printf 'herdr-agents: %s is an edited copy of the retired main-push guard stub; leaving it unchanged. Remove it by hand: without the guard mode it may refuse every push to main.\n' "${hook}" >&2
    fi
}

# @description Report whether a Claude Code settings file carries an agmsg hook.
#   jq -e exits 1 only for a false result; any other failure (an unreadable,
#   empty or malformed file) is an inspection error, never "no hooks".
# @arg $1 path Settings file.
# @exitcode 0 When any hook command contains `agmsg/scripts/`.
# @exitcode 1 When the file is absent or carries no agmsg hook.
# @exitcode 2 When the file exists but cannot be read as JSON.
function agmsg_hook_state() {
    local status=0

    [[ -e $1 || -L $1 ]] || return 1
    jq -e 'any(.hooks[]?[]?.hooks[]?; (.command // "") | contains("agmsg/scripts/"))' "$1" > /dev/null 2>&1 || status=$?
    ((status <= 1)) || return 2
    return "${status}"
}

# @description Print the agmsg hook state of a settings file, or exit 1 naming
#   it when it cannot be inspected.
# @arg $1 path Settings file.
# @arg $2 string When the check runs: `before` or `after` delivery.sh set off.
# @stdout `present` or `absent`.
function agmsg_hooks_or_fail() {
    local status=0

    agmsg_hook_state "$1" || status=$?
    case "${status}" in
    0) printf 'present\n' ;;
    1) printf 'absent\n' ;;
    *)
        printf 'herdr-agents: cannot read %s as JSON %s delivery.sh set off; agmsg hooks unknown, nothing retired from it\n' "$1" "$2" >&2
        exit 1
        ;;
    esac
}

# @description Skip $HOME or turn the checkout's agmsg wiring off: remove the
#   agmsg hooks from DIR/.claude/settings.local.json with `delivery.sh set off`
#   and make every claude-code identity registered at DIR leave its team, after
#   removing the retired main-push guard stub (remove_retired_pre_push_stub).
#   Prints one line per action, or one `agmsg already retired` line. delivery.sh
#   never touches permissions, so an agmsg allow rule it leaves is reported,
#   never edited here.
# @arg $1 workdir Repository path used for repo-scoped agmsg registration; a
#   registered path whose directory is gone skips the $HOME and pre-push steps.
# @arg $2 string Optional `--registered <identity>`, the no-DIR form: before a
#   leave.sh call, keep a membership whose member is also registered at a
#   project that is not a clone of this repository (repository_identity equal
#   to <identity>), since leave.sh drops the whole member (leave.sh:85-93)
#   while join.sh appends one registration per project (join.sh:211-228).
# @arg $4 string Optional `--report-skips` after `--registered <identity>`:
#   print a line when DIR has no agmsg hook (each registered project visited).
# @exitcode 1 When the settings file cannot be read as JSON, an agmsg hook
#   survives `set off`, identities.sh fails, or leave.sh fails.
function retire_agmsg() {
    local workdir="$1" registered=false identity="" report_skips="" other

    if [[ ${2:-} == --registered ]]; then
        registered=true
        identity="${3:-}"
        report_skips="${4:-}"
    fi

    if [[ -d ${workdir} ]]; then
        local real_workdir real_home
        if ! real_workdir="$(cd -- "${workdir}" && pwd -P)" || ! real_home="$(cd -- "${HOME}" && pwd -P)"; then
            printf 'herdr-agents: cannot resolve %s or the home directory to a physical path; nothing retired from it\n' "${workdir}" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
        if [[ ${real_workdir} == "${real_home}" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
            printf "Skipping agmsg retire for \$HOME; use a repository directory instead.\n" >&2
            return 0
        fi
        remove_retired_pre_push_stub "${real_workdir}"
    fi

    local scripts="${HOME}/.agents/skills/agmsg/scripts"
    local delivery="${scripts}/delivery.sh"
    local claude_hooks_file="${workdir}/.claude/settings.local.json"
    local log_file="${HOME}/.config/herdr/herdr-agents.log"
    local teams_dir="${HOME}/.agents/skills/agmsg/teams"
    local acted=false rows team name rule rules hooks guard

    mkdir -p "${log_file%/*}"
    # The command substitution runs in a subshell, so a read error exits it and
    # is turned into this function's exit here.
    hooks="$(agmsg_hooks_or_fail "${claude_hooks_file}" before)" || exit 1
    if [[ ${hooks} == present ]]; then
        acted=true
        if [[ ! -f ${delivery} ]]; then
            printf 'agmsg delivery script not found; skipping hook removal: %s\n' "${delivery}" >&2
        else
            "${delivery}" set off claude-code "${workdir}" >> "${log_file}" 2>&1 || true
            hooks="$(agmsg_hooks_or_fail "${claude_hooks_file}" after)" || exit 1
            if [[ ${hooks} == present ]]; then
                printf 'herdr-agents: agmsg hooks remain in %s after delivery.sh set off claude-code %s (log: %s)\n' \
                    "${claude_hooks_file}" "${workdir}" "${log_file}" >&2
                exit 1
            fi
            printf 'agmsg retired: removed the agmsg hooks from %s\n' "${claude_hooks_file}"
            if ! rules="$(jq -r '.permissions.allow[]? | select(contains("agmsg/scripts/"))' "${claude_hooks_file}" 2> /dev/null)"; then
                printf 'herdr-agents: cannot read the allow rules of %s after delivery.sh set off\n' "${claude_hooks_file}" >&2
                exit 1
            fi
            while IFS= read -r rule; do
                [[ -z ${rule} ]] || printf 'agmsg retired: %s keeps the allow rule %s (delivery.sh set off leaves permissions alone)\n' "${claude_hooks_file}" "${rule}"
            done <<< "${rules}"
        fi
    elif [[ ${report_skips} == --report-skips ]]; then
        acted=true
        printf 'agmsg retire: no agmsg hook in %s (missing or none); hook removal skipped\n' "${claude_hooks_file}"
    fi

    # A failed or missing lookup is not "no identity": never claim retired then.
    rows=""
    if [[ ! -x ${scripts}/identities.sh ]]; then
        acted=true
        printf 'agmsg identities script not found; skipping team leave: %s\n' "${scripts}/identities.sh" >&2
    elif ! rows="$(AGMSG_RESOLVE_PROJECT=0 "${scripts}/identities.sh" "${workdir}" claude-code 2>> "${log_file}")"; then
        printf 'herdr-agents: identities.sh %s claude-code failed, so its agmsg identities are unknown (log: %s)\n' \
            "${workdir}" "${log_file}" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    rows="$(sort -u <<< "${rows}")"
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r team name; do
        [[ -n ${team} && -n ${name} ]] || continue
        acted=true
        if [[ ! -f ${teams_dir}/${team}/config.json ]]; then
            printf 'agmsg retire: team %s of %s no longer exists; skipped\n' "${team}" "${name}"
            continue
        fi
        if [[ ${registered} == true ]]; then
            guard=0
            other="$(agmsg_member_other_project "${teams_dir}/${team}/config.json" "${name}" "${workdir}" "${identity}")" || guard=$?
            case "${guard}" in
            0)
                printf 'agmsg retire: %s in team %s is also registered at %s; membership kept\n' "${name}" "${team}" "${other}"
                continue
                ;;
            1) ;;
            *)
                printf 'herdr-agents: cannot read the registrations of %s in %s, so what leave.sh would remove is unknown; nothing left (log: %s)\n' \
                    "${name}" "${teams_dir}/${team}/config.json" "${log_file}" >&2
                exit 1
                ;;
            esac
        fi
        if [[ ! -x ${scripts}/leave.sh ]]; then
            printf 'agmsg leave script not found; skipping team leave for %s: %s\n' "${name}" "${scripts}/leave.sh" >&2
            continue
        fi
        if ! "${scripts}/leave.sh" "${team}" "${name}" >> "${log_file}" 2>&1; then
            printf 'herdr-agents: leave.sh %s %s failed (log: %s)\n' "${team}" "${name}" "${log_file}" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
        printf 'agmsg retired: %s left team %s\n' "${name}" "${team}"
    done <<< "${rows}"

    [[ ${acted} == true ]] || printf 'agmsg already retired for %s\n' "${workdir}"
}

# @description Print the first registration of a team member, of any agmsg
#   type, that lies outside this repository, since leave.sh removes the whole
#   member whatever the type (leave.sh:85-93) and join.sh keeps one registration
#   per type/project pair (join.sh:211-228). Outside means a directory other
#   than DIR whose repository_identity differs from <identity>, or a project
#   that cannot be checked (absent, not a string, gone, or holding a newline).
#   The registrations are read from the team config as JSON, so a tab in a path
#   survives, and the read is checked: a failure is never "nothing outside".
# @arg $1 path Team config.json.
# @arg $2 string Member name.
# @arg $3 path DIR, the project being retired.
# @arg $4 string This repository's identity (empty when it has none).
# @exitcode 0 When such a registration exists (its project printed on stdout).
# @exitcode 1 When every registration is DIR or a clone of this repository.
# @exitcode 2 When the member's registrations cannot be read.
function agmsg_member_other_project() {
    local config="$1" name="$2" project="$3" identity="$4" rows row other other_identity
    local log_file="${HOME}/.config/herdr/herdr-agents.log"
    local -a registrations=()

    # An absent member is a read failure: identities.sh just named it here.
    rows="$(jq -c --arg n "${name}" '.agents[$n] // error("member \($n) is not in the team config")
        | if (.registrations | type) == "array" then .registrations[] else {type, project} end
        | {type: (.type // null), project: (.project // null)}' "${config}" 2>> "${log_file}")" || return 2
    while IFS= read -r row; do
        [[ -n ${row} ]] && registrations+=("${row}")
    done <<< "${rows}"
    for row in ${registrations[@]+"${registrations[@]}"}; do
        other="$(jq -r 'if (.project | type) == "string" then .project else "" end' <<< "${row}")" || return 2
        if [[ -z ${other} ]]; then
            # No project to check: what leave.sh would drop is not provably ours.
            printf '%s\n' "${row}"
            return 0
        fi
        if [[ ${other} != *$'\n'* && -d ${other} ]]; then
            # The same directory (by device and inode), whatever path spells it.
            [[ ! ${other} -ef ${project} ]] || continue
            if [[ -n ${identity} ]]; then
                other_identity="$(repository_identity "${other}")" || return 2
                [[ ${other_identity} != "${identity}" ]] || continue
            fi
        fi
        printf '%s\n' "${other}"
        return 0
    done
    return 1
}

# @description List every claude-code registration the local agmsg team store
#   holds as one compact JSON object per line, `{"project":…,"team":…}`. JSON
#   keeps a path lossless: agmsg accepts a tab in a path (delivery.sh:12-17),
#   and jq -c escapes it, and a newline, inside the line. It reads each
#   teams/<team>/config.json with the schema identities.sh reads
#   (identities.sh:31-58, team.sh:265-285: `.agents.<name>.registrations[]`,
#   or the legacy `.type`/`.project` pair); the team name is the config's
#   directory, as leave.sh resolves it. team.sh is not used: it probes delivery
#   state and panes per member.
# @exitcode 1 When a team config exists but cannot be read as JSON.
function registered_agmsg_projects() {
    local teams_dir="${HOME}/.agents/skills/agmsg/teams" config team

    [[ -d ${teams_dir} ]] || return 0
    for config in "${teams_dir}"/*/config.json; do
        [[ -f ${config} ]] || continue
        # The glob ends in /config.json, so the team is the directory above it.
        team="${config%/config.json}"
        team="${team##*/}"
        if ! jq -c --arg team "${team}" '.agents // {} | to_entries[] | .value
            | (if (.registrations | type) == "array" then .registrations else [{type: .type, project: .project}] end)[]
            | select(.type == "claude-code" and (.project | type) == "string" and .project != "") | {project, team: $team}' "${config}" 2> /dev/null; then
            printf 'herdr-agents: cannot read %s as JSON, so its registered agmsg projects are unknown\n' "${config}" >&2
            return 1
        fi
    done
}

# @description Print a checkout's repository identity on one line: its root
#   commits and the host/owner/repo its origin fetch URL names, so two clones
#   match whatever their URL spelling (https or ssh, with or without .git) and a
#   fork, which shares the root but not the remote, does not (D-024-147).
#   Prints nothing for a checkout without commits or an origin.
#   shortcut: a shallow clone reports its shallow boundary, not the root, so it
#   counts as another repository; upgrade to an explicit project list if a
#   shallow agmsg project appears.
# @arg $1 dir Directory.
function repository_identity() {
    local roots url

    roots="$(git -C "$1" rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD 2> /dev/null | sort | tr '\n' ' ')" || roots=""
    url="$(git -C "$1" config --get remote.origin.url 2> /dev/null)" || url=""
    [[ -n ${roots} && -n ${url} ]] || return 0
    # https://host/owner/repo(.git) and git@host:owner/repo(.git) -> host/owner/repo
    if ! url="$(sed -E -e 's#^[a-z+]+://([^@/]*@)?##' -e 's#^[^@/]*@([^:/]+):#\1/#' -e 's#/+$##' -e 's#\.git$##' <<< "${url}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"; then
        printf 'herdr-agents: cannot normalize the origin URL of %s\n' "$1" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    printf '%s| %s\n' "${roots}" "${url}"
}

# @description Retire agmsg in every project the team store registers that is
#   a clone of the repository in DIR (repository_identity, D-024-147), then in DIR
#   itself. A registered project of another repository, one whose directory is
#   gone, or one whose path holds a newline (agmsg refuses those,
#   delivery.sh:12-17) is reported with its team and left alone: no delivery.sh
#   or leave.sh call. A member also registered at a project outside this
#   repository keeps its membership (retire_agmsg --registered). Paths travel as
#   JSON from the store to each call, never cut at a tab.
# @arg $1 clone Absolute path of the clone this runs in.
# @exitcode 1 As retire_agmsg, or when a team config cannot be read.
function retire_registered_agmsg_projects() {
    local clone="$1" registrations grouped row project project_identity team identity
    local -a rows=()

    registrations="$(registered_agmsg_projects)" || exit 1
    identity="$(repository_identity "${clone}")" || exit 1
    # One visit per project, its teams joined; collected first so no command
    # below reads the list as its stdin.
    if ! grouped="$(jq -sc 'group_by(.project)[] | {project: .[0].project, teams: (map(.team) | unique | join(","))}' <<< "${registrations}")"; then
        printf 'herdr-agents: cannot group the registered agmsg projects by project\n' >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    while IFS= read -r row; do
        [[ -n ${row} ]] && rows+=("${row}")
    done <<< "${grouped}"
    for row in ${rows[@]+"${rows[@]}"}; do
        project="$(jq -r '.project' <<< "${row}")"
        team="$(jq -r '.teams' <<< "${row}")"
        if [[ ${project} == *$'\n'* ]]; then
            printf 'agmsg retire: registered project %q (team %s) holds a newline; skipped\n' "${project}" "${team}"
            continue
        fi
        if [[ ! -d ${project} ]]; then
            printf 'agmsg retire: registered project %s (team %s) is gone; skipped\n' "${project}" "${team}"
            continue
        fi
        # The same directory (by device and inode), whatever path spells it.
        [[ ! ${project} -ef ${clone} ]] || continue
        project_identity=""
        if [[ -n ${identity} ]]; then
            project_identity="$(repository_identity "${project}")" || exit 1
        fi
        if [[ -z ${identity} || ${project_identity} != "${identity}" ]]; then
            printf 'agmsg retire: registered project %s (team %s) is not a clone of this repository; skipped\n' "${project}" "${team}"
            continue
        fi
        printf 'agmsg retire: registered project %s (team %s)\n' "${project}" "${team}"
        retire_agmsg "${project}" --registered "${identity}" --report-skips
    done
    retire_agmsg "${clone}" --registered "${identity}"
}

# @description Require a command before starting a partial layout.
# @arg $1 string Command name.
function require_command() {
    local command_name="$1"

    if ! command -v "${command_name}" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        printf '%s command not found\n' "${command_name}" >&2
        exit 127
    fi
}

if [[ ${1:-} == "--help" || ${1:-} == "-h" ]]; then
    usage
    exit 0
fi

if [[ ${1:-} != "--retire-agmsg" || $# -gt 2 ]]; then
    usage >&2
    exit 2
fi
shift

require_command jq
if [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; then
    cd -- "$1"
fi
if ! here="$(pwd -P)"; then
    printf 'herdr-agents: cannot resolve the current directory to a physical path\n' >&2
    exit 1
fi
if [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; then
    retire_agmsg "${here}"
else
    require_command git
    retire_registered_agmsg_projects "${here}"
fi
exit 0
</code></pre>

#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --no-cache --script
"""Deterministic permission gate for Claude Code and Codex."""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import shlex
import sys
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any


SENTINEL_ENV = "PERMGATE_INNER"
SHELL_CONTROL = re.compile(r"[;&|><`\n]|\$\(")
SHELL_EXPANSION = re.compile(r"[$*?\[\]{}~]")
UNSAFE_READ_OPTIONS = {
    "--ext-diff",
    "--hostname-bin",
    "--no-index",
    "--open-files-in-pager",
    "--output",
    "--pre",
    "--textconv",
    "--watch",
    "--web",
    "-O",
    "-w",
}
SUMMARY_COMMANDS = {
    "ccgate",
    "chezmoi",
    "claude",
    "codex",
    "crit",
    "gh",
    "git",
    "herdr",
    "jq",
    "make",
    "mise",
    "npm",
    "node",
    "pgrep",
    "pnpm",
    "ps",
    "python3",
    "rg",
    "sysctl",
    "uv",
}


def policy_path() -> Path:
    override = os.environ.get("PERMGATE_POLICY_PATH")
    return Path(override) if override else Path.home() / ".agents/permgate-policy.yaml"


def state_path() -> Path:
    override = os.environ.get("PERMGATE_STATE_PATH")
    if override:
        return Path(override)
    state_home = Path(os.environ.get("XDG_STATE_HOME", Path.home() / ".local/state"))
    return state_home / "permgate/decisions.jsonl"


def load_policy() -> dict[str, Any]:
    policy = json.loads(policy_path().read_text())
    if not isinstance(policy, dict) or policy.get("schema_version") != 3:
        raise ValueError("unsupported policy schema")
    return policy


def request_parts(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any], str]:
    tool = payload.get("tool_name")
    tool = tool if isinstance(tool, str) else "unknown"
    tool_input = payload.get("tool_input")
    tool_input = tool_input if isinstance(tool_input, dict) else {}
    command = tool_input.get("command")
    match_text = (
        command
        if isinstance(command, str)
        else json.dumps(tool_input, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
    )
    return tool, tool_input, match_text


def input_summary(tool: str, tool_input: dict[str, Any], match_text: str) -> str:
    if tool != "Bash":
        return f"{tool}:structured"[:160]
    first = re.match(r"\s*([^\s;&|><]+)", match_text)
    operation = Path(first.group(1)).name if first else "other"
    if operation not in SUMMARY_COMMANDS:
        operation = "other"
    return f"{tool}:{operation}"[:160]


def pattern_match(pattern: dict[str, Any], tool: str, text: str) -> bool:
    return pattern.get("tool") == tool and bool(
        re.fullmatch(str(pattern.get("regex", r"(?!x)x")), text)
    )


def has_unsafe_read_option(command: str) -> bool:
    try:
        parts = shlex.split(command)
    except ValueError:
        return True
    return any(
        token.split("=", 1)[0] in UNSAFE_READ_OPTIONS for token in parts[1:]
    )


def is_bounded_shell_command(command: str) -> bool:
    return not (
        SHELL_CONTROL.search(command)
        or SHELL_EXPANSION.search(command)
        or has_unsafe_read_option(command)
    )


def hook_output(behavior: str, message: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    decision = {"behavior": behavior}
    if message is not None:
        decision["message"] = message
    return {
        "hookSpecificOutput": {
            "hookEventName": "PermissionRequest",
            "decision": decision,
        }
    }


def append_log(record: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    path = state_path()
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    line = (json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n").encode()
    descriptor = os.open(path, os.O_APPEND | os.O_CREAT | os.O_WRONLY, 0o600)
    try:
        os.write(descriptor, line)
    finally:
        os.close(descriptor)


def decision_record(
    agent: str,
    payload: dict[str, Any],
    layer: str,
    decision: str,
    latency_ms: int,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    tool, tool_input, match_text = request_parts(payload)
    return {
        "ts": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "agent": agent,
        "tool": tool,
        "input_hash": hashlib.sha256(
            json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
        ).hexdigest(),
        "input_summary": input_summary(tool, tool_input, match_text),
        "layer": layer,
        "decision": decision,
        "latency_ms": latency_ms,
    }


def decide(
    agent: str, payload: dict[str, Any], policy: dict[str, Any]
) -> tuple[dict[str, Any] | None, dict[str, Any]]:
    started = time.monotonic()
    tool, _, match_text = request_parts(payload)
    layer = "fallthrough"
    decision = "ask"
    output: dict[str, Any] | None = None

    for pattern in policy.get("deny_patterns", []):
        if pattern_match(pattern, tool, match_text):
            layer = "deterministic"
            decision = "deny"
            output = hook_output("deny", str(pattern["message"]))
            break
    else:
        if tool != "Bash" or is_bounded_shell_command(match_text):
            for pattern in policy.get("allow_patterns", []):
                if pattern_match(pattern, tool, match_text):
                    layer = "deterministic"
                    decision = "allow"
                    output = hook_output("allow")
                    break

    latency_ms = round((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000)
    return output, decision_record(agent, payload, layer, decision, latency_ms)


def main() -> int:
    if os.environ.get(SENTINEL_ENV):
        return 0
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        return 0
    agent = sys.argv[1]
    if agent not in {"claude", "codex"}:
        return 0
    raw_input = sys.stdin.read()
    try:
        payload = json.loads(raw_input)
        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
            raise ValueError("hook input must be an object")
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
        try:
            append_log(
                {
                    "ts": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
                    "agent": agent,
                    "tool": "unknown",
                    "input_hash": hashlib.sha256(raw_input.encode()).hexdigest(),
                    "input_summary": "unknown:invalid-json",
                    "layer": "input-error",
                    "decision": "ask",
                    "latency_ms": 0,
                }
            )
        except OSError:
            pass
        return 0
    try:
        policy = load_policy()
    except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        try:
            append_log(decision_record(agent, payload, "config-error", "ask", 0))
        except OSError:
            pass
        return 0
    try:
        output, record = decide(agent, payload, policy)
    except (AttributeError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError, re.error):
        output = None
        record = decision_record(agent, payload, "config-error", "ask", 0)
    try:
        append_log(record)
    except OSError:
        return 0
    if output is not None:
        print(json.dumps(output, separators=(",", ":")))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file pr-body-edit.sh
# @brief Replace the body of the open pull request of the current branch, the worker seat's lever.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U28, the worker seat's lever, allowed only in the form
#   `~/.local/bin/common/pr-body-edit.sh --body-file *` by `home/dot_agents/omp/policies/worker.yml`
#   (scripts/orchestrator/README.md, "Seat levers for GitHub writes"); the orchestrator's policy denies it. It
#   edits only the pull request of the branch the seat has checked out: `git branch --show-current` must name a
#   branch other than `main`, and `gh pr view --json number,headRefName,state` (the pull request of that branch)
#   must report it as `headRefName` and `OPEN`. The body file is a regular file (not a symlink) of 1 to 65536
#   bytes whose real path is inside `$TMPDIR` or the checkout. The new body must hold exactly one line starting
#   `Program-Unit:`, and it must be `Program-Unit: regime-cutover/U<n>`, the plain unit id `regime-ci.py` reads
#   (a fix round writes its parent id, `preferences.md` standing order 24); when the current body already
#   carries one such line, the unit must stay the same, so an edit fixes the line or the text but never moves a
#   pull request to another unit. Every `## ` heading line and the `Generated with [Claude Code]` footer line of
#   the current body must still be in the new body, so sections are added or rewritten, never dropped. The one
#   write is `gh pr edit <n> --body-file <file>`. Each `gh` call is bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds (perl
#   `alarm`).
# @option --body-file <file> The new body.
# @env PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT Seconds per `gh` call (default 60).
# @stdout One receipt line: `edited pr=<n> branch=<b> unit=U<n> sha256=<body sha256>`.
# @exitcode 0 The body was replaced.
# @exitcode 1 A `git` or `gh` read, or the edit, failed.
# @exitcode 2 Refused: usage, the branch, the pull request's state, the body file, or the body's content.
# @example
#   ~/.local/bin/common/pr-body-edit.sh --body-file "$TMPDIR/body.md"
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

lever='pr-body-edit.sh'
usage='usage: pr-body-edit.sh --body-file <file>'
gh_timeout=${PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT:-60}
unit_line='^Program-Unit: regime-cutover/U[0-9]+$'
footer_re='Generated with \[Claude Code\]\(https://claude\.com/claude-code\)'

# @description Print the refusal on stderr and exit 2; nothing was written to GitHub.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
refuse() {
    echo "${lever}: refused: $*" >&2
    exit 2
}

# @description Print the failure on stderr and exit 1: a read or the write failed.

view=$(gh_bounded pr view --json number,headRefName,state --jq '[(.number | tostring), .headRefName, .state] | @tsv') ||
    fail "cannot read the pull request of ${branch}"

[[ ${head} == "${branch}" ]] || refuse "pull request ${number} is the pull request of ${head}, not of the current branch ${branch}"

current=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/pr-body-edit.XXXXXX") || fail 'mktemp failed'
trap 'rm -f "${current}"' EXIT
gh_bounded pr view "${number}" --json body --jq .body > "${current}" || fail "cannot read the body of pull request ${number}"
old_markers=$(lines_matching "${unit_line}" "${current}") || fail "cannot read ${current}"
if [[ -n ${old_markers} && ${old_markers} != *$'\n'* && ${old_markers##*/} != "${unit}" ]]; then
    refuse "the current body names ${old_markers##*/}; an edit keeps the unit (the new body names ${unit})"
fi
kept=$(lines_matching "^## |${footer_re}" "${current}") || fail "cannot read ${current}"
new_lines=$(lines_matching '' "${body_path}") || refuse "cannot read ${body_path}"
while IFS= read -r line; do
    [[ -n ${line} ]] || continue
    grep -Fxq -- "${line}" <<< "${new_lines}" || refuse "the new body drops the line of the current body: ${line}"

gh_bounded pr edit "${number}" --body-file "${body_path}" >&2 || fail "gh pr edit ${number} failed"
if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
    digest=$(sha256sum < "${body_path}") || digest=''
else
    digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${body_path}") || digest=''
fi
echo "edited pr=${number} branch=${branch} unit=${unit} sha256=${digest%% *}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file pr-close.sh
# @brief Close the pull requests a clean-up table marks `close:`, with the row's text as the comment.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U28, a lever of the omp orchestrator seat, allowed only in the form
#   `~/.local/bin/common/pr-close.sh --from-table *` by `home/dot_agents/omp/policies/orchestrator.yml`
#   (scripts/orchestrator/README.md, "Seat levers for GitHub writes"). The table is a table the orchestrator
#   wrote: a regular file (not a symlink) whose real path is under
#   `<toplevel>/.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>/handouts/` of the main checkout, where the orchestrator seat
#   runs (a linked worktree, a worker's clone, is refused). The lever reads its `## Open pull requests` section,
#   whose header row must be `| PR | branch | opened | files | title | default |`; every row must carry a `#<n>`
#   PR cell and a backticked branch cell, else the whole table is refused before any `gh` call. The selected rows
#   are those whose `default` cell starts with `close:`; `--only <pr>` narrows them to that one row and is refused
#   when the table has no such `close:` row. Then, per row, read-only: `gh pr view <n>` must report `OPEN` and the
#   table's branch as `headRefName`, and `gh pr list --state open --head <branch>` must list no other pull
#   request (#396 and #412 share `tools/anthropic-auth-route-structured`); a row failing that is refused with its
#   own line. A failed `gh` read aborts the run before any close. Only then does each remaining row get
#   `gh pr close <n> --comment <default cell>`. The lever never passes `--delete-branch` (closing one of two pull
#   requests on a shared branch that way would close the other) and never deletes a branch. Each `gh` call is
#   bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds (perl `alarm`).
# @option --from-table <file> The clean-up table.
# @option --only <pr> Close only this row.
# @env PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT Seconds per `gh` call (default 60).
# @stdout One line per selected row, `closed pr=<n> branch=<b>` or `refused pr=<n> reason=<why>`, then
#   `summary closed=<n> refused=<n>`.
# @exitcode 0 Every selected row was closed.
# @exitcode 1 A `gh` read failed (nothing was closed) or a close failed (the lines say which were closed).
# @exitcode 2 Refused: usage, the table's path or shape, no selected row, or at least one row refused (its line
#   says why; the other rows were closed).
# @example
#   ~/.local/bin/common/pr-close.sh --from-table .orchestration/orchestrate/regime-cutover/handouts/cleanup-table.md
#   ~/.local/bin/common/pr-close.sh --from-table .orchestration/orchestrate/regime-cutover/handouts/cleanup-table.md --only 378
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac

    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }

        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }

    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi

        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}

lever='pr-close.sh'
usage='usage: pr-close.sh --from-table <table.md> [--only <pr>]'
gh_timeout=${PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT:-60}
header='| PR | branch | opened | files | title | default |'
# The `## Open pull requests` rows as `<pr>\t<branch>\t<default>`; exit 3 for a missing section or header, 4 for a
# row without a `#<n>` PR cell or a backticked branch cell. `\|` inside a cell is text, not a separator.
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # awk source, not shell
table_awk='
function trim(s) { sub(/^[ \t]+/, "", s); sub(/[ \t]+$/, "", s); return s }
/^## / { if (in_section) { done = 1 } in_section = ($0 == "## Open pull requests"); next }
!in_section || done { next }
/^[ \t]*$/ { if (rows) { done = 1 } next }
!seen_header { if ($0 != header) { exit 3 } seen_header = 1; next }
/^\|( *:?-+:? *\|)+ *$/ { next }

    line = $0
    gsub(/\\\|/, "\001", line)
    n = split(line, cell, "|")

    pr = trim(cell[2]); branch = trim(cell[3]); text = trim(cell[7])
    gsub(/\001/, "|", text); gsub(/\t/, " ", text)
    if (pr !~ /^#[1-9][0-9]*$/ || branch !~ /^`[A-Za-z0-9._\/-]+`$/) { exit 4 }
    rows++
    print substr(pr, 2) "\t" substr(branch, 2, length(branch) - 2) "\t" text
}
END { if (!seen_header) { exit 3 } }
'

# @description Print the refusal on stderr and exit 2; nothing was written to GitHub.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
refuse() {
    echo "${lever}: refused: $*" >&2
    exit 2
}

# @description Print the failure on stderr and exit 1.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
fail() {
    echo "${lever}: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

# @description Run `gh` with its wait bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds.
# @arg $@ string The `gh` arguments.
gh_bounded() {
    perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV or die "exec gh: $!\n"' "${gh_timeout}" gh "$@"
}

table=''
only=''
while (($#)); do
    case $1 in
    --from-table)
        (($# >= 2)) || refuse "${usage}"
        table=$2
        shift 2
        ;;
    --only)
        (($# >= 2)) || refuse "${usage}"
        only=$2
        shift 2
        ;;
    *) refuse "${usage}" ;;
    esac
done
[[ -n ${table} ]] || refuse "${usage}"
[[ -z ${only} || ${only} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,9}$ ]] || refuse "--only is not a decimal number: ${only}"
[[ ${gh_timeout} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || refuse 'PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT must be a positive integer'

toplevel=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2> /dev/null) || refuse 'not in a git checkout'
toplevel=$(cd "${toplevel}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${toplevel}"
git_dir=$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir) || refuse 'cannot read the git directory'
common_dir=$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir) || refuse 'cannot read the git common directory'
git_dir=$(cd "${git_dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${git_dir}"
common_dir=$(cd "${common_dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${common_dir}"
[[ ${git_dir} == "${common_dir}" ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
    refuse "${toplevel} is a linked worktree; run from the main checkout, where the orchestrator writes its tables"
[[ -f ${table} && ! -L ${table} ]] || refuse "the table is not a regular file: ${table}"
case ${table} in
*/*) table_dir=${table%/*} ;;
*) table_dir=. ;;
esac
[[ -n ${table_dir} ]] || table_dir=/
table_dir=$(cd "${table_dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve the directory of ${table}"
handouts='^/.+/\.orchestration/orchestrate/[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*/handouts$'
[[ ${table_dir} =~ ${handouts} && ${table_dir} == "${toplevel}/.orchestration/orchestrate/"* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
    refuse "the table is not under ${toplevel}/.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>/handouts/: ${table_dir}"

0) ;;
3) refuse "no '## Open pull requests' section with the header ${header} in ${table}" ;;
4) refuse "a row of '## Open pull requests' in ${table} has no #<n> PR cell or backticked branch cell" ;;

    refuse "the table has no row whose default starts with close:"
fi

refused=0

        refused=$((refused + 1))
        continue
    fi
    if [[ ${head} != "${branch}" ]]; then
        echo "refused pr=${pr} reason=head branch ${head} is not the table's ${branch}"
        refused=$((refused + 1))
        continue
    fi
    sharing=$(gh_bounded pr list --state open --head "${branch}" --json number --jq '[.[].number | tostring] | join(",")') ||
        fail "cannot list the open pull requests of ${branch}; nothing was closed"

        echo "refused pr=${pr} reason=branch ${branch} is the head of open pull requests ${sharing:-none}"
        refused=$((refused + 1))
        continue
    fi
    closable+=("${row}")
done

closed=0
for row in ${closable[@]+"${closable[@]}"}; do
    IFS=$'\t' read -r pr branch text <<< "${row}"
    gh_bounded pr close "${pr}" --comment "${text}" >&2 || {
        echo "summary closed=${closed} refused=${refused}"
        fail "gh pr close ${pr} failed after ${closed} closed"
    }
    echo "closed pr=${pr} branch=${branch}"
    closed=$((closed + 1))
done

# @description Refuse unless $1 is a regular file of 1 to 65536 bytes inside $TMPDIR or <toplevel>/.orchestration.
# @arg $1 path The body file.

    local file=$1 dir root size
    [[ -f ${file} && ! -L ${file} ]] || refuse "the body file is not a regular file: ${file}"
    case ${file} in # lint-comparisons: allow splits the argument at its last slash; the real path is compared below
    */*) dir=${file%/*} ;;

comment=$2

[[ ${reply_to} == 0 ]] || refuse "review comment ${comment} is a reply (to ${reply_to}); name the thread's first comment"

posted=$(gh_bounded api -X POST "repos/${repo}/pulls/${pr}/comments/${comment}/replies" -F "body=@${body_path}" \
    --jq '[(.id | tostring), .html_url] | @tsv') || fail "the reply to ${comment} on pull request ${pr} failed"
IFS=$'\t' read -r reply url <<< "${posted}"
echo "replied pr=${pr} comment=${comment} reply=${reply} url=${url}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file pr-thread-resolve.sh
# @brief Resolve one review thread of a pull request after its disposition reply, the orchestrator seat's lever.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U28, a lever of the omp orchestrator seat, allowed by the row
#   `~/.local/bin/common/pr-thread-resolve.sh *` of `home/dot_agents/omp/policies/orchestrator.yml`
#   (scripts/orchestrator/README.md, "Seat levers for GitHub writes"). `<pr>` and `<comment-id>` are decimal and
#   checked before the first `gh` call. The thread is the one whose first comment's `databaseId` is `<comment-id>`
#   among the pull request's `reviewThreads` (GraphQL, read-only); the lever refuses when no thread has it, when
#   the thread is already resolved, and when the listing has more than 100 threads or a thread more than 100
#   comments (a page it did not read). The thread's newest reply must hold a disposition that is valid by the rule
#   `pr-threads-check.sh` applies before a merge (U28b F1; the function `disposition` is the same in both files):
#   `fixed: <sha>` names a commit of this checkout that is the pull request's head or an ancestor of it and was
#   committed after the thread's first comment; `refuted:` cites a URL or a `file:line`; `residual: unit=U<n>`
#   answers a P2 or P3 finding and `units.tsv` in `--records` has the row; `residual: operator=<ts>` has its
#   `decisions.tsv` row in `--records`. So a resolution never hides a finding the merge check would refuse. The
#   one write is the `resolveReviewThread` mutation on that thread id. `<owner>/<repo>` comes from
#   `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner`. Each `gh` call is bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds (perl `alarm`).
# @arg $1 int The pull request number.
# @arg $2 int The id of the thread's first review comment.
# @option --records <dir> The program's records directory, holding `units.tsv` and `decisions.tsv`.
# @env PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT Seconds per `gh` call (default 60).
# @stdout One receipt line: `resolved pr=<pr> comment=<id> thread=<node id> disposition=<disposition>`.
# @exitcode 0 The thread was resolved.
# @exitcode 1 A `gh` or `git` read or the mutation failed, or the mutation did not report the thread resolved.
# @exitcode 2 Refused: usage, no such thread, already resolved, no valid disposition, or an unread page.
# @example
#   ~/.local/bin/common/pr-thread-resolve.sh 480 4365170609 --records .orchestration/orchestrate/regime-cutover
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

lever='pr-thread-resolve.sh'
usage='usage: pr-thread-resolve.sh <pr> <comment-id> [--records <dir>]'
gh_timeout=${PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT:-60}
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # GraphQL variables, not shell
threads_query='query($owner: String!, $name: String!, $pr: Int!) {
  repository(owner: $owner, name: $name) {
    pullRequest(number: $pr) {
      headRefOid
      reviewThreads(first: 100) {
        pageInfo { hasNextPage }
        nodes { id isResolved comments(first: 100) { totalCount nodes { databaseId createdAt body } } }
      }
    }
  }
}'
# `head <sha> <hasNextPage>`, then per thread `<node id> <resolved> <first id> <created epoch> <P0-P3 or -> <count>
# <newest reply's first line>` (TSV; the reply is last because it may be empty).
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # jq source, not shell
threads_jq='.data.repository.pullRequest
  | (["head", .headRefOid, (.reviewThreads.pageInfo.hasNextPage | tostring)] | @tsv),
    (.reviewThreads.nodes[] | .comments as $c | [.id, (.isResolved | tostring),
      ($c.nodes[0].databaseId | tostring), ($c.nodes[0].createdAt | fromdateiso8601 | tostring),
      ([($c.nodes[0].body // "") | capture("!\\[P(?<p>[0-3]) Badge\\]") | "P" + .p] | first // "-"),
      ($c.totalCount | tostring),
      (($c.nodes[1:] | last | .body // "") | split("\n") | (.[0] // "") | rtrimstr("\r"))] | @tsv)'
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # GraphQL variables, not shell
resolve_mutation='mutation($thread: ID!) { resolveReviewThread(input: {threadId: $thread}) { thread { id isResolved } } }'

# @description Print the refusal on stderr and exit 2; nothing was written to GitHub.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
refuse() {
    echo "${lever}: refused: $*" >&2
    exit 2
}

# @description Print the failure on stderr and exit 1: a read or the write failed.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
fail() {
    echo "${lever}: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

# @description Run `gh` with its wait bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds.
# @arg $@ string The `gh` arguments.
gh_bounded() {
    perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV or die "exec gh: $!\n"' "${gh_timeout}" gh "$@"
}

# @description Succeed when the TSV file $1 has a row whose first field is $2.
# @arg $1 path The file.
# @arg $2 string The key.
# @exitcode 0 Found. 1 Not found. 2 Unreadable.
has_row() {
    [[ -r $1 ]] || return 2
    ROW_KEY=$2 awk -F '\t' '$1 == ENVIRON["ROW_KEY"] { found = 1 } END { exit !found }' "$1" || return 1
}

# @description Print the disposition a thread's newest reply carries, or `open (<why>)`.
# @arg $1 int The created epoch of the thread's first comment.
# @arg $2 string Its severity, P0-P3 or `-`.
# @arg $3 string The first line of the newest reply.
disposition() {
    local created=$1 severity=$2 line=$3 fix fix_time status
    local fixed='^fixed: ([0-9a-f]{40})( |$)'
    local refuted='^refuted: .*(https://[^[:space:]]+|[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)*:[0-9]+)'
    local unit='^residual: unit=(U[0-9]+[a-z]?) gate=[^[:space:]]'
    local operator='^residual: operator=([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z)$'
    if [[ ${line} =~ ${fixed} ]]; then
        fix=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
        git cat-file -e "${fix}^{commit}" 2> /dev/null || {
            echo "open (fixed: ${fix} is not a commit here)"
            return
        }
        status=0
        git merge-base --is-ancestor "${fix}" "${head}" || status=$?
        case ${status} in
        0) ;;
        1)
            echo "open (fixed: ${fix} is not in the head)"
            return
            ;;
        *) fail "git merge-base --is-ancestor ${fix} ${head} failed" ;;
        esac
        fix_time=$(git show -s --format=%ct "${fix}") || fail "git show ${fix} failed"
        if ((fix_time < created)); then
            echo "open (fixed: ${fix} predates the finding)"
            return
        fi
        echo "fixed ${fix}"
    elif [[ ${line} =~ ${refuted} ]]; then
        echo refuted
    elif [[ ${line} =~ ${unit} ]]; then
        fix=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
        [[ ${severity} == P2 || ${severity} == P3 ]] || {
            echo "open (residual: unit= is for P2 and P3; this is ${severity/-/P1 (no badge)})"
            return
        }
        [[ -n ${records} ]] || refuse "a residual needs --records to check units.tsv"
        status=0
        has_row "${records}/units.tsv" "${fix}" || status=$?
        case ${status} in
        0) echo "residual ${fix}" ;;
        1) echo "open (residual: no units.tsv row ${fix})" ;;
        *) fail "cannot read ${records}/units.tsv" ;;
        esac
    elif [[ ${line} =~ ${operator} ]]; then
        fix=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
        [[ -n ${records} ]] || refuse "a residual needs --records to check decisions.tsv"
        status=0
        has_row "${records}/decisions.tsv" "${fix}" || status=$?
        case ${status} in
        0) echo "residual operator=${fix}" ;;
        1) echo "open (residual: no decisions.tsv row at ${fix})" ;;
        *) fail "cannot read ${records}/decisions.tsv" ;;
        esac
    elif [[ -z ${line} ]]; then
        echo 'open (no reply)'
    else
        echo 'open (the newest reply is not a disposition)'
    fi
}

pr=''
comment=''
records=''
while (($#)); do
    case $1 in
    --records)
        (($# >= 2)) || refuse "${usage}"
        records=$2
        shift 2
        ;;
    -*) refuse "${usage}" ;;
    *)
        if [[ -z ${pr} ]]; then
            pr=$1
        elif [[ -z ${comment} ]]; then
            comment=$1
        else
            refuse "${usage}"
        fi
        shift
        ;;
    esac
done
[[ -n ${pr} && -n ${comment} ]] || refuse "${usage}"
[[ ${pr} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,9}$ ]] || refuse "the pull request is not a decimal number: ${pr}"
[[ ${comment} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,19}$ ]] || refuse "the comment id is not a decimal number: ${comment}"
[[ -z ${records} || (-f ${records}/units.tsv && -f ${records}/decisions.tsv) ]] ||
    refuse "--records holds no units.tsv and decisions.tsv: ${records}"
[[ ${gh_timeout} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || refuse 'PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT must be a positive integer'

repo=$(gh_bounded repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq .nameWithOwner) || fail 'gh repo view failed'
[[ ${repo} =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ ]] || fail "gh repo view printed no owner/repo: ${repo}"
listing=$(gh_bounded api graphql -f "query=${threads_query}" -f "owner=${repo%%/*}" -f "name=${repo#*/}" \
    -F "pr=${pr}" --jq "${threads_jq}") || fail "cannot list the review threads of pull request ${pr}"

head=''
page=''
thread=''
while IFS=$'\t' read -r id resolved first created severity count reply; do
    if [[ ${id} == head ]]; then
        head=${resolved}
        page=${first}
    elif [[ ${first} == "${comment}" ]]; then
        thread=${id}
        thread_resolved=${resolved}
        thread_created=${created}
        thread_severity=${severity}
        thread_count=${count}
        thread_reply=${reply}
    fi
done <<< "${listing}"
[[ ${head} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || fail "the listing of pull request ${pr} has no readable head"
[[ ${page} == false ]] || refuse "pull request ${pr} has more than 100 review threads; resolve it by hand"
[[ -n ${thread} ]] || refuse "no review thread of pull request ${pr} starts with comment ${comment}"
[[ ${thread_resolved} == false ]] || refuse "the thread of comment ${comment} is already resolved"
if ! [[ ${thread_count} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || ((thread_count > 100)); then
    refuse "the thread of comment ${comment} has more than 100 comments; resolve it by hand"
fi
[[ ${thread_created} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || fail "unreadable creation time for the thread of comment ${comment}"
git cat-file -e "${head}^{commit}" 2> /dev/null || refuse "the head ${head} of pull request ${pr} is not a commit here; git fetch first"
state=$(disposition "${thread_created}" "${thread_severity}" "${thread_reply}") || exit $?
[[ ${state} != open* ]] ||
    refuse "the thread of comment ${comment} has no valid disposition, ${state#open }; reply with pr-thread-reply.sh first"

done_id=$(gh_bounded api graphql -f "query=${resolve_mutation}" -f "thread=${thread}" \
    --jq '.data.resolveReviewThread.thread | select(.isResolved) | .id') || fail "resolveReviewThread failed for ${thread}"
[[ ${done_id} == "${thread}" ]] || fail "resolveReviewThread did not report ${thread} resolved"
echo "resolved pr=${pr} comment=${comment} thread=${thread} disposition=${state}"

#   a commit in this checkout (`git fetch` first). Every thread, resolved or not (GitHub's `isResolved` alone

#   `fixed: <sha>` when `<sha>` is `--head` or an ancestor of it and was committed after the thread's first
#   comment (so a thread opened after the head cannot be `fixed`); `refuted: <text>` citing a URL or a
#   `file:line`; `residual: unit=U<n> gate=<clause>` when the finding is P2 or P3 (the `![P<n> Badge]` of its
#   first comment; no badge counts as P1) and `units.tsv` in `--records` has the row `U<n>`; or

# @arg $1 int The pull request number.

# @option --records <dir> The program's records directory, holding `units.tsv` and `decisions.tsv`.
# @env PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT Seconds per `gh` call (default 60).

    pullRequest(number: $pr) {
      headRefOid
      reviewThreads(first: 100) {
        pageInfo { hasNextPage }
        nodes { isResolved comments(first: 100) { totalCount nodes { databaseId createdAt body } } }

threads_jq='.data.repository.pullRequest
  | (["head", .headRefOid, (.reviewThreads.pageInfo.hasNextPage | tostring)] | @tsv),

      ([($c.nodes[0].body // "") | capture("!\\[P(?<p>[0-3]) Badge\\]") | "P" + .p] | first // "-"),
      ($c.totalCount | tostring),
      (($c.nodes[1:] | last | .body // "") | split("\n") | (.[0] // "") | rtrimstr("\r"))] | @tsv)'

# @arg $@ string The reason.

    echo "${lever}: refused: $*" >&2
    exit 2
}

# @description Print the failure on stderr and exit 1: a read failed.
# @arg $@ string The reason.

    exit 1

# @description Run `gh` with its wait bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds.
# @arg $@ string The `gh` arguments.

# @description Succeed when the TSV file $1 has a row whose first field is $2.
# @arg $1 path The file.
# @arg $2 string The key.
# @exitcode 0 Found. 1 Not found. 2 Unreadable.

    [[ -r $1 ]] || return 2
    ROW_KEY=$2 awk -F '\t' '$1 == ENVIRON["ROW_KEY"] { found = 1 } END { exit !found }' "$1" || return 1

# @description Print the disposition a thread's newest reply carries, or `open (<why>)`.
# @arg $1 int The created epoch of the thread's first comment.
# @arg $2 string Its severity, P0-P3 or `-`.
# @arg $3 string The first line of the newest reply.
disposition() {
    local created=$1 severity=$2 line=$3 fix fix_time status
    local fixed='^fixed: ([0-9a-f]{40})( |$)'
    local refuted='^refuted: .*(https://[^[:space:]]+|[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)*:[0-9]+)'
    local unit='^residual: unit=(U[0-9]+[a-z]?) gate=[^[:space:]]'

        0) ;;

            return
            ;;
        *) fail "git merge-base --is-ancestor ${fix} ${head} failed" ;;
        esac
        fix_time=$(git show -s --format=%ct "${fix}") || fail "git show ${fix} failed"
        if ((fix_time < created)); then
            echo "open (fixed: ${fix} predates the finding)"
            return
        fi
        echo "fixed ${fix}"
    elif [[ ${line} =~ ${refuted} ]]; then
        echo refuted
    elif [[ ${line} =~ ${unit} ]]; then
        fix=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
        [[ ${severity} == P2 || ${severity} == P3 ]] || {
            echo "open (residual: unit= is for P2 and P3; this is ${severity/-/P1 (no badge)})"
            return
        }
        [[ -n ${records} ]] || refuse "a residual needs --records to check units.tsv"
        status=0
        has_row "${records}/units.tsv" "${fix}" || status=$?
        case ${status} in
        0) echo "residual ${fix}" ;;
        1) echo "open (residual: no units.tsv row ${fix})" ;;
        *) fail "cannot read ${records}/units.tsv" ;;
        esac
    elif [[ ${line} =~ ${operator} ]]; then
        fix=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
        [[ -n ${records} ]] || refuse "a residual needs --records to check decisions.tsv"
        status=0
        has_row "${records}/decisions.tsv" "${fix}" || status=$?
        case ${status} in
        0) echo "residual operator=${fix}" ;;
        1) echo "open (residual: no decisions.tsv row at ${fix})" ;;
        *) fail "cannot read ${records}/decisions.tsv" ;;
        esac
    elif [[ -z ${line} ]]; then
        echo 'open (no reply)'
    else
        echo 'open (the newest reply is not a disposition)'
    fi
}

pr=''
head=''
records=''
while (($#)); do
    case $1 in
    --head | --records)
        (($# >= 2)) || refuse "${usage}"
        if [[ $1 == --head ]]; then
            head=$2
        else
            records=$2
        fi
        shift 2
        ;;
    -*) refuse "${usage}" ;;
    *)
        [[ -z ${pr} ]] || refuse "${usage}"
        pr=$1
        shift
        ;;
    esac
done

[[ ${head} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || refuse "--head is not a 40-hex sha: ${head:-none}"
[[ -z ${records} || (-f ${records}/units.tsv && -f ${records}/decisions.tsv) ]] ||
    refuse "--records holds no units.tsv and decisions.tsv: ${records}"
[[ ${gh_timeout} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || refuse 'PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT must be a positive integer'
git cat-file -e "${head}^{commit}" 2> /dev/null || refuse "${head} is not a commit in this checkout; git fetch first"

repo=$(gh_bounded repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq .nameWithOwner) || fail 'gh repo view failed'
[[ ${repo} =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ ]] || fail "gh repo view printed no owner/repo: ${repo}"
listing=$(gh_bounded api graphql -f "query=${threads_query}" -f "owner=${repo%%/*}" -f "name=${repo#*/}" \
    -F "pr=${pr}" --jq "${threads_jq}") || fail "cannot list the review threads of pull request ${pr}"

threads=0
open=0
seen_head=0
while IFS=$'\t' read -r first resolved created severity count reply; do
    if [[ ${first} == head ]]; then
        [[ ${resolved} == "${head}" ]] || refuse "the head of pull request ${pr} is ${resolved}, not ${head}"
        [[ ${created} == false ]] || refuse "pull request ${pr} has more than 100 review threads; check it by hand"
        seen_head=1
        continue
    fi
    ((seen_head)) || fail "the listing of pull request ${pr} does not start with its head"
    [[ ${first} =~ ^[0-9]+$ && ${created} =~ ^[0-9]+$ && ${count} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] ||
        fail "unreadable thread row: ${first}"
    ((count <= 100)) || refuse "the thread of comment ${first} has more than 100 comments; check it by hand"
    threads=$((threads + 1))
    # A resolved thread is judged like an open one (U28b F1): GitHub's isResolved says someone clicked, not why.
    state=$(disposition "${created}" "${severity}" "${reply}") || exit $?
    if [[ ${resolved} == true ]]; then
        case ${state} in
        open*) state="open (resolved without a valid disposition: ${state#open (}" ;;
        *) state="resolved ${state}" ;;
        esac
    fi
    [[ ${state} != open* ]] || open=$((open + 1))
    echo "thread comment=${first} severity=${severity/-/none} state=${state}"
done <<< "${listing}"
((seen_head)) || fail "the listing of pull request ${pr} has no head"
echo "summary threads=${threads} open=${open}"
((open == 0)) || exit 2

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_provision-machine-key
# @brief Provision a per-machine SSH key for commit signing and push authentication.
# @description
#   Generates ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 non-interactively when it does not already
#   exist, then prints the exact `gh ssh-key add` commands needed to register
#   it with the operator's GitHub account for both authentication and commit
#   signing. Idempotent: an existing key is only displayed, never regenerated.
# @example
#   provision-machine-key

set -Eeuo pipefail

readonly MACHINE_SSH_KEY_PATH="${HOME%/}/.ssh/id_ed25519"
readonly MACHINE_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH="${MACHINE_SSH_KEY_PATH}.pub"

# @description Print the short host name, or fail naming the read when neither form works.
function short_hostname() {
    if ! hostname -s 2> /dev/null && ! hostname; then
        printf 'provision-machine-key: cannot read the host name for the SSH key comment\n' >&2
        return 1
    fi
}

# @description Return the email address used as the SSH key comment.
function ssh_key_email() {
    local configured_email host
    configured_email="$(git config --global --get user.email || true)"

    if [[ -n "${configured_email}" ]]; then
        printf '%s\n' "${configured_email}"
        return 0
    fi

    host="$(short_hostname)" || return 1
    printf '%s@%s\n' "${USER:-user}" "${host}"
}

# @description Generate the machine SSH key through ssh-keygen when it does not already exist.
function ensure_machine_ssh_key() {
    local email host

    if [[ -r "${MACHINE_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH}" ]]; then
        printf 'Machine SSH key already exists: %s\n' "${MACHINE_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH}"
        return 0
    fi

    mkdir -p "${HOME%/}/.ssh"
    chmod 0700 "${HOME%/}/.ssh"

    email="$(ssh_key_email)" || return 1
    host="$(short_hostname)" || return 1
    printf 'Generating machine SSH key: %s\n' "${MACHINE_SSH_KEY_PATH}"
    ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "${email} (${host})" \
        -f "${MACHINE_SSH_KEY_PATH}" -N ""
    chmod 0600 "${MACHINE_SSH_KEY_PATH}"
    chmod 0644 "${MACHINE_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH}"
}

# @description Print the manual GitHub registration steps for the public key.
function print_registration_instructions() {
    printf '\nRegister the public key with the operator'\''s GitHub account for BOTH scopes:\n\n'
    printf '  gh ssh-key add %q --type authentication\n' "${MACHINE_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH}"
    printf '  gh ssh-key add %q --type signing\n\n' "${MACHINE_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH}"
    printf 'Without the signing registration, commit.gpgsign=true environments cannot create commits.\n\n'
    printf 'Public key:\n'
    cat "${MACHINE_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH}"
}

# @description Run the machine key provisioning flow.
function main() {
    ensure_machine_ssh_key
    print_registration_instructions
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
    main
fi
