#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file records-sync.sh
# @brief Carry the program's records from the main checkout to a `records/sync-<n>` pull request.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U28 (ADDENDUM), the orchestrator seat's lever, allowed by the rows
#   `~/.local/bin/common/records-sync.sh *` and the bare `~/.local/bin/common/records-sync.sh` of
#   `home/dot_agents/omp/policies/orchestrator.yml` (the seat's own `git push` and `gh pr create` stay denied;
#   `worker.yml` denies every form, bare included, U28b F3). It runs in the main checkout, where the orchestrator
#   writes its records (a linked worktree is refused), and `.orchestration` there must be a real directory. The
#   copy set is the tracked changes against `HEAD` (`git diff --no-renames --name-only HEAD`, so a staged rename
#   lists its source too, U28c F1) and the untracked, not ignored
#   files (`git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`) under `.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>/` and
#   `.orchestration/validation/`; every path must lie under `.orchestration/`, no component of it may be a
#   symlink (git lists the tracked files below a linked directory too, U28b F2), and an existing source must be a
#   regular file whose directory resolves (`pwd -P`) inside the store, else the run is refused before anything is
#   created. `<n>` is one more than the largest number among the remote heads, the local branches (U28b F6) and
#   the heads of the newest 1000 pull requests named `records/sync-<n>`, `records/program-store-<n>` or
#   `records/<program>-sync-<n>` (the earlier syncs), and the branch must match `records/sync-<n>`. In a new
#   worktree under `$TMPDIR` on that branch from `origin/main` it copies the set, masks the copies with the
#   worktree's own `scripts/validate-agent-assets.py --mask-secrets` (the checkout's files are never changed;
#   a masking failure aborts), refuses a staged path outside `.orchestration/`, commits
#   `chore(records): <program> sync <n>` with the footer, pushes that branch only, and opens the pull request
#   with `gh pr create --base main --head records/sync-<n> --title ... --body-file ...`; the body lists the
#   `units.tsv` ids and the `decisions.tsv` timestamps the sync adds or changes and the line
#   `Program-Unit: <program>/<unit>`, which the `regime` check requires (U28c F2). The worktree is removed on every
#   exit (`git worktree remove --force`, only
#   on the path this run created), and a run that exits before its push deletes the branch it created (only that
#   one), so a retry takes the same number; a pushed branch stays. Each `gh` call is bounded by
#   PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds.
# @option --base <ref> The start point; only `origin/main` (the default) is accepted.
# @option --program <name> The program directory under `.orchestration/orchestrate/`; default: the only one.
# @option --unit <U<n>> The unit the body's `Program-Unit:` line names; default: U20, the records unit.
# @env PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT Seconds per `gh` call (default 60).
# @stdout One receipt line: `synced branch=records/sync-<n> files=<n> pr=<url>`.
# @exitcode 0 The pull request was opened.
# @exitcode 1 A `git` or `gh` step, or the masking, failed; nothing was pushed unless the receipt says so.
# @exitcode 2 Refused: usage, a linked worktree, the program, the copy set, or nothing to sync.
# @example
#   ~/.local/bin/common/records-sync.sh --program regime-cutover --unit U20
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

lever='records-sync.sh'
usage='usage: records-sync.sh [--base origin/main] [--program <name>] [--unit U<n> (default U20)]'
gh_timeout=${PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT:-60}
footer='Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>'
pr_footer='🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)'

# @description Print the refusal on stderr and exit 2.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
refuse() {
    echo "${lever}: refused: $*" >&2
    exit 2
}

# @description Print the failure on stderr and exit 1.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
fail() {
    echo "${lever}: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

# @description Run `gh` with its wait bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds.
# @arg $@ string The `gh` arguments.
gh_bounded() {
    perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV or die "exec gh: $!\n"' "${gh_timeout}" gh "$@"
}

# @description Remove the worktree this run created, and its scratch directory.
cleanup() {
    if [[ -n ${scratch:-} && -d ${scratch} ]]; then
        if [[ -d ${scratch}/tree ]]; then
            git -C "${toplevel}" worktree remove --force "${scratch}/tree" > /dev/null 2>&1 ||
                echo "${lever}: could not remove the worktree ${scratch}/tree" >&2
        fi
        rm -r "${scratch}" 2> /dev/null || echo "${lever}: could not remove ${scratch}" >&2
    fi
    # U28b F6: a run that created its branch and never pushed it deletes exactly that branch, so a retry is not
    # blocked by it; a pushed branch stays (the remote holds it, and the next run numbers past it).
    if [[ -n ${created_branch:-} && ${pushed:-0} == 0 ]]; then
        git -C "${toplevel}" branch -D "${created_branch}" > /dev/null 2>&1 ||
            echo "${lever}: could not delete the unpushed branch ${created_branch}" >&2
    fi
}

base=origin/main
program=''
unit=U20
while (($#)); do
    case $1 in
    --base | --program | --unit)
        (($# >= 2)) || refuse "${usage}"
        case $1 in
        --base) base=$2 ;;
        --program) program=$2 ;;
        --unit) unit=$2 ;;
        esac
        shift 2
        ;;
    *) refuse "${usage}" ;;
    esac
done
[[ ${base} == origin/main ]] || refuse "--base accepts only origin/main: ${base}" # lint-comparisons: allow a git ref name, not a path
[[ ${unit} =~ ^U[0-9]+$ ]] || refuse "--unit is not a plain unit id U<n>: ${unit}"
[[ ${gh_timeout} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || refuse 'PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT must be a positive integer'

toplevel=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2> /dev/null) || refuse 'not in a git checkout'
git_dir=$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir) || refuse 'cannot read the git directory'
common_dir=$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir) || refuse 'cannot read the git common directory'
git_dir=$(cd "${git_dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${git_dir}"
common_dir=$(cd "${common_dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${common_dir}"
[[ ${git_dir} == "${common_dir}" ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
    refuse "${toplevel} is a linked worktree; run from the main checkout, where the orchestrator writes its records"
cd "${toplevel}" || refuse "cannot enter ${toplevel}"
# U28b F2: the store root itself is no symlink, so every canonical path below is measured against the real store.
top_real=$(pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${toplevel}"
[[ -d .orchestration && ! -L .orchestration ]] || refuse ".orchestration is missing or a symlink in ${toplevel}"
store_root=$(cd .orchestration && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${toplevel}/.orchestration"
[[ ${store_root} == "${top_real}/.orchestration" ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
    refuse ".orchestration resolves outside ${top_real}: ${store_root}"
if [[ -z ${program} ]]; then
    programs=()
    for dir in .orchestration/orchestrate/*/; do
        dir=${dir%/}
        [[ -d ${dir} ]] && programs+=("${dir##*/}")
    done
    ((${#programs[@]} == 1)) || refuse "name the program with --program; .orchestration/orchestrate/ holds ${#programs[@]}"
    program=${programs[0]}
fi
[[ ${program} =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$ ]] || refuse "the program name is outside [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*: ${program}"
[[ -d .orchestration/orchestrate/${program} && ! -L .orchestration/orchestrate/${program} ]] ||
    refuse "no program directory .orchestration/orchestrate/${program}"
dirs=(".orchestration/orchestrate/${program}/" .orchestration/validation/)

changed=$(git diff --no-renames --name-only -z HEAD -- "${dirs[@]}" | tr '\0' '\n') || fail 'git diff --name-only HEAD failed'
untracked=$(git ls-files -z --others --exclude-standard -- "${dirs[@]}" | tr '\0' '\n') || fail 'git ls-files --others failed'
listed=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "${changed}" "${untracked}" | sort -u) || fail 'cannot list the copy set'
files=()
while IFS= read -r path; do
    [[ -n ${path} ]] || continue
    case ${path} in # lint-comparisons: allow a repository-relative path as git prints it, refused unless under the store
    .orchestration/*) ;;
    *) refuse "a path of the copy set is outside .orchestration/: ${path}" ;;
    esac
    [[ ${path} != *..* ]] || refuse "a path of the copy set holds '..': ${path}" # lint-comparisons: allow refuses a raw git path that holds ..
    # U28b F2: no component may be a symlink (git lists the tracked files below a linked directory too), and an
    # existing source must resolve inside the store before anything is copied.
    prefix=''
    IFS=/ read -r -a parts <<< "${path}"
    for part in "${parts[@]}"; do
        prefix=${prefix:+${prefix}/}${part}
        [[ ! -L ${prefix} ]] || refuse "a component of a path of the copy set is a symlink: ${prefix} (in ${path})"
    done
    if [[ -e ${path} ]]; then
        [[ -f ${path} ]] || refuse "a path of the copy set is not a regular file: ${path}"
        source_dir=$(cd "${path%/*}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve the directory of ${path}"
        [[ ${source_dir} == "${store_root}" || ${source_dir} == "${store_root}"/* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
            refuse "a path of the copy set resolves outside ${store_root}: ${path}"
    fi
    files+=("${path}")
done <<< "${listed}"
((${#files[@]} > 0)) || refuse "nothing to sync under ${dirs[*]}"

remote_heads=$(git ls-remote --heads origin 'refs/heads/records/*') || fail 'git ls-remote origin failed'
# U28b F6: a local branch occupies its number too, whatever left it behind.
local_heads=$(git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' 'refs/heads/records/') || fail 'git for-each-ref failed'
pr_heads=$(gh_bounded pr list --state all --limit 1000 --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName') ||
    fail 'gh pr list failed'
last=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "${remote_heads}" "${local_heads}" "${pr_heads}" |
    PROGRAM=${program} awk '{ ref = $NF; sub(/^refs\/heads\//, "", ref) }
        ref ~ "^records/(sync|program-store|" ENVIRON["PROGRAM"] "-sync)-[0-9]+$" { n = ref; sub(/.*-/, "", n); if (n + 0 > max) max = n + 0 }
        END { print max + 0 }') || fail 'cannot number the sync'
n=$((last + 1))
branch=records/sync-${n}
[[ ${branch} =~ ^records/sync-[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || refuse "the branch is outside records/sync-<n>: ${branch}"

git fetch --quiet origin main || fail 'git fetch origin main failed'
scratch=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/records-sync.XXXXXX") || fail 'mktemp failed'
trap cleanup EXIT
tree=${scratch}/tree
git worktree add --quiet -b "${branch}" "${tree}" "${base}" || fail "git worktree add ${branch} failed"
created_branch=${branch}
pushed=0
masked=()
for path in "${files[@]}"; do
    if [[ -e ${path} ]]; then
        mkdir -p "${tree}/${path%/*}" || fail "mkdir for ${path} failed"
        cp -p "${path}" "${tree}/${path}" || fail "cp ${path} failed"
        masked+=("${tree}/${path}")
    elif [[ -e ${tree}/${path} ]]; then
        git -C "${tree}" rm --quiet -- "${path}" || fail "git rm ${path} failed"
    fi
done
if ((${#masked[@]})); then
    uv run --no-project python -I "${tree}/scripts/validate-agent-assets.py" --mask-secrets "${masked[@]}" >&2 ||
        fail 'masking the copies failed; nothing was committed or pushed'
fi
git -C "${tree}" add -A -- .orchestration || fail 'git add failed'
staged=$(git -C "${tree}" diff --cached --no-renames --name-only -z | tr '\0' '\n') || fail 'git diff --cached failed'
[[ -n ${staged} ]] || refuse 'the copies equal origin/main; nothing to sync'
while IFS= read -r path; do
    [[ ${path} == .orchestration/* ]] || refuse "a staged path is outside .orchestration/: ${path}" # lint-comparisons: allow a repository-relative path as git prints it
done <<< "${staged}"
count=$(printf '%s\n' "${staged}" | wc -l) || fail 'wc failed'
count=${count//[[:space:]]/}

records=.orchestration/orchestrate/${program}
units=$(git -C "${tree}" diff --cached -U0 -- "${records}/units.tsv" | sed -n -E 's/^\+(U[0-9]+[a-z]?)\t.*/\1/p' | sort -u | paste -sd ' ' -) ||
    fail 'cannot list the units'
decisions=$(git -C "${tree}" diff --cached -U0 -- "${records}/decisions.tsv" | sed -n -E 's/^\+([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:]+Z)\t.*/\1/p' | sort -u | paste -sd ' ' -) ||
    fail 'cannot list the decisions'
title="chore(records): ${program} sync ${n}"
git -C "${tree}" commit --quiet -m "${title}" -m "Carries ${count} file(s) of ${records}/ and .orchestration/validation/ from the main checkout (records-sync.sh)." -m "${footer}" ||
    fail 'git commit failed'
git -C "${tree}" push --quiet origin "refs/heads/${branch}:refs/heads/${branch}" || fail "git push ${branch} failed; nothing was opened"
pushed=1
body=${scratch}/body.md
{
    # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # the backticks are Markdown code spans
    printf '## Summary\n\nRecords sync %s of `%s` (%s file(s)), carried by `records-sync.sh` from the main checkout; every copy was masked with `validate-agent-assets.py --mask-secrets`.\n\n' "${n}" "${program}" "${count}"
    printf -- '- units.tsv rows added or changed: %s\n' "${units:-none}"
    printf -- '- decisions.tsv rows added or changed: %s\n\n' "${decisions:-none}"
    printf 'Program-Unit: %s/%s\n\n' "${program}" "${unit}"
    printf '%s\n' "${pr_footer}"
} > "${body}" || fail 'cannot write the body'
url=$(gh_bounded pr create --base main --head "${branch}" --title "${title}" --body-file "${body}") ||
    fail "gh pr create failed; the branch ${branch} is pushed"
echo "synced branch=${branch} files=${count} pr=${url}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file regime-env
# @brief The per-repository regime derivation the levers source: repository slug, hcom store, team, seat root.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U33. Sourced by `hcom-seat`, `hcom-dispatch`, `bus-history.sh` and `regime-init` from the
#   directory they run from (`LEVER_DIR`), never run on its own. It checks its own sha256 against its
#   `claude.levers.sha256.regime-env` pin first, like every lever, so a rewritten helper stops the caller.
#   Defaults, an explicit environment always winning: `HCOM_TEAM=<slug>`, `HCOM_DIR=~/.local/state/hcom/<slug>`,
#   seats root `~/.local/state/omp-seats/<slug>`, where `<slug>` is the checkout's basename lower-cased with
#   every character outside `[a-z0-9_-]` replaced by `-`, at most 40 characters. A derived store's `origin`
#   file, written by `regime-init`, must name this checkout, so two checkouts with one basename cannot share a
#   store unnoticed.
# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
# @set LEVER_DIR The physical directory of this file, where the sourced regime-env helper sits (U33).
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    # shellcheck disable=SC2034 # read by the levers that source regime-env from this directory
    LEVER_DIR=${dir}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

# @description Print the physical toplevel of the repository's main checkout: the parent of the git common
#   directory, so every linked worktree of a repository (a seat worktree, `.claude/worktrees/*`) derives the
#   same slug as the checkout it was added from; a repository whose git directory is elsewhere falls back to
#   its own toplevel.
# @stdout The toplevel, `pwd -P` form.
# @exitcode 0 Inside a checkout.
# @exitcode 1 Outside a checkout, or the toplevel cannot be resolved.
regime_toplevel() {
    local common top
    common=$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2> /dev/null) || return 1
    if [[ ${common##*/} == .git ]]; then
        top=${common%/*}
    else
        top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2> /dev/null) || return 1
    fi
    [[ -n ${top} ]] || return 1
    (cd "${top}" && pwd -P)
}

# @description Print the repository slug of a toplevel: its basename lower-cased, every character outside
#   `[a-z0-9_-]` replaced by `-`, at most 40 characters, so hcom's team and tag grammar accept it.
# @arg $1 path The toplevel.
# @stdout The slug.
# @exitcode 0 A usable slug.
# @exitcode 1 The slug does not start with `[a-z0-9]`, or the lower-casing failed.
regime_slug() {
    local base slug
    base=${1%/}
    base=${base##*/}
    slug=$(printf '%s' "${base}" | LC_ALL=C tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]') || return 1
    slug=${slug//[^a-z0-9_-]/-}
    slug=${slug:0:40}
    [[ ${slug} =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,39}$ ]] || return 1
    printf '%s\n' "${slug}"
}

# @description Derive the regime environment of the checkout the working directory is in; an explicit value
#   always wins. A derived store is bound to its checkout by its `origin` file, which only `regime-init` writes:
#   every other caller requires it to exist and name this toplevel, so a second checkout with the same slug
#   cannot open or create the store. No part of a derived store path may be a symlink (`~/.local/state/hcom`,
#   the store, `origin`), so nothing reads or writes through one. A refusal prints its reason prefixed with the
#   caller's name and returns 1.
# @arg $1 string The caller's name, for messages.
# @option --unbound-ok The caller is `regime-init`: a derived store without its `origin` file is allowed.
# @set REGIME_TOPLEVEL The physical toplevel, empty when HCOM_DIR is explicit and the cwd is outside a checkout.
# @set REGIME_SLUG The repository slug (empty with REGIME_TOPLEVEL).
# @set REGIME_ORIGIN The derived store's origin file, empty when HCOM_DIR is explicit.
# @set HCOM_TEAM `<slug>` unless set (exported).
# @set HCOM_DIR `~/.local/state/hcom/<slug>` unless set (exported).
# @set REGIME_SEATS_ROOT `~/.local/state/omp-seats/<slug>` unless set.
# @exitcode 1 Outside a checkout with HCOM_DIR unset; an unusable slug; a symlink in the derived store path; a
#   derived store without `origin` (unless --unbound-ok), or whose `origin` is unreadable or names another toplevel.
regime_env() {
    local who=$1 unbound_ok=${2:-} recorded part
    REGIME_TOPLEVEL='' REGIME_SLUG='' REGIME_ORIGIN='' REGIME_SEATS_ROOT=${REGIME_SEATS_ROOT:-}
    if ! REGIME_TOPLEVEL=$(regime_toplevel); then
        REGIME_TOPLEVEL=''
        if [[ -n ${HCOM_DIR:-} ]]; then
            export HCOM_DIR
            [[ -z ${HCOM_TEAM:-} ]] || export HCOM_TEAM
            return 0
        fi
        echo "${who}: not inside a git checkout and HCOM_DIR is unset, so no hcom store can be derived" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    REGIME_SLUG=$(regime_slug "${REGIME_TOPLEVEL}") || {
        echo "${who}: cannot derive a repository slug from ${REGIME_TOPLEVEL} (it must start with [a-z0-9])" >&2
        return 1
    }
    : "${HCOM_TEAM:=${REGIME_SLUG}}"
    : "${REGIME_SEATS_ROOT:=${HOME}/.local/state/omp-seats/${REGIME_SLUG}}"
    if [[ -z ${HCOM_DIR:-} ]]; then
        HCOM_DIR=${HOME}/.local/state/hcom/${REGIME_SLUG}
        REGIME_ORIGIN=${HCOM_DIR}/origin
        for part in "${HOME}/.local/state/hcom" "${HCOM_DIR}" "${REGIME_ORIGIN}"; do
            if [[ -L ${part} ]]; then
                echo "${who}: refused: ${part} is a symlink; a derived hcom store is a plain directory" >&2
                return 1
            fi
        done
        if [[ -e ${REGIME_ORIGIN} ]]; then
            recorded=$(cat "${REGIME_ORIGIN}") || {
                echo "${who}: cannot read ${REGIME_ORIGIN}" >&2
                return 1
            }
            if [[ ${recorded} != "${REGIME_TOPLEVEL}" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both are pwd -P forms written by regime-init
                echo "${who}: refused: the store ${HCOM_DIR} belongs to ${recorded}, not ${REGIME_TOPLEVEL} (same slug ${REGIME_SLUG}); set HCOM_DIR and HCOM_TEAM explicitly" >&2
                return 1
            fi
        elif [[ ${unbound_ok} != --unbound-ok ]]; then
            echo "${who}: refused: the derived store ${HCOM_DIR} has no origin file binding it to ${REGIME_TOPLEVEL}; run regime-init <program> in the checkout first" >&2
            return 1
        fi
    fi
    export HCOM_DIR HCOM_TEAM
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file regime-init
# @brief Prepare a repository on this host for the hcom regime: the program store, the store origin, the AGENTS.md audit section.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U33, a coordinator lever pre-authorized by `Bash(~/.local/bin/common/regime-init *)`. Run it
#   in the git checkout of the repository. It derives the repository slug, hcom store and team through the
#   sourced regime-env helper, then creates `<toplevel>/.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>/` with the
#   templates from `~/.agents/regime/` (preferences.md, units.tsv, ledger.tsv, decisions.tsv, gates.md),
#   writes `~/.local/state/hcom/<slug>/origin` with the toplevel, and prints the AGENTS.md audit section, or
#   appends it with `--write-agents` when AGENTS.md has no `## Audit` heading. It is idempotent: an existing
#   file equal to its template is left alone, one that differs is kept unless `--force` replaces it, and a
#   second run says that nothing changed. It never writes through a symlink, and it refuses outside a git
#   checkout and when the derived store's origin names another checkout with the same slug.
# @arg $1 string Program name (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`), the store directory under .orchestration/orchestrate.
# @option --force Replace store files that differ from their template.
# @option --write-agents Append the audit section to AGENTS.md when it has no `## Audit` heading.
# @stdout One row per file (`created`, `unchanged`, `kept`, `replaced`, `appended`), the section when not written, the next commands.
# @exitcode 0 Done, including when nothing changed.
# @exitcode 2 A refusal, before or instead of the write it names.
# @example
#   regime-init pilot --write-agents
set -euo pipefail
# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
# @set LEVER_DIR The physical directory of this file, where the sourced regime-env helper sits (U33).
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    LEVER_DIR=${dir}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

usage='usage: regime-init <program> [--force] [--write-agents]'
refuse() {
    echo "regime-init: $*" >&2
    exit 2
}
(($# >= 1)) || refuse "${usage}"
program=$1
shift
force=0 write_agents=0
while (($#)); do
    case $1 in
    --force) force=1 ;;
    --write-agents) write_agents=1 ;;
    *) refuse "${usage}" ;;
    esac
    shift
done
[[ ${program} =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$ ]] || refuse "program '${program}' is outside ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}\$"

[[ -r ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env ]] || refuse "regime-env unreadable beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env"
# shellcheck source=scripts/orchestrator/regime-env
. "${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env"
checkout=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2> /dev/null) || refuse 'run regime-init inside the git checkout of the repository'
checkout=$(cd "${checkout}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${checkout}"
# A seat inherits HCOM_DIR and HCOM_TEAM from its launch, and an explicit value wins over the derivation.
inherited=''
[[ -z ${HCOM_DIR:-} && -z ${HCOM_TEAM:-} ]] || inherited="HCOM_DIR=${HCOM_DIR:-} HCOM_TEAM=${HCOM_TEAM:-}"
regime_env regime-init --unbound-ok || exit 2
templates=${LEVER_MANIFEST%/*}/regime
[[ -d ${templates} ]] || refuse "templates absent: ${templates}"
store=${checkout}/.orchestration/orchestrate/${program}
origin=${REGIME_ORIGIN:-${HCOM_DIR}/origin}
# Checked before anything is written: an explicit HCOM_DIR gets the same no-symlink rule as a derived one.
[[ ! -L ${HCOM_DIR} && ! -L ${origin} ]] || refuse "refused: ${HCOM_DIR} or ${origin} is a symlink"

# Nothing is written through a symlink: the store, each file and AGENTS.md are refused when one stands there.
for path in "${checkout}/.orchestration" "${checkout}/.orchestration/orchestrate" "${store}" "${checkout}/AGENTS.md"; do
    [[ ! -L ${path} ]] || refuse "refused: ${path} is a symlink"
done

changed=0
# @description Copy one template into the store: create it when absent, keep it when equal, replace it only
#   with --force; print one row `<created|unchanged|kept|replaced>\t<path>`.
# @arg $1 string The template file name.
place() {
    local source=${templates}/$1 target=${store}/$1
    [[ -f ${source} ]] || refuse "template absent: ${source}"
    [[ ! -L ${target} ]] || refuse "refused: ${target} is a symlink"
    if [[ ! -e ${target} ]]; then
        cp "${source}" "${target}" || refuse "cannot write ${target}"
        printf 'created\t%s\n' "${target}"
        changed=1
        return
    fi
    local same=0
    cmp -s "${source}" "${target}" || same=$?
    ((same <= 1)) || refuse "cannot compare ${target} with ${source}"
    if ((same == 0)); then
        printf 'unchanged\t%s\n' "${target}"
    elif ((force)); then
        cp "${source}" "${target}" || refuse "cannot write ${target}"
        printf 'replaced\t%s\n' "${target}"
        changed=1
    else
        printf 'kept\t%s\t(differs from the template; --force replaces it)\n' "${target}"
    fi
}

mkdir -p "${store}" || refuse "cannot create ${store}"
for file in preferences.md units.tsv ledger.tsv decisions.tsv gates.md; do
    place "${file}"
done

# The origin file binds the derived store to this checkout, so a second checkout with the same slug is refused.
if [[ -e ${origin} ]]; then
    printf 'unchanged\t%s\n' "${origin}"
else
    mkdir -p "${HCOM_DIR}" || refuse "cannot create ${HCOM_DIR}"
    printf '%s\n' "${REGIME_TOPLEVEL}" > "${origin}" || refuse "cannot write ${origin}"
    printf 'created\t%s\n' "${origin}"
    changed=1
fi

section=${templates}/AGENTS-audit-section.md
[[ -f ${section} ]] || refuse "template absent: ${section}"
agents=${checkout}/AGENTS.md
if ((write_agents)); then
    has_audit=1
    if [[ -e ${agents} ]]; then
        has_audit=0
        grep -q '^## Audit$' "${agents}" || has_audit=$?
        ((has_audit <= 1)) || refuse "cannot read ${agents}"
    fi
    if ((has_audit == 0)); then
        printf 'unchanged\t%s\t(it has an "## Audit" section)\n' "${agents}"
    else
        if [[ -s ${agents} ]]; then printf '\n' >> "${agents}" || refuse "cannot write ${agents}"; fi
        cat "${section}" >> "${agents}" || refuse "cannot write ${agents}"
        printf 'appended\t%s\n' "${agents}"
        changed=1
    fi
else
    printf '\nAppend to %s (or rerun with --write-agents):\n\n' "${agents}"
    cat "${section}" || refuse "cannot read ${section}"
fi

((changed)) || echo 'regime-init: nothing changed; the program store, origin and AGENTS.md were already in place'
# hcom reads only HCOM_DIR, which the levers export to their own children, so the listing names the store itself.
listing=$(printf 'HCOM_DIR=%q hcom list -v' "${HCOM_DIR}") || refuse 'cannot format the store-scoped hcom listing'
cat << EOF

Next, in ${checkout}:
  hcom-seat orchestrator; hcom-seat worker
  ${listing}
  hcom-dispatch ${HCOM_TEAM} operator orchestrator-<word> - "TASK v1 task_id=O1 brief=<absolute path of the program brief>"
From inside a seat, which inherits HCOM_DIR and HCOM_TEAM from its launch, unset both first
(env -u HCOM_DIR -u HCOM_TEAM <command>), or the seats join the inheriting seat's store and team.
EOF
if [[ -n ${inherited} ]]; then
    echo "regime-init: note: this shell set ${inherited}, so the origin and the lines above use them, not the store derived for ${REGIME_SLUG:-this repository}; rerun as env -u HCOM_DIR -u HCOM_TEAM regime-init ${program} to bind the repository's own store" >&2
fi

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""regime-open-url: hand a sign-in URL from a seat host to the laptop's browser (regime-cutover U37).

On the seat host (Ubuntu), the SSH session from the laptop carries `RemoteForward 127.0.0.1:1456
127.0.0.1:1456` (the `Match tagged seat-host` block of `~/.ssh/config`), so `127.0.0.1:1456` here is the
laptop's `regime-url-opener`, which opens only allow-listed sign-in hosts. Claude Code calls it as
`BROWSER`; omp's `openPath` calls `xdg-open`, which `seat-login-preflight` points here for the login
only. The URL is posted as the body of `POST /open` with `X-Regime-Open: 1`; the URL is never logged here.

Exit 0 when the laptop opened it; 1 with the reason on stderr otherwise, and the caller has already shown
the URL, so the operator can open it by hand.

Usage: regime-open-url <url>
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.request


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    if len(argv) != 1 or not argv[0]:
        print("usage: regime-open-url <url>", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    url = argv[0]
    port = os.environ.get("REGIME_URL_OPENER_PORT", "1456")
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/open",
        data=url.encode("utf-8"),
        method="POST",
        headers={"X-Regime-Open": "1", "Content-Type": "text/plain; charset=utf-8"},
    )
    # A proxy setting must never carry the loopback request off this host.
    opener = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.ProxyHandler({}))
    try:
        with opener.open(request, timeout=10) as response:
            response.read()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
        reason = error.read().decode("utf-8", "replace").strip() or error.reason
        print(
            f"regime-open-url: the laptop opener refused the URL ({error.code}: {reason}); open the URL shown above yourself",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 1
    except (urllib.error.URLError, OSError) as error:
        reason = getattr(error, "reason", error)
        print(
            f"regime-open-url: no laptop opener on 127.0.0.1:{port} ({reason}); connect with the `seat-host` SSH entry "
            "and run regime-url-opener on the laptop, or open the URL shown above yourself",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 1
    print("regime-open-url: opened the sign-in URL in the laptop browser", file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

# @description Take the host's one regime lock, which regime-start, its supervisor pass and regime-stop share, so a
#   stop never interleaves with a launch (U36 F2). The lock is the kernel's flock(2) on the file `lock`, held through
#   descriptor 9 of this process: perl (on both hosts; macOS ships no flock command) takes it on that inherited
#   descriptor and exits, and the lock stays with the open file, which this process keeps, and the subshell that runs
#   a launch keeps until the launch returns. Every hcom call and hcom-seat get the descriptor closed, so no seat or
#   hcom process ever holds it. The kernel releases it when the last holder exits or dies, so nothing is ever
#   recovered by age or pid, no other process can release it, and the file itself is never removed. The holder
#   writes its pid into the file, for messages only. A lock file replaced after it was opened (another inode at the
#   path) is opened again, at most three times.
# @arg $1 string `wait` (up to REGIME_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS, default 300) or `try` (once).
# @set lock_holder The pid the current holder wrote, when the lock is held.
# @exitcode 1 The lock is held by another process.
take_lock() {
    local seconds=0 status attempt=0
    [[ $1 == wait ]] && seconds=${lock_wait}
    mkdir -p "${registry}" || refuse "cannot create ${registry}"
    while ((attempt < 3)); do
        attempt=$((attempt + 1))
        [[ ! -L ${lock} ]] || refuse "${lock} is a symlink; nothing changed"
        exec 9>> "${lock}" || refuse "cannot open ${lock}; nothing changed"
        status=0
        perl -MFcntl=:flock -e '
            my ($wait, $owner, $path) = @ARGV;
            open(my $fh, ">>&=", 9) or exit 3;
            for my $try (0 .. $wait) {
                if (flock($fh, LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)) {
                    my @held = stat($fh);
                    my @named = stat($path);
                    exit 4 unless @named && $named[0] == $held[0] && $named[1] == $held[1];
                    truncate($fh, 0) or exit 3;
                    syswrite($fh, "$owner\n") or exit 3;
                    exit 0;
                }
                sleep 1 if $try < $wait;
            }
            exit 1;' "${seconds}" "$$" "${lock}" || status=$?
        case ${status} in
        0) return 0 ;;
        1)
            lock_holder=$(cat "${lock}" 2> /dev/null) || lock_holder=''
            [[ ${lock_holder} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || lock_holder=unknown
            exec 9>&-
            return 1
            ;;
        4) exec 9>&- ;;
        *) refuse "cannot take the flock on ${lock} (perl exited ${status}); nothing changed" ;;
        esac
    done
    refuse "${lock} was replaced while it was being locked, three times; nothing changed"
}

# @description Print the registration file of a checkout: `<slug>-<first 12 hex of sha256(toplevel)>.conf`, so two
#   checkouts with one basename never share a registration (U36 F3).
# @arg $1 path The physical toplevel.
# @arg $2 string Its slug.
# @exitcode 1 The digest could not be computed.
registration_path() {
    local digest
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(printf '%s' "$1" | sha256sum) || return 1
    else
        digest=$(printf '%s' "$1" | shasum -a 256) || return 1
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || return 1
    printf '%s/%s-%s.conf\n' "${registry}" "$2" "${digest:0:12}"
}

# @description Read a registration into reg_top, reg_store, reg_team, reg_program, reg_seat, reg_base, reg_fails and
#   reg_next. Every key must appear exactly once and nothing else may (U36 F4); the seat is `orchestrator-<base>`;
#   the counters have bounded lengths (U36 F5); and the file must be the one registration_path names for its own
#   toplevel, so a registration copied to another checkout's name is refused, and a store with an `origin` file
#   (a derived one, written by regime-init) must name that toplevel (U36 F3).
# @arg $1 path The registration file.
# @stdout Nothing.
# @stderr Nothing.
# @set reg_error Why the registration is unusable, empty when it is usable.
read_registration() {
    local conf=$1 line key value expected slug recorded
    # Bash 3.2 (macOS /bin/bash) has no associative arrays, so the keys seen are one space-separated string.
    local seen=' '
    reg_error='' reg_top='' reg_store='' reg_team='' reg_program='' reg_seat='' reg_base='' reg_fails='' reg_next=''
    if ! [[ -f ${conf} && -r ${conf} ]]; then
        reg_error='unreadable'
        return 0
    fi
    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n ${line} ]]; do
        key=${line%%=*}
        value=${line#*=}
        if [[ ${line} != *=* ]]; then
            reg_error="a line without a key: '${line}'"
            return 0
        fi
        case ${key} in
        toplevel | hcom_dir | hcom_team | program | seat | base | fails | next) ;;
        *)
            reg_error="unknown key '${key}'"
            return 0
            ;;
        esac
        if [[ ${seen} == *" ${key} "* ]]; then
            reg_error="key '${key}' appears twice"
            return 0
        fi
        seen+="${key} "
        printf -v "reg_${key/toplevel/top}" '%s' "${value}"
    done < "${conf}" || {
        reg_error='unreadable'
        return 0
    }
    reg_store=${reg_hcom_dir:-} reg_team=${reg_hcom_team:-}
    for key in toplevel hcom_dir hcom_team program seat base fails next; do
        if [[ ${seen} != *" ${key} "* ]]; then
            reg_error="key '${key}' is missing"
            return 0
        fi
    done
    if [[ ${reg_top} != /* || ! -d ${reg_top} || ${reg_store} != /* || ! -d ${reg_store} ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path prefix test, not a comparison of two paths
        reg_error='the toplevel or the store is not an existing absolute directory'
    elif [[ ! ${reg_team} =~ ${name_grammar} || ! ${reg_base} =~ ${name_grammar} ]]; then
        reg_error='the team or the base name is outside the grammar'
    elif [[ -n ${reg_program} && ! ${reg_program} =~ ${name_grammar} ]]; then
        reg_error='the program is outside the grammar'
    elif [[ ${reg_seat} != "orchestrator-${reg_base}" ]]; then
        reg_error="the seat '${reg_seat}' is not orchestrator-<base>"
    elif [[ ! ${reg_fails} =~ ^[0-9]{1,4}$ || ! ${reg_next} =~ ^[0-9]{1,12}$ ]]; then
        reg_error='the counters are not bounded numbers'
    elif ! slug=$(regime_slug "${reg_top}" 2> /dev/null) || ! expected=$(registration_path "${reg_top}" "${slug}"); then
        reg_error="cannot derive the registration name of ${reg_top}"
    elif [[ ${conf##*/} != "${expected##*/}" ]]; then
        reg_error="the file name does not belong to the toplevel ${reg_top}"
    elif [[ -e ${reg_store}/origin ]]; then
        if ! recorded=$(cat "${reg_store}/origin" 2> /dev/null); then
            reg_error="cannot read ${reg_store}/origin"
        elif [[ ${recorded} != "${reg_top}" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both are pwd -P forms (regime-init, regime_toplevel)
            reg_error="the store ${reg_store} belongs to ${recorded}, not ${reg_top}"
        fi
    fi
    return 0
}

# @description Append one timestamped line to the store's supervisor log; a log that cannot be written is said on stderr.
# @arg $1 path The hcom store.
# @arg $@ string The line.
log_line() {
    local store=$1 stamp
    shift
    stamp=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) || stamp=unknown-time
    printf '%s %s\n' "${stamp}" "$*" >> "${store}/supervisor.log" 2> /dev/null ||
        echo "regime-start: cannot write ${store}/supervisor.log: $*" >&2
}

# @description Print `<name> <base name>` of every alive seat tagged orchestrator in the store HCOM_DIR names.
# @exitcode 1 hcom could not be read (a failed read is never "no seat").
alive_orchestrators() {
    local listing name base tag status
    listing=$(hcom list --format '{name} {base_name} {tag} {status}' 9>&-) || return 1
    while read -r name base tag status; do
        [[ ${tag} == orchestrator ]] || continue
        case ${status} in
        active | listening | blocked) printf '%s %s\n' "${name}" "${base}" ;;
        esac
    done <<< "${listing}"
}

# @description Launch the orchestrator seat from the checkout and wait for it to be alive.
# @arg $1 path The checkout's toplevel.
# @stdout `<name> <base name>` of the seat that came alive.
# @exitcode 1 hcom-seat failed, or no seat was alive within the wait.
launch_orchestrator() {
    local top=$1 status=0 waited=0 alive=''
    # Killing regime-start cannot release the lock while a launch runs (U36 F2): both callers run this function in a
    # command-substitution subshell, which keeps descriptor 9 until the launch and its wait return, and the subshell
    # below keeps it until hcom-seat returns, so the hold does not depend on the caller (the command after hcom-seat
    # keeps bash from exec-ing it in place of that subshell). hcom-seat, and the hcom and seat processes it starts,
    # get the descriptor closed, so a detached seat never holds the lock after the launch.
    (
        cd "${top}" || exit 1
        "${LEVER_DIR}/hcom-seat" orchestrator 9>&-
        launched=$?
        exit "${launched}"
    ) >&2 || status=$?
    # hcom's status 2 is "still launching": wait for the seat like a ready one.
    if ((status != 0 && status != 2)); then
        echo "regime-start: hcom-seat orchestrator exited ${status}" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    while ((waited <= wait_seconds)); do
        if alive=$(alive_orchestrators) && [[ -n ${alive} ]]; then
            printf '%s\n' "${alive%%$'\n'*}"
            return 0
        fi
        sleep 2
        waited=$((waited + 2))
    done
    echo "regime-start: no orchestrator seat alive in ${HCOM_DIR} after ${wait_seconds} s" >&2
    return 1
}

# @description Write a registration atomically (a temporary file, then a rename).
# @arg $1 path The registration file.
# @arg $@ string `key=value` lines.
write_registration() {
    local file=$1 temp
    shift
    mkdir -p "${registry}"
    temp=$(mktemp "${file}.XXXXXX")
    printf '%s\n' "$@" > "${temp}"
    mv -f "${temp}" "${file}"
}

# @description Print the backoff after the given number of failed launches: 60 s doubling, saturated at 1800 s
#   before it can overflow (U36 F5).
# @arg $1 int Failed launches in a row, at least 1.
backoff_seconds() {
    local delay=60 step=1
    while ((step < $1 && delay < 1800)); do
        delay=$((delay * 2))
        step=$((step + 1))
    done
    ((delay <= 1800)) || delay=1800
    printf '%s\n' "${delay}"
}

mode=start all=0
case ${1:-} in
--supervise)
    (($# == 1)) || refuse "${usage}"
    mode=supervise
    ;;
--stop)
    me=regime-stop
    case ${#}:${2:-} in
    1:) ;;
    2:--all) all=1 ;;
    *) refuse 'usage: regime-stop [--all]' ;;
    esac
    mode=stop
    ;;
*) (($# <= 1)) || refuse "${usage}" ;;
esac
command -v hcom > /dev/null || refuse 'hcom not found on PATH'
[[ -x ${LEVER_DIR}/hcom-seat ]] || refuse "hcom-seat is not beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/hcom-seat"
[[ -r ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env ]] || refuse "regime-env unreadable beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env"
# shellcheck source=scripts/orchestrator/regime-env
. "${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env"

if [[ ${mode} == supervise ]]; then
    # A pass that finds the lock held skips: the next one comes in 60 s.
    if ! take_lock try; then
        echo "regime-start: pid ${lock_holder} holds ${lock}; this pass skips" >&2
        exit 0
    fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    for conf in "${registry}"/*.conf; do
        [[ -f ${conf} ]] || continue
        newest=''
        read_registration "${conf}"
        if [[ -n ${reg_error} ]]; then
            echo "regime-start: skipped ${conf}: ${reg_error}" >&2
            if [[ ${reg_store} == /* && -d ${reg_store} ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path prefix test
                log_line "${reg_store}" "skipped ${conf}: ${reg_error}; nothing launched"
            fi
            continue
        fi
        top=${reg_top} store=${reg_store} team=${reg_team} program=${reg_program}
        seat=${reg_seat} base=${reg_base} fails=$((10#${reg_fails})) next=$((10#${reg_next}))
        export HCOM_DIR=${store} HCOM_TEAM=${team}
        if ! alive=$(alive_orchestrators); then
            log_line "${store}" "hcom list failed; nothing launched"
            continue
        fi
        if [[ -n ${alive} ]]; then
            read -r seat base <<< "${alive%%$'\n'*}"
            if ((fails != 0)) || [[ ${seat} != "${reg_seat}" ]]; then
                write_registration "${conf}" "toplevel=${top}" "hcom_dir=${store}" "hcom_team=${team}" "program=${program}" "seat=${seat}" "base=${base}" fails=0 next=0
            fi
            continue
        fi
        if ! stopped=$(hcom list --stopped "${base}" 9>&-); then
            log_line "${store}" "hcom list --stopped ${base} failed; nothing launched"
            continue
        fi
        # The named form ends with `Stop history (<n> events):` and one `<age>  [<reason> by:<who>]` line per event,
        # the newest marked `(latest)` (hcom 0.7.30 and 0.7.31, measured; 0.7.31 on 2026-10-24, U22b). A stop record
        # that cannot be read is no license.
        newest=$(grep -m1 -E '\[[^]]+\] \(latest\)$' <<< "${stopped}" || true)
        newest=${newest#"${newest%%[![:space:]]*}"}
        if [[ -z ${newest} ]]; then
            log_line "${store}" "cannot read the stop record of ${seat}; nothing launched"
            continue
        fi
        if [[ ${newest} == *"[killed by:cli] (latest)" ]]; then
            log_line "${store}" "${seat} was stopped with hcom kill; supervision of ${top} ends (registration removed)"
            rm -f "${conf}"
            continue
        fi
        if ((now < next)); then
            continue
        fi
        log_line "${store}" "no orchestrator alive (last seat ${seat}: ${newest}); relaunching from ${top}"
        if alive=$(launch_orchestrator "${top}" 2>> "${store}/supervisor.log"); then
            read -r seat base <<< "${alive}"
            log_line "${store}" "relaunched ${seat}"
            write_registration "${conf}" "toplevel=${top}" "hcom_dir=${store}" "hcom_team=${team}" "program=${program}" "seat=${seat}" "base=${base}" fails=0 next=0
        else
            ((fails >= 9999)) || fails=$((fails + 1))
            delay=$(backoff_seconds "${fails}")
            log_line "${store}" "relaunch failed (${fails} in a row); next attempt in ${delay} s"
            write_registration "${conf}" "toplevel=${top}" "hcom_dir=${store}" "hcom_team=${team}" "program=${program}" "seat=${seat}" "base=${base}" "fails=${fails}" "next=$((now + delay))"
        fi
    done
    exit 0
fi

# @description Choose the store and team of this checkout when it has no registration: an explicit pair, else the
#   dotfiles pre-move pair, else regime-env's derivation. A store whose `origin` names another checkout is refused,
#   an explicit one included (U36 F3).
choose_store() {
    local legacy=${HOME}/.local/state/hcom-regime recorded
    if [[ -z ${HCOM_DIR:-} && -z ${HCOM_TEAM:-} && ${slug} == dotfiles && ! -e ${HOME}/.local/state/hcom/dotfiles/origin && -f ${legacy}/hcom.db ]]; then
        # The dotfiles program before its one-time store move (README "Run a program in another repository").
        export HCOM_DIR=${legacy} HCOM_TEAM=regime
        echo "${me}: the dotfiles program has not moved its store yet; using HCOM_DIR=${HCOM_DIR} HCOM_TEAM=${HCOM_TEAM}" >&2
    fi
    regime_env "${me}" || exit 2
    [[ -d ${HCOM_DIR} ]] || refuse "the hcom store ${HCOM_DIR} does not exist; run regime-init <program> first or set an existing store"
    [[ ${HCOM_TEAM} =~ ${name_grammar} ]] || refuse "team '${HCOM_TEAM}' is outside ${name_grammar}"
    if [[ -e ${HCOM_DIR}/origin ]]; then
        recorded=$(cat "${HCOM_DIR}/origin") || refuse "cannot read ${HCOM_DIR}/origin"
        if [[ ${recorded} != "${top}" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both are pwd -P forms (regime-init, regime_toplevel)
            refuse "the store ${HCOM_DIR} belongs to ${recorded}, not ${top}"
        fi
    fi
}

top=$(regime_toplevel) || refuse "run ${me} inside the repository checkout"
slug=$(regime_slug "${top}") || refuse "cannot derive a repository slug from ${top}"
conf=$(registration_path "${top}" "${slug}") || refuse "cannot hash the toplevel ${top}"

if [[ ${mode} == stop ]]; then
    take_lock wait || refuse "pid ${lock_holder} still holds ${lock} after ${lock_wait} s; nothing changed"
    if [[ -e ${conf} ]]; then
        # The registered store wins: it is the one the supervisor would relaunch into.
        read_registration "${conf}"
        [[ -z ${reg_error} ]] || refuse "the registration ${conf} is unusable (${reg_error}); check it and remove it by hand; nothing changed"
        if [[ ${reg_top} != "${top}" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both are pwd -P forms
            refuse "the registration ${conf} names ${reg_top}, not ${top}; nothing changed"
        fi
        export HCOM_DIR=${reg_store} HCOM_TEAM=${reg_team}
    else
        choose_store
    fi
    listing=$(hcom list --format '{name} {tag} {status}' 9>&-) || refuse "cannot read the seats of ${HCOM_DIR} (hcom list failed); nothing changed"
    rm -f "${conf}"
    log_line "${HCOM_DIR}" "regime-stop: supervision of ${top} ended"
    failed=0 stopped=0
    while read -r name tag status; do
        [[ -n ${name} ]] || continue
        case ${status} in active | listening | blocked) ;; *) continue ;; esac
        ((all)) || [[ ${tag} == orchestrator ]] || continue
        if hcom kill "${name}" --go > /dev/null 9>&-; then
            echo "regime-stop: stopped ${name}"
            log_line "${HCOM_DIR}" "regime-stop: stopped ${name}"
            stopped=$((stopped + 1))
        else
            echo "regime-stop: hcom kill ${name} failed" >&2
            failed=1
        fi
    done <<< "${listing}"
    ((stopped || failed)) || echo "regime-stop: no seat to stop in ${HCOM_DIR}; supervision ended"
    exit "${failed}"
fi

program=${1:-}
[[ -z ${program} || ${program} =~ ${name_grammar} ]] || refuse "program '${program}' is outside ${name_grammar}"
choose_store
store_dir=''
if [[ -n ${program} ]]; then
    store_dir=${top}/.orchestration/orchestrate/${program}
    [[ -d ${store_dir} ]] || refuse "no program store ${store_dir}; run regime-init ${program} first"
fi
take_lock wait || refuse "pid ${lock_holder} still holds ${lock} after ${lock_wait} s; nothing changed"
# This checkout's own registration is replaced only for the same store and team (U36 F3).
if [[ -e ${conf} ]]; then
    read_registration "${conf}"
    [[ -z ${reg_error} ]] || refuse "the registration ${conf} is unusable (${reg_error}); check it, remove it, then run regime-start again"
    if [[ ${reg_store} != "${HCOM_DIR}" || ${reg_team} != "${HCOM_TEAM}" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both are the absolute store paths regime-start wrote
        refuse "this checkout is registered on the store ${reg_store} and team ${reg_team}; run regime-stop first to move it to ${HCOM_DIR} and ${HCOM_TEAM}"
    fi
fi
alive=$(alive_orchestrators) || refuse "cannot read the seats of ${HCOM_DIR} (hcom list failed)"
if [[ -n ${alive} ]]; then
    read -r seat base <<< "${alive%%$'\n'*}"
    state="is already alive"
    log_line "${HCOM_DIR}" "regime-start found ${seat} alive; registered for the supervisor"
else
    alive=$(launch_orchestrator "${top}") || {
        log_line "${HCOM_DIR}" "regime-start could not launch the orchestrator from ${top}"
        exit 1
    }
    read -r seat base <<< "${alive}"
    state="is listening"
    log_line "${HCOM_DIR}" "regime-start launched ${seat} from ${top}"
fi
write_registration "${conf}" "toplevel=${top}" "hcom_dir=${HCOM_DIR}" "hcom_team=${HCOM_TEAM}" "program=${program}" "seat=${seat}" "base=${base}" fails=0 next=0
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # the backticks are text: the pane's name, set off for the reader
printf '%s %s on team %s. Type your instruction in the pane `orchestrator`; the store is %s.\n' \
    "${seat}" "${state}" "${HCOM_TEAM}" "${store_dir:-${HCOM_DIR}}"
</code></pre>

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file regime-stop
# @brief Stop a program's orchestrator seat on purpose and end its supervision.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U36. Run in the repository checkout. It is `regime-start --stop` (the regime-start beside this
#   file), so it takes the same host lock as regime-start and its supervisor pass and never interleaves with a
#   relaunch. Under that lock it reads this checkout's own registration (`~/.local/state/regime-supervisor/
#   <slug>-<hash of the toplevel>.conf`, which must name this toplevel), removes it, then runs
#   `hcom kill <name> --go` for every alive seat tagged `orchestrator` in the registered store (with `--all`, for
#   every alive seat in that store), and logs each step in `<store>/supervisor.log`. Without a registration it uses
#   the store regime-start would choose (an explicit HCOM_DIR and HCOM_TEAM, the dotfiles pre-move pair, else
#   regime-env), and a store whose `origin` names another checkout is refused. A seat's worktree and branch stay; a
#   later `regime-start` starts the program again.
# @option --all Also stop the worker seats of the store.
# @stdout One line per seat stopped, or that none was alive.
# @exitcode 0 Stopped, or nothing was alive.
# @exitcode 1 An hcom kill failed (the registration is already removed).
# @exitcode 2 A refusal, before anything is changed.
# @example
#   regime-stop
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
# @set LEVER_DIR The physical directory of this file, where the sourced regime-env helper sits (U33).
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    LEVER_DIR=${dir}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

[[ -x ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-start ]] || {
    echo "regime-stop: regime-start is not beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-start" >&2
    exit 2
}
exec "${LEVER_DIR}/regime-start" --stop "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""regime-url-opener: open a seat host's sign-in URL in this laptop's default browser (regime-cutover U37).

A seat on a remote host (Ubuntu, reached through `herdr --remote` over SSH) cannot open a browser, and the
vendors' sign-in flows end in a browser consent. The SSH host entry tagged `seat-host` carries
`RemoteForward 127.0.0.1:1456 127.0.0.1:1456`, so the remote `regime-open-url <url>` reaches this
loopback listener (docs/remote-host-logins.md). launchd starts it
(`~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.mryfmo.dotfiles.url-opener.plist`).

It accepts exactly one request shape, `POST /open` with the header `X-Regime-Open: 1` and the URL as the
body, and opens the URL only when it is `https` on an allow-listed sign-in host with no user info and no
port but 443. The header keeps a web page in this browser from posting here, since a cross-origin request
with a custom header needs a CORS preflight this server never answers. Every request is logged to
`~/.local/state/hcom/url-opener.log` with the decision and the URL's scheme, host and path only, never
its query. It binds 127.0.0.1 only and never runs a shell.

launchd sends its stdout and stderr to /dev/null, because launchd opens those files before Python starts
and a fresh home has no log directory yet. The start, a failed bind and every request therefore go to the
log file, whose parent this script creates before it binds.

Usage: regime-url-opener [--port 1456] [--log PATH]
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime
import http.server
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import urllib.parse
from pathlib import Path

# The sign-in hosts of the two seat routes: SIWC (`auth.openai.com`) and Claude Code's `claude auth login`
# (`claude.com/cai/oauth/authorize`, measured 2026-10-24 with Claude Code 2.1.309) and its Console flow.
ALLOWED_HOSTS = frozenset(
    {"auth.openai.com", "claude.ai", "claude.com", "console.anthropic.com", "platform.claude.com"}
)
MAX_BODY = 8192
HEADER = "X-Regime-Open"


def utc_now() -> str:
    # datetime.UTC is Python 3.11+; launchd runs /usr/bin/python3, which is 3.9 on this macOS.
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")  # noqa: UP017


def check_url(text: str) -> tuple[str | None, str]:
    """Return (reason it is refused or None, the scheme://host/path to log)."""
    if not text or any(ch.isspace() or ord(ch) < 32 or ord(ch) == 127 for ch in text):
        return "not one URL", ""
    try:
        parts = urllib.parse.urlsplit(text)
        port = parts.port
    except ValueError:
        return "not a URL", ""
    host = (parts.hostname or "").lower()
    shown = f"{parts.scheme}://{host}{parts.path}"
    if parts.scheme != "https":
        return "not https", shown
    if parts.username is not None or parts.password is not None:
        return "user info in the URL", shown
    if port not in (None, 443):
        return f"port {port}", shown
    if host not in ALLOWED_HOSTS:
        return "host not on the allow-list", shown
    return None, shown


def opener() -> str | None:
    return shutil.which("open" if sys.platform == "darwin" else "xdg-open")


def append_log(path: Path, entry: str) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o700)
    with open(path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as log:
        log.write(f"{utc_now()} {entry}\n")


class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    server_version = "regime-url-opener"
    log_path: Path

    def log_message(self, format: str, *args: object) -> None:
        return None  # the decision log below is the only record

    def record(self, decision: str, shown: str = "") -> None:
        append_log(self.log_path, f"{decision}{' ' + shown if shown else ''}")

    def reply(self, status: int, text: str) -> None:
        body = (text + "\n").encode()
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/plain; charset=utf-8")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def do_GET(self) -> None:
        self.record("refused method GET")
        self.reply(405, "POST /open only")

    def do_POST(self) -> None:
        if self.path != "/open":  # lint-comparisons: allow an HTTP request target, not a filesystem path
            self.record(f"refused path {self.path[:80]!r}")
            self.reply(404, "POST /open only")
            return
        if self.headers.get(HEADER) != "1":
            self.record(f"refused missing {HEADER} header")
            self.reply(403, f"the {HEADER}: 1 header is required")
            return
        try:
            length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", ""))
        except ValueError:
            length = -1
        if length < 0 or length > MAX_BODY:
            self.record("refused body length")
            self.reply(413, f"the body must be one URL of at most {MAX_BODY} bytes")
            return
        try:
            url = self.rfile.read(length).decode("utf-8").strip()
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            self.record("refused body not UTF-8")
            self.reply(400, "the body must be one UTF-8 URL")
            return
        reason, shown = check_url(url)
        if reason:
            self.record(f"refused {reason}", shown)
            self.reply(403 if shown else 400, f"refused: {reason}")
            return
        command = opener()
        if command is None:
            self.record("failed no opener on PATH", shown)
            self.reply(502, "no `open` or `xdg-open` on PATH")
            return
        result = subprocess.run([command, url], stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, capture_output=True, check=False)
        if result.returncode != 0:
            self.record(f"failed opener exit {result.returncode}", shown)
            self.reply(502, f"the opener exited {result.returncode}")
            return
        self.record("opened", shown)
        self.reply(200, "opened")


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="regime-url-opener")
    parser.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=int(os.environ.get("REGIME_URL_OPENER_PORT", "1456")))
    parser.add_argument("--log", type=Path, default=Path.home() / ".local/state/hcom/url-opener.log")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    Handler.log_path = args.log
    try:
        args.log.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o700)
    except OSError as error:
        print(f"regime-url-opener: cannot create the log directory {args.log.parent}: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    try:
        server = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", args.port), Handler)
    except OSError as error:
        append_log(args.log, f"failed to bind 127.0.0.1:{args.port}: {error.strerror or error}")
        print(f"regime-url-opener: cannot bind 127.0.0.1:{args.port}: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    host, port = server.server_address[:2]
    append_log(args.log, f"listening on {host}:{port}")
    print(f"regime-url-opener: listening on {host}:{port}", flush=True)
    try:
        server.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        server.server_close()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
