#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file remove-agent-asset
# @brief Remove one installed agent asset step from its recorded manifest entry.
# @description
#   Defaults to a non-mutating dry run. Actual removal requires `--yes`, and
#   file deletion is limited to normalized paths recorded by the selected step
#   under fixed agent-asset roots. Final symlinks are removed without following
#   their targets.
# @arg $1 string Manifest step name.
# @option --dry-run Print exact inverse operations without executing them.
# @option --yes Execute the guarded inverse operations and remove the step record.

set -Eeuo pipefail

readonly MANIFEST_PATH="${HOME}/.agents/.installed-manifest.json"
readonly CODEX_ASSET_ROOT="${CODEX_HOME:-${HOME}/.codex}"

declare -a RECORDED_PATHS=()
declare -a RECORDED_COMMANDS=()
ENTRY=""
MODE="dry-run"
STEP=""

#
# @description Print command usage.
#
function usage() {
    printf 'Usage: remove-agent-asset <step-name> [--dry-run|--yes]\n' >&2
}

#
# @description Print an error and return failure.
# @arg $@ string Error message words.
#
function fail() {
    printf 'ERROR: %s\n' "$*" >&2
    return 1
}

#
# @description Return success when a command is available.
# @arg $1 string Command name.
#
function has_command() {
    command -v "$1" > /dev/null 2>&1
}

#
# @description Normalize a path while leaving its final symlink unresolved.
# @arg $1 path Absolute path to normalize.
#
function normalize_action_path() {
    python3 - "$1" << 'PY'
import os
import sys

path = os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(sys.argv[1]))
print(os.path.join(os.path.realpath(os.path.dirname(path)), os.path.basename(path)))
PY
}

#
# @description Resolve a trusted directory root including its final symlink.
# @arg $1 path Directory root to normalize.
#
function normalize_root_path() {
    python3 - "$1" << 'PY'
import os
import sys

print(os.path.realpath(os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(sys.argv[1]))))
PY
}

#
# @description Return success when a path equals or descends from a prefix, both folded by os.path.normpath first.
# @arg $1 path Candidate path.
# @arg $2 path Prefix path.
# @arg $3 string Optional `strict`, which refuses the prefix itself.
#
function path_has_prefix() {
    python3 -I -c 'import os, sys; p, q = map(os.path.normpath, sys.argv[1:3]); sys.exit(not (p.startswith(q + os.sep) or p == q and sys.argv[3:] != ["strict"]))' "$@"
}

#
# @description Return success when a normalized path is under a fixed removable asset root.
# @arg $1 path Normalized candidate path.
#
function path_is_in_safe_root() {
    local candidate="$1"
    local root

    for root in \
        "${HOME}/.agents" \
        "${HOME}/.claude/plugins/cache" \
        "${CODEX_ASSET_ROOT}/plugins/cache" \
        "${CODEX_ASSET_ROOT}/.tmp/plugins/plugins" \
        "${HOME}/.local/share/mise/installs" \
        "${HOME}/.local/share/agent-assets"; do
        root="$(normalize_root_path "${root}")" || return 1
        if path_has_prefix "${candidate}" "${root}" strict; then
            return 0
        fi
    done

    for root in \
        "${CODEX_ASSET_ROOT}/plugins/crit" \
        "${HOME}/.understand-anything/repo"; do
        root="$(normalize_root_path "${root}")" || return 1
        if path_has_prefix "${candidate}" "${root}"; then
            return 0
        fi
    done

    for root in \
        "${HOME}/.claude/hooks/herdr-agent-state.sh" \
        "${CODEX_ASSET_ROOT}/herdr-agent-state.sh" \
        "${HOME}/.local/bin/hcom"; do
        root="$(normalize_action_path "${root}")" || return 1
        [ "${candidate}" = "${root}" ] && return 0 # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are normalize_action_path forms
    done
    return 1
}

#
# @description Return success when a deletion path stays inside a recorded prefix and a fixed safe root.
# @arg $1 path Candidate deletion path.
# @stdout Prints the normalized deletion path on success.
#
function guard_deletion_path() {
    local candidate recorded normalized_recorded
    candidate="$(normalize_action_path "$1")" || return 1

    if ! path_is_in_safe_root "${candidate}"; then
        fail "refusing path outside allowed asset roots: ${candidate}"
        return 1
    fi
    for recorded in "${RECORDED_PATHS[@]}"; do
        normalized_recorded="$(normalize_action_path "${recorded}")" || continue
        if path_has_prefix "${candidate}" "${normalized_recorded}"; then
            printf '%s\n' "${candidate}"
            return 0
        fi
    done
    fail "refusing path outside recorded manifest prefixes: ${candidate}"
}

#
# @description Print and optionally execute one inverse command.
# @arg $@ string Command and arguments.
#
function run_operation() {
    if [ "${MODE}" = "dry-run" ]; then
        printf 'DRY-RUN:'
    else
        printf 'REMOVE:'
    fi
    printf ' %q' "$@"
    printf '\n'
    [ "${MODE}" = "dry-run" ] || "$@"
}

#
# @description Remove one guarded manifest-recorded filesystem path.
# @arg $1 path Recorded target path.
#
function remove_recorded_path() {
    local target
    target="$(guard_deletion_path "$1")" || return 1
    if [ -L "${target}" ] || [ -f "${target}" ]; then
        run_operation rm -f -- "${target}"
    else
        run_operation rm -rf -- "${target}"
    fi
}

#
# @description Validate every filesystem path before the first destructive operation.
# @arg $@ path Recorded target paths.
#
function preflight_deletion_paths() {
    local path
    for path in "$@"; do
        guard_deletion_path "${path}" > /dev/null
    done
}

#
# @description Remove a preflighted list of manifest-recorded paths.
# @arg $@ path Recorded target paths.
#
function remove_recorded_paths() {
    local path
    preflight_deletion_paths "$@"
    for path in "$@"; do
        remove_recorded_path "${path}"
    done
}

#
# @description Return success when a recorded path is plugin cache or plugin data, not shared config.
# @arg $1 path Recorded path.
#
function is_plugin_data_path() {
    local candidate root
    candidate="$(normalize_action_path "$1")" || return 1
    for root in \
        "${HOME}/.claude/plugins/cache" \
        "${CODEX_ASSET_ROOT}/plugins/cache" \
        "${CODEX_ASSET_ROOT}/.tmp/plugins/plugins"; do
        root="$(normalize_root_path "${root}")" || return 1
        if path_has_prefix "${candidate}" "${root}" strict; then
            return 0
        fi
    done
    root="$(normalize_root_path "${CODEX_ASSET_ROOT}/plugins/crit")" || return 1
    path_has_prefix "${candidate}" "${root}"
}

#
# @description Return success for shared plugin config files that must never be removed wholesale.
# @arg $1 path Recorded path.
#
function is_plugin_config_path() {
    local candidate settings_path config_path
    candidate="$(normalize_action_path "$1")" || return 1
    settings_path="$(normalize_action_path "${HOME}/.claude/settings.json")" || return 1
    config_path="$(normalize_action_path "${CODEX_ASSET_ROOT}/config.toml")" || return 1
    [ "${candidate}" = "${settings_path}" ] || [ "${candidate}" = "${config_path}" ] # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are normalize_action_path forms
}

#
# @description Remove guarded plugin data when the owning CLI has no usable uninstall.
#
function remove_plugin_data_paths() {
    local path
    local -a data_paths=()
    for path in "${RECORDED_PATHS[@]}"; do
        if is_plugin_data_path "${path}"; then
            data_paths+=("${path}")
        elif ! is_plugin_config_path "${path}"; then
            fail "plugin entry contains an unrecognized fallback path: ${path}"
            return 1
        fi
    done
    [ "${#data_paths[@]}" -gt 0 ] || {
        fail "plugin entry has no guarded cache/data fallback: ${STEP}"
        return 1
    }
    remove_recorded_paths "${data_paths[@]}"
}

#
# @description Execute the inverse for a plugin manifest entry.
#
function remove_plugin() {
    local command owner="" plugin_id="" candidate_owner candidate_id

    for command in "${RECORDED_COMMANDS[@]}"; do
        candidate_owner=""
        candidate_id=""
        case "${command}" in
        "claude plugin install "*)
            candidate_owner="claude"
            candidate_id="${command#claude plugin install }"
            ;;
        "claude plugin update "*)
            candidate_owner="claude"
            candidate_id="${command#claude plugin update }"
            ;;
        "codex plugin add "*)
            candidate_owner="codex"
            candidate_id="${command#codex plugin add }"
            ;;
        "crit install codex-plugin" | "crit install codex-plugin "*)
            candidate_owner="crit"
            candidate_id="codex-plugin"
            ;;
        esac
        [ -n "${candidate_owner}" ] || continue
        if [ -n "${owner}" ] && { [ "${owner}" != "${candidate_owner}" ] || [ "${plugin_id}" != "${candidate_id}" ]; }; then
            fail "ambiguous plugin owner or id for step: ${STEP}"
            return 1
        fi
        owner="${candidate_owner}"
        plugin_id="${candidate_id}"
    done

    [[ "${plugin_id}" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.@/+:-]+$ ]] || {
        fail "missing or unsafe plugin id for step: ${STEP}"
        return 1
    }
    case "${owner}" in
    claude)
        if has_command claude; then
            run_operation claude plugin uninstall "${plugin_id}"
        else
            remove_plugin_data_paths
        fi
        ;;
    codex)
        if has_command codex; then
            run_operation codex plugin remove "${plugin_id}"
        else
            remove_plugin_data_paths
        fi
        ;;
    crit)
        # Crit exposes install but no uninstall command; remove only its recorded data root.
        remove_plugin_data_paths
        ;;
    *)
        fail "unknown plugin owner for step: ${STEP}"
        return 1
        ;;
    esac
}

#
# @description Execute the inverse for a Brew manifest entry.
#
function remove_brew() {
    local command formula="" candidate
    for command in "${RECORDED_COMMANDS[@]}"; do
        case "${command}" in
        "brew install "*)
            candidate="${command#brew install }"
            if [ -n "${formula}" ] && [ "${formula}" != "${candidate}" ]; then
                fail "ambiguous brew formula for step: ${STEP}"
                return 1
            fi
            formula="${candidate}"
            ;;
        esac
    done
    [[ "${formula}" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9@+._-]+$ ]] || {
        fail "missing or unsafe brew formula for step: ${STEP}"
        return 1
    }
    if [ "${MODE}" = "yes" ] && ! has_command brew; then
        fail "brew command not found"
        return 1
    fi
    run_operation brew uninstall "${formula}"
}

#
# @description Execute the inverse for a Herdr integration manifest entry.
#
function remove_integration() {
    local command integration
    local -a integrations=()
    for command in "${RECORDED_COMMANDS[@]}"; do
        case "${command}" in
        "herdr integration install "*)
            integration="${command#herdr integration install }"
            [[ "${integration}" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || {
                fail "unsafe Herdr integration name for step: ${STEP}"
                return 1
            }
            integrations+=("${integration}")
            ;;
        esac
    done
    if [ "${#integrations[@]}" -gt 0 ] && has_command herdr && herdr integration uninstall --help > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        for integration in "${integrations[@]}"; do
            run_operation herdr integration uninstall "${integration}"
        done
        return 0
    fi
    [ "${#RECORDED_PATHS[@]}" -gt 0 ] || {
        fail "integration entry has no guarded fallback paths: ${STEP}"
        return 1
    }
    remove_recorded_paths "${RECORDED_PATHS[@]}"
}

#
# @description Atomically remove the completed step from the manifest.
#
function remove_manifest_step() {
    if [ "${MODE}" = "dry-run" ]; then
        printf 'DRY-RUN: remove manifest step %s\n' "${STEP}"
        return 0
    fi

    local temporary_path
    temporary_path="$(mktemp "${MANIFEST_PATH}.tmp.XXXXXX")"
    chmod 600 "${temporary_path}"
    if ! jq --arg step "${STEP}" 'del(.steps[$step])' "${MANIFEST_PATH}" > "${temporary_path}"; then
        rm -f "${temporary_path}"
        return 1
    fi
    if ! mv "${temporary_path}" "${MANIFEST_PATH}"; then
        rm -f "${temporary_path}"
        return 1
    fi
    printf 'REMOVE: manifest step %s\n' "${STEP}"
}

#
# @description Load and validate the selected manifest entry.
#
function load_entry() {
    [ -f "${MANIFEST_PATH}" ] || {
        fail "installed asset manifest not found: ${MANIFEST_PATH}"
        return 1
    }
    jq -e '.version == 1 and (.steps | type == "object")' "${MANIFEST_PATH}" > /dev/null || {
        fail "invalid installed asset manifest: ${MANIFEST_PATH}"
        return 1
    }
    if ! ENTRY="$(jq -ce --arg step "${STEP}" '.steps[$step] // empty' "${MANIFEST_PATH}")"; then
        ENTRY=""
    fi
    if [ -z "${ENTRY}" ]; then
        printf 'ERROR: unknown manifest step: %s\n' "${STEP}" >&2
        local known_steps
        known_steps="$(jq -r '.steps | keys | join(", ")' "${MANIFEST_PATH}")" || {
            fail "cannot list the steps of ${MANIFEST_PATH}"
            return 1
        }
        printf 'Known steps: %s\n' "${known_steps}" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "${ENTRY}" | jq -e '
        (.kind | type == "string") and
        (.paths | type == "array" and all(.[]; type == "string")) and
        (.commands | type == "array" and all(.[]; type == "string"))
    ' > /dev/null || {
        fail "invalid manifest entry: ${STEP}"
        return 1
    }

    local value values
    values="$(jq -r '.paths[]' <<< "${ENTRY}")" || {
        fail "cannot read the recorded paths of manifest entry: ${STEP}"
        return 1
    }
    while IFS= read -r value; do
        [ -z "${value}" ] || RECORDED_PATHS+=("${value}")
    done <<< "${values}"
    values="$(jq -r '.commands[]' <<< "${ENTRY}")" || {
        fail "cannot read the recorded commands of manifest entry: ${STEP}"
        return 1
    }
    while IFS= read -r value; do
        [ -z "${value}" ] || RECORDED_COMMANDS+=("${value}")
    done <<< "${values}"
}

#
# @description Remove hcom: uv uninstalls its tool environment and receipt, then the recorded binary and wheel go.
#
function remove_hcom() {
    local tools=""
    if has_command uv; then
        tools="$(uv tool dir --color never)" || return 1 # herdr panes export FORCE_COLOR and CLICOLOR_FORCE
    elif [ "${MODE}" = "yes" ]; then
        fail "uv command not found, so hcom's uv tool environment and receipt cannot be uninstalled; nothing was removed"
        return 1
    fi
    preflight_deletion_paths "${RECORDED_PATHS[@]}"
    # An hcom uv no longer has (uninstalled by hand or by an earlier run) must not stop the rest of the removal.
    if [ -z "${tools}" ] || [ -d "${tools}/hcom" ]; then
        run_operation uv tool uninstall hcom
    else
        printf 'SKIP: uv has no hcom tool environment under %s\n' "${tools}"
    fi
    remove_recorded_paths "${RECORDED_PATHS[@]}"
}

#
# @description Parse arguments and perform the selected inverse operation.
# @arg $@ string Command-line arguments.
#
function main() {
    if [ "$#" -lt 1 ] || [ "$#" -gt 2 ]; then
        usage
        return 2
    fi
    STEP="$1"
    case "${2:---dry-run}" in
    --dry-run) MODE="dry-run" ;;
    --yes) MODE="yes" ;;
    *)
        usage
        return 2
        ;;
    esac

    load_entry
    local kind
    kind="$(printf '%s\n' "${ENTRY}" | jq -r '.kind')"
    case "${kind}" in
    plugin)
        remove_plugin
        ;;
    rsync | installer)
        [ "${#RECORDED_PATHS[@]}" -gt 0 ] || {
            fail "manifest step has no removal paths: ${STEP}"
            return 1
        }
        if [ "${STEP}" = "update_hcom" ]; then
            remove_hcom
        else
            remove_recorded_paths "${RECORDED_PATHS[@]}"
        fi
        ;;
    brew)
        remove_brew
        ;;
    integration)
        remove_integration
        ;;
    *)
        fail "unsupported manifest kind for step ${STEP}: ${kind}"
        return 1
        ;;
    esac
    remove_manifest_step
}

main "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file seat-login-preflight
# @brief Report each omp seat profile's login on this host, and before a seat starts on a remote host, get its route logged in.
# @description
#   regime-cutover U37 (docs/remote-host-logins.md). A seat's model route is the provider of
#   `modelRoles.default` in its deployed overlay `~/.agents/omp/profiles/<profile>.yml`: `openai-siwc`
#   (SIWC, the audit side) or `claude-bridge` (the Claude Code child). A login is per host, so a seat on
#   the Ubuntu host reached through `herdr --remote` needs that host's own login, and the browser for it
#   is on the laptop.
#
#   `--check [<profile>...]` prints one line per profile (all overlays when none is named) from metadata
#   only, never a token: SIWC is `registration.json` (host id and issued client id, which carry no token),
#   held to the extension's record schema (one JSON document), plus the mtime of the profile's `agent.db`; Claude is the
#   `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` variable, the credentials file, the macOS Keychain item (attributes only), or
#   the token file a login shell exports. A record that exists but cannot be read or breaks its schema, and
#   a producer (`uname`, `stat`, `date`, `security`) that fails, are reported as unreadable, never as
#   absent, and make the exit status 1.
#
#   `<profile>` (a seat profile of the manifest's `omp.roles`: orchestrator, worker, audit, review or
#   security; `hcom-seat` calls it with the seat's role before it creates or starts anything) does nothing
#   on a local host. On a remote host (`SSH_CONNECTION` set, or a Linux host without a display, which a
#   herdr pane on the seat host can be even when its server did not inherit `SSH_CONNECTION`) it checks
#   that a seat can use the login, which is more than `--check` shows. SIWC needs an active `openai-siwc`
#   login in `agent.db`, counted by the extension's `src/credentials.ts` without reading a token: the
#   issued client is saved before the token exchange, so a record proves only that a sign-in began.
#   Claude needs the variable in this environment, the credentials file or the Keychain item; a token file
#   this shell has not exported is refused with the instruction to open a new login shell, since Claude
#   Code reads the variable and never that file. An absent
#   login is logged in here only in the operator's own terminal (stdin and stdout a TTY, not inside a seat):
#   SIWC through `omp --profile <profile> login openai-siwc` with `OPENAI_SIWC_CALLBACK_PORT=1455`, which
#   the `seat-host` SSH entry forwards back from the laptop, and `xdg-open`/`open` pointed at
#   `regime-open-url` for that command only; Claude through `claude auth login` with
#   `BROWSER=regime-open-url`, whose callback port is random, so the browser shows a code the operator
#   pastes into the pane. The consent click and that paste are the human steps. Anywhere else (a seat, a
#   script) it prints the command and refuses, since a login is the operator's step (standing order 4).
# @arg $1 string `--check`, or the profile.
# @arg $@ string With `--check`: profile names (default: every deployed overlay).
# @env SSH_CONNECTION Set by sshd: this host is remote to the operator's terminal.
# @env DISPLAY With WAYLAND_DISPLAY: a Linux host with neither has no local browser, so it counts as remote.
# @env HCOM_LAUNCHED Set by hcom inside a seat: never run a login there.
# @env CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN Claude Code's token; only its presence is tested.
# @stdout With `--check`: one line per profile.
# @stderr The profile mode's report and refusals.
# @exitcode 0 Checked, or the profile's route is usable (or the host is local).
# @exitcode 1 A record or producer is unreadable, or a login ran and the route is still not usable.
# @exitcode 2 A usage error, a remote seat without a login outside the operator's terminal, or a token file
#   this shell has not exported.
# @example
#   seat-login-preflight --check
#   seat-login-preflight audit
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

profiles_dir=${HOME}/.agents/omp/profiles
siwc_ext=${HOME}/.agents/omp/extensions/openai-siwc
token_file=${HOME}/.config/claude-code/oauth-token
callback_port=1455
# The seat profiles, the values of `omp.roles` in home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml.
seat_profiles=(orchestrator worker audit review security)
# openai-siwc `src/store.ts`: `JSON.parse` of the whole file, so exactly one top-level document (jq reads a stream, so
# `-s` gathers every document and the filter requires one), then `isRegistration`, with the issued client id held to
# the charset `src/seed.ts` accepts, so nothing else reaches the terminal. \A and \z anchor the whole string.
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # jq source, not shell
registration_filter='
if length != 1 then error("not exactly one JSON document")
else .[0]
    | if type == "object"
        and (.hostId | type == "string"
            and test("\\Aurn:uuid:[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}\\z"))
        and ((has("clientId") | not) or (.clientId | type == "string" and test("\\A[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,200}\\z")))
        and ((has("accountId") | not) or (.accountId | type == "string" and length > 0))
    then [.hostId, (.clientId // "")] | @tsv
    else error("not a registration record")
    end
end'
# The login's scratch overlay and opener shims, removed on every exit.
scratch=""
trap '[[ -z ${scratch} ]] || rm -rf -- "${scratch}"' EXIT

die() {
    printf 'seat-login-preflight: %s\n' "$*" >&2
    exit "${2:-2}"
}

# Every decision below that depends on the system reads this once, so a failed `uname` stops here.
os=$(uname -s) || die 'cannot read the system name: uname -s failed' 1
[[ -n ${os} ]] || die 'cannot read the system name: uname -s printed nothing' 1

# @description Print a file's mtime in UTC; GNU and BSD `date -r <file>` agree on this form.
# @arg $1 path File.
# @exitcode 2 `date` failed or printed nothing.
stamp() {
    local value
    value=$(date -u -r "$1" +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) || return 2
    [[ -n ${value} ]] || return 2
    printf '%s\n' "${value}"
}

# @description Print a file's permission bits in octal.
# @arg $1 path File.
# @exitcode 2 `stat` failed or printed no mode.
mode_of() {
    local value
    if [[ ${os} == Darwin ]]; then
        value=$(stat -f %Lp "$1") || return 2
    else
        value=$(stat -c %a "$1") || return 2
    fi
    [[ ${value} =~ ^[0-7]{3,4}$ ]] || return 2
    printf '%s\n' "${value}"
}

# @description Print the provider of a profile's `modelRoles.default` (openai-siwc, claude-bridge, ...).
# @arg $1 string Profile name.
# @exitcode 2 The overlay exists but cannot be read.
# @exitcode 3 The overlay is absent or names no default model with a provider.
route_of() {
    local overlay=${profiles_dir}/$1.yml model
    [[ -f ${overlay} ]] || return 3
    model=$(awk '/^modelRoles:/ { in_roles = 1; next } /^[^ ]/ { in_roles = 0 } in_roles && $1 == "default:" { print $2; exit }' "${overlay}") || return 2
    # A model id without a provider prefix leaves the prefix strip unchanged.
    [[ -n ${model} && ${model%%/*} != "${model}" ]] || return 3
    printf '%s\n' "${model%%/*}"
}

# @description Print the SIWC login line of a profile.
# @arg $1 string Profile name.
# @arg $2 int 1 to also require an active login in agent.db (launch readiness), else metadata only.
# @exitcode 0 Registered with an issued client and an agent.db (and, with $2=1, a login in it). 1 Absent. 2 Unreadable.
siwc_state() {
    local profile=$1 ready=${2:-0} agent reg fields host client db mtime count
    agent=${HOME}/.omp/profiles/${profile}/agent
    reg=${agent}/openai-siwc/registration.json
    db=${agent}/agent.db
    if [[ ! -e ${reg} ]]; then
        printf 'absent (no %s)\n' "${reg}"
        return 1
    fi
    if ! fields=$(jq -ers "${registration_filter}" "${reg}" 2> /dev/null); then
        printf 'unreadable (%s)\n' "${reg}"
        return 2
    fi
    IFS=$'\t' read -r host client <<< "${fields}"
    if [[ -z ${client} ]]; then
        printf 'absent (registration started, no issued client yet: host %s)\n' "${host}"
        return 1
    fi
    if [[ ! -f ${db} ]]; then
        printf 'absent (registered: host %s, client %s; no %s)\n' "${host}" "${client}" "${db}"
        return 1
    fi
    if ! mtime=$(stamp "${db}"); then
        printf 'unreadable (cannot read the mtime of %s)\n' "${db}"
        return 2
    fi
    if ((ready)); then
        if ! count=$(bun "${siwc_ext}/src/credentials.ts" --profile "${profile}") || [[ ! ${count} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
            printf 'unreadable (cannot count the openai-siwc logins in %s)\n' "${db}"
            return 2
        fi
        if ((count == 0)); then
            printf 'absent (registered: host %s, client %s; no openai-siwc login in %s)\n' "${host}" "${client}" "${db}"
            return 1
        fi
    fi
    printf 'registered (host %s, client %s), agent.db mtime %s\n' "${host}" "${client}" "${mtime}"
}

# @description Print the Claude Code login line of this host (the bridge child uses the host login).
# @arg $1 int 1 to require a login Claude Code can use from this environment (launch readiness).
# @exitcode 0 Present. 1 Absent. 2 Unreadable. 4 Only a token file this shell has not exported (with $1=1).
claude_state() {
    local ready=${1:-0} credentials=${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-${HOME}/.claude}/.credentials.json mode mtime status=0
    if [[ -n ${CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN:-} ]]; then
        printf 'login present (env token)\n'
        return 0
    fi
    if [[ -f ${credentials} ]]; then
        if ! mode=$(mode_of "${credentials}") || ! mtime=$(stamp "${credentials}"); then
            printf 'unreadable (cannot read the mode or mtime of %s)\n' "${credentials}"
            return 2
        fi
        printf 'login present (credentials file %s, mtime %s)\n' "${mode}" "${mtime}"
        return 0
    fi
    if [[ ${os} == Darwin ]]; then
        # Exit 44 is security's "item not found"; any other failure is a failed read.
        security find-generic-password -s 'Claude Code-credentials' > /dev/null 2>&1 || status=$?
        case ${status} in
        0)
            printf 'login present (Keychain item)\n'
            return 0
            ;;
        44) ;;
        *)
            printf 'unreadable (security find-generic-password exited %s)\n' "${status}"
            return 2
            ;;
        esac
    fi
    if [[ -s ${token_file} ]]; then
        if ! mode=$(mode_of "${token_file}") || ! mtime=$(stamp "${token_file}"); then
            printf 'unreadable (cannot read the mode or mtime of %s)\n' "${token_file}"
            return 2
        fi
        if ((ready)); then
            printf 'login not in this environment (token file %s, mtime %s; CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is unset here)\n' "${mode}" "${mtime}"
            return 4
        fi
        printf 'login present (token file %s, mtime %s; a new login shell exports it)\n' "${mode}" "${mtime}"
        return 0
    fi
    printf 'absent\n'
    return 1
}

# @description Print `<profile> <route>: <state>` for one profile.
# @arg $1 string Profile name.
# @arg $2 int 1 for launch readiness (the profile mode), else metadata only (`--check`).
# @exitcode 0 Logged in. 1 Absent. 2 Unreadable. 3 No seat login route, so nothing to log in. 4 Token not exported.
profile_line() {
    local route state status=0 ready=${2:-0}
    route=$(route_of "$1") || status=$?
    case ${status} in
    0) ;;
    2)
        printf '%s: unreadable (%s)\n' "$1" "${profiles_dir}/$1.yml"
        return 2
        ;;
    *)
        printf '%s: no route (overlay %s absent or without modelRoles.default)\n' "$1" "${profiles_dir}/$1.yml"
        return 3
        ;;
    esac
    case ${route} in
    openai-siwc) state=$(siwc_state "$1" "${ready}") || status=$? ;;
    claude-bridge) state=$(claude_state "${ready}") || status=$? ;;
    *) state="not a seat login route" status=3 ;;
    esac
    printf '%s %s: %s\n' "$1" "${route}" "${state}"
    return "${status}"
}

# @description `--check`: one line per profile, exit 1 when any record is unreadable.
check() {
    local profile overlay failed=0 status
    local -a profiles=("$@")
    if ((${#profiles[@]} == 0)); then
        for overlay in "${profiles_dir}"/*.yml; do
            # Parameter expansion, so no external producer (basename) can fail unseen.
            [[ -f ${overlay} ]] || continue
            overlay=${overlay##*/}
            profiles+=("${overlay%.yml}")
        done
    fi
    if ((${#profiles[@]} == 0)); then
        printf 'not applicable: no omp seat profiles under %s\n' "${profiles_dir}"
        return 0
    fi
    for profile in "${profiles[@]}"; do
        status=0
        profile_line "${profile}" || status=$?
        ((status == 2)) && failed=1
    done
    return "${failed}"
}

# @description Name the laptop this SSH session comes from, from the tailnet when it knows the address.
peer_name() {
    local client=${SSH_CONNECTION%% *} name=""
    if [[ -n ${client} ]] && command -v tailscale > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        name=$(tailscale status --json 2> /dev/null | jq -r --arg ip "${client}" \
            'first(.Peer[]? | select(any(.TailscaleIPs[]?; . == $ip)) | .DNSName) // empty' 2> /dev/null) || name=""
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "${name:-${client:-the laptop of the seat-host SSH session}}"
}

# @description Run the role's login in the operator's terminal, then report whether it took.
# @arg $1 string Role (its profile has the same name).
# @arg $2 string Route.
login() {
    local role=$1 route=$2 status=0 peer
    scratch=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/seat-login.XXXXXX") || die "cannot create a scratch directory" 1
    peer=$(peer_name) || die "cannot name the host whose browser opens the sign-in" 1
    printf 'seat-login-preflight: %s needs a %s login on this host; the sign-in opens in the browser of %s\n' "${role}" "${route}" "${peer}" >&2
    case ${route} in
    openai-siwc)
        # The CLI login loads extensions from settings only, so a one-command overlay names it.
        printf 'extensions:\n  - %s\n' "${siwc_ext}" > "${scratch}/siwc.yml"
        for opener in xdg-open open; do
            printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec regime-open-url "$@"\n' > "${scratch}/${opener}"
            chmod 700 "${scratch}/${opener}"
        done
        PATH="${scratch}:${PATH}" PI_CONFIG_FILES="${scratch}/siwc.yml" OPENAI_SIWC_CALLBACK_PORT=${callback_port} \
            omp --profile "${role}" login openai-siwc || status=$?
        ;;
    claude-bridge)
        printf 'seat-login-preflight: when the browser shows a code, paste it at the prompt below\n' >&2
        BROWSER=regime-open-url claude auth login || status=$?
        ;;
    esac
    ((status == 0)) || die "the ${route} login exited ${status}" 1
}

usage='usage: seat-login-preflight --check [<profile>...] | seat-login-preflight <orchestrator|worker|audit|review|security>'
(($# > 0)) || die "${usage}"
if [[ $1 == --check ]]; then
    shift
    check "$@"
    exit $?
fi
(($# == 1)) || die "${usage}"
role=$1
known=0
for profile in "${seat_profiles[@]}"; do
    if [[ ${role} == "${profile}" ]]; then known=1; fi
done
((known)) || die "unknown seat profile '${role}'; expected one of: ${seat_profiles[*]}"
# A local host keeps its own browser and login; nothing new happens there.
if [[ -z ${SSH_CONNECTION:-} ]] && ! [[ ${os} == Linux && -z ${DISPLAY:-} && -z ${WAYLAND_DISPLAY:-} ]]; then
    exit 0
fi

status=0
line=$(profile_line "${role}" 1) || status=$?
case ${status} in
0)
    printf 'seat-login-preflight: %s\n' "${line}" >&2
    exit 0
    ;;
2) die "${line}; fix or move the record aside before a seat starts" 1 ;;
3)
    printf 'seat-login-preflight: %s; nothing to log in\n' "${line}" >&2
    exit 0
    ;;
4) die "${line}; Claude Code reads the variable, never the file: open a new login shell on this host (it exports the file), then start the seat again" ;;
esac
route=$(route_of "${role}") || die "${line}" 1
if [[ ! -t 0 || ! -t 1 || -n ${HCOM_LAUNCHED:-} ]]; then
    die "${line}; a login is the operator's step: run \`seat-login-preflight ${role}\` in your own terminal on this host, then start the seat again"
fi
login "${role}" "${route}"
status=0
line=$(profile_line "${role}" 1) || status=$?
((status == 0)) || die "${line} after the login" 1
printf 'seat-login-preflight: %s\n' "${line}" >&2

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_setup-gh
# @brief Authenticate `gh` and upload the local SSH key.
# @description
#   Logs into GitHub through the GitHub CLI, ensures the local SSH public key
#   exists through an explicit interactive flow, and registers the public key as
#   both an authentication key and a commit signing key on the authenticated
#   account.
# @example
#   setup-gh

set -Eeuo pipefail

readonly DEFAULT_SSH_KEY_PATH="${HOME%/}/.ssh/id_ed25519"
readonly DEFAULT_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH="${DEFAULT_SSH_KEY_PATH}.pub"

# @description Authenticate GitHub CLI against github.com over HTTPS.
function login_to_github() {
    gh auth login -h github.com -p https
}

# @description Print the short host name, or fail naming the read when neither form works.
function short_hostname() {
    if ! hostname -s 2> /dev/null && ! hostname; then
        printf 'setup-gh: cannot read the host name for the SSH key comment\n' >&2
        return 1
    fi
}

# @description Return the email address used as the SSH key comment.
function ssh_key_comment() {
    local configured_email host
    configured_email="$(git config --global --get user.email || true)"

    if [[ -n "${configured_email}" ]]; then
        printf '%s\n' "${configured_email}"
        return 0
    fi

    host="$(short_hostname)" || return 1
    printf '%s@%s\n' "${USER:-user}" "${host}"
}

# @description Create the default SSH key through ssh-keygen when it is missing.
function ensure_default_ssh_key() {
    local comment

    if [[ -r "${DEFAULT_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH}" ]]; then
        return 0
    fi

    if [[ -e "${DEFAULT_SSH_KEY_PATH}" && ! -e "${DEFAULT_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH}" && -t 0 ]]; then
        ssh-keygen -y -f "${DEFAULT_SSH_KEY_PATH}" > "${DEFAULT_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH}"
        chmod 0644 "${DEFAULT_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH}"
        return 0
    fi

    if [[ ! -t 0 ]]; then
        printf 'Public SSH key not found: %s\n' "${DEFAULT_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH}" >&2
        printf "Run \`ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f %s -C \"\$(git config --global --get user.email)\"\` or restore the key from private chezmoi state.\n" "${DEFAULT_SSH_KEY_PATH}" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    mkdir -p "${HOME%/}/.ssh"
    chmod 0700 "${HOME%/}/.ssh"

    comment="$(ssh_key_comment)" || return 1
    printf 'Default SSH key not found. Creating %s interactively.\n' "${DEFAULT_SSH_KEY_PATH}" >&2
    ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f "${DEFAULT_SSH_KEY_PATH}" -C "${comment}"
    chmod 0600 "${DEFAULT_SSH_KEY_PATH}"
    chmod 0644 "${DEFAULT_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH}"
}

# @description Upload the local public SSH key through GitHub CLI.
function add_ssh_key_to_github() {
    ensure_default_ssh_key
    gh auth refresh -h github.com -s admin:public_key
    gh auth refresh -h github.com -s admin:ssh_signing_key
    gh ssh-key add "${DEFAULT_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH}" --type authentication
    gh ssh-key add "${DEFAULT_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH}" --type signing
}

# @description Run the GitHub authentication and SSH key setup flow.
function main() {
    login_to_github
    add_ssh_key_to_github
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
    main
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_setup-gpg
# @brief Prepare the local GnuPG secret keyring when no private source restored it.
# @description
#   Checks whether a local GnuPG secret key already exists. If not, starts the
#   standard interactive `gpg --full-generate-key` flow. Secret keys and trust
#   databases are intentionally not stored in the public chezmoi source state.
# @example
#   setup-gpg

set -Eeuo pipefail

# @description Return success when at least one GnuPG secret key exists.
function has_gpg_secret_key() {
    gpg --batch --list-secret-keys --with-colons 2> /dev/null | grep -q '^sec:'
}

# @description Create a GnuPG secret key through the standard interactive flow.
function generate_gpg_secret_key() {
    if [[ ! -t 0 ]]; then
        printf 'No local GnuPG secret key was found.\n' >&2
        printf "Run \`gpg --full-generate-key\` interactively or restore keys from the private chezmoi source.\n" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    printf 'No local GnuPG secret key was found. Starting interactive key generation.\n' >&2
    gpg --full-generate-key
}

# @description Run the GnuPG setup flow.
function main() {
    if has_gpg_secret_key; then
        printf 'GnuPG secret key already exists. Nothing to do.\n'
        return 0
    fi

    generate_gpg_secret_key
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
    main
fi

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compare function+class node counts per file between two Understand-Anything graphs.

Usage: ua-symbol-coverage <old-graph.json> <new-graph.json> [--repo-ref REF [--old-ref OLD]]

REF is the revision the new graph was built from (the new graph's
`.ua/meta.json` `gitCommitHash`, normally `HEAD`), never the pre-change base:
only the source the new graph describes can explain a symbol it no longer has.
OLD is the revision the previous graph was built from (its `gitCommitHash`);
it lets a path absent at REF be told apart as a rename or a deletion.

Prints one row per `filePath`: old count, new count, the number of def-like
source lines at REF (information only), status and note. Two principles:

- Structural git facts explain a loss; def-line counts never do. A decrease
  is `explained` only with --old-ref and only when the path is absent at REF
  and was not renamed (a deletion, shown `gone`). A path renamed between OLD
  and REF (`git diff -M --diff-filter=R`) is judged on its successor's new
  count, which its row's new column shows: `ok` when the successor keeps at
  least the old count, otherwise a regression. Every other decrease is a
  regression, including a legitimate function deletion in a changed file; the
  acceptance rule then requires the validation to cite the source change
  behind it. A decrease in a file whose blob is identical at OLD and REF is
  noted `source unchanged`, since no source change can be cited for it.
- Def-line counts only flag. A path new to the graph that exists at REF with
  at least one def-like line but no symbols is a regression noted
  `new file, no symbols`; this also catches a move plus rewrite below git's
  50% rename-similarity threshold. Likewise, a grammar file that exists at
  REF with at least one def-like line but appears in neither graph is a
  regression noted `missing from graph`, but
  only in a directory the new graph already covers (some listed path shares
  its parent), so the graph's own include scope is respected. Candidates are
  `.py`/`.rb`/`.sh`/`.bash`/`.zsh`/`.bats` files and mode-100755 files whose
  shebang selects a grammar.

Def-like lines skip comment lines (first non-blank character `#`) in every
grammar. For Python they are the `ast` count of function, async function and
class definitions, so a `def` inside a string literal counts nothing; the
line regex is used only when the file does not parse.

Ceiling (measured): the def-like count overcounts relative to graph nodes
(nested functions and methods often get no node), so partial
under-extraction of a brand-new file is not detectable from it: in the
accepted graph of 2026-10-01, 138 of 185 files with a def grammar have fewer
symbols than def-like lines. Only the zero-symbol case is flagged, and the
`def-like lines` column is informational. File types without a def grammar
(`-`) are never flagged by the new-file check.
`validateGraph` checks schema and references only, so this is the
completeness gate for a `.ua/` refresh
(home/dot_config/claude/rules/understand-anything.md).

Exit status: 0 no regressions, 1 regressions, 2 when REF or OLD does not resolve to
a commit or a path cannot be read at REF (fail closed, no table-based pass).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import ast
import json
import posixpath
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

SYMBOL_TYPES = {"function", "class"}
PYTHON_DEF = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:async\s+def|def|class)\s+\w+")
RUBY_DEF = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:(?:private|protected|public)\s+)?(?:def|class|module)\s+\S+")
# Any name without whitespace, parentheses or `=` (`arr=()` is an array assignment).
SHELL_DEF = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:function\s+\S+|[^\s()=]+\s*\(\))(?:\s*[{(].*)?\s*$")
GRAMMAR_SUFFIXES = (".py", ".rb", ".sh", ".bash", ".zsh", ".bats")
PYTHON_NODES = (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.ClassDef)


def symbol_counts(graph_path: Path) -> dict[str, int]:
    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
    for node in json.loads(graph_path.read_text())["nodes"]:
        path = node.get("filePath")
        if not path:
            continue
        counts.setdefault(path, 0)
        if node.get("type") in SYMBOL_TYPES:
            counts[path] += 1
    return counts


def def_pattern(path: str, text: str) -> re.Pattern[str] | None:
    first = text.split("\n", 1)[0]
    if path.endswith(".py") or "python" in first or "uv run" in first:
        return PYTHON_DEF
    if path.endswith(".rb") or "ruby" in first:
        return RUBY_DEF
    if path.endswith((".sh", ".bash", ".zsh", ".bats")) or re.search(
        r"\b(?:ba|z)?sh\b", first
    ):
        return SHELL_DEF
    return None


class CoverageError(Exception):
    """A ref or path could not be resolved; the gate must fail closed."""


def git(*args: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
    return subprocess.run(["git", *args], capture_output=True, text=True, errors="replace", check=False)


def verify_ref(ref: str, option: str = "--repo-ref") -> None:
    if not ref.strip() or ref.startswith("-"):
        raise CoverageError(f"{option} {ref!r} is not a git ref")
    if git("rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", "--end-of-options", f"{ref}^{{commit}}").returncode != 0:
        raise CoverageError(f"{option} {ref!r} does not resolve to a commit")


def def_lines(ref: str, path: str) -> int | str | None:
    """Return def-like line count at REF, "-" without a grammar, or None when the path is absent at REF."""
    shown = git("show", f"{ref}:{path}")
    if shown.returncode != 0:
        listed = git("ls-tree", "--name-only", ref, "--", path)
        if listed.returncode == 0 and not listed.stdout.strip():
            return None
        raise CoverageError(f"cannot read {path} at {ref}: {shown.stderr.strip() or listed.stderr.strip()}")
    pattern = def_pattern(path, shown.stdout)
    if pattern is None:
        return "-"
    return count_defs(pattern, shown.stdout)


def count_defs(pattern: re.Pattern[str], text: str) -> int:
    """Count definitions: Python via `ast` (regex only on a SyntaxError), else non-comment regex lines."""
    if pattern is PYTHON_DEF:
        try:
            return sum(isinstance(node, PYTHON_NODES) for node in ast.walk(ast.parse(text)))
        except (SyntaxError, ValueError):
            pass
    return sum(1 for line in text.splitlines() if not line.lstrip().startswith("#") and pattern.search(line))


def renames(old_ref: str, ref: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Map each path renamed between OLD and REF to its successor."""
    diff = git("diff", "-z", "--name-status", "-M", "--diff-filter=R", old_ref, ref, "--")
    if diff.returncode != 0:
        raise CoverageError(f"cannot diff {old_ref}..{ref}: {diff.stderr.strip()}")
    fields = diff.stdout.split("\0")
    return {fields[i + 1]: fields[i + 2] for i in range(0, len(fields) - 2, 3)}


def blobs(ref: str) -> dict[str, tuple[str, str]]:
    """Map every blob path at REF to its (mode, blob id) (REF is already verified)."""
    tree = git("ls-tree", "-r", "-z", ref)
    if tree.returncode != 0:
        raise CoverageError(f"cannot list {ref}: {tree.stderr.strip()}")
    entries: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {}
    for entry in filter(None, tree.stdout.split("\0")):
        meta, _, path = entry.partition("\t")
        mode, kind, blob = meta.split()
        if kind == "blob":
            entries[path] = (mode, blob)
    return entries


def missing_from_graph(
    ref: str, entries: dict[str, tuple[str, str]], old: dict[str, int], new: dict[str, int]
) -> list[tuple[str, int]]:
    """Grammar files at REF with def-like lines that neither graph lists, in directories the new graph covers."""
    covered = {posixpath.dirname(path) for path in new}
    found = []
    for path, (mode, _) in sorted(entries.items()):
        if path in old or path in new or posixpath.dirname(path) not in covered:
            continue
        if not path.endswith(GRAMMAR_SUFFIXES):
            if mode != "100755":
                continue
            shown = git("show", f"{ref}:{path}")
            if shown.returncode != 0:
                raise CoverageError(f"cannot read {path} at {ref}: {shown.stderr.strip()}")
            first = shown.stdout.split("\n", 1)[0]
            if not first.startswith("#!") or def_pattern(path, first) is None:
                continue
        defs = def_lines(ref, path)
        if isinstance(defs, int) and defs:
            found.append((path, defs))
    return found


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("old_graph", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("new_graph", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--repo-ref", help="revision the new graph was built from (its .ua/meta.json gitCommitHash)")
    parser.add_argument("--old-ref", help="revision the previous graph was built from (its .ua/meta.json gitCommitHash)")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.old_ref is not None and args.repo_ref is None:
        parser.error("--old-ref requires --repo-ref")

    old, new = symbol_counts(args.old_graph), symbol_counts(args.new_graph)
    moved: dict[str, str] = {}
    old_blobs: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {}
    new_blobs: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {}
    missing: list[tuple[str, int]] = []
    try:
        if args.repo_ref is not None:
            verify_ref(args.repo_ref)
            new_blobs = blobs(args.repo_ref)
            missing = missing_from_graph(args.repo_ref, new_blobs, old, new)
        if args.old_ref is not None:
            verify_ref(args.old_ref, "--old-ref")
            moved = renames(args.old_ref, args.repo_ref)
            old_blobs = blobs(args.old_ref)
        rows = [
            (path, old.get(path, 0), new.get(path, 0), def_lines(args.repo_ref, path) if args.repo_ref else "-")
            for path in sorted(set(old) | set(new))
        ]
        successors = {
            path: (moved[path], new.get(moved[path], 0))
            for path, _, _, defs in rows
            if defs is None and path in moved
        }
    except CoverageError as error:
        print(f"ua-symbol-coverage: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    # A successor whose predecessor had symbols is judged on the predecessor's row.
    judged = {successor for path, (successor, _) in successors.items() if old.get(path, 0)}
    regressions = 0
    print("| file | old | new | def-like lines | status | note |")
    print("|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for path, before, after, defs in rows:
        status, shown, note, source = "ok", defs, "", path
        if path in successors:
            source, after = successors[path]
            shown = f"renamed → {source}"
        elif defs is None:
            shown = "gone"
        if after < before:
            deleted = defs is None and args.old_ref is not None and path not in successors
            status = "explained" if deleted else "REGRESSION"
            # Blob ids only: a chmod-only change leaves the bytes unchanged.
            if path in old_blobs and old_blobs[path][1] == new_blobs.get(source, ("", ""))[1]:
                note = "source unchanged"
        elif path not in old and path not in judged and isinstance(defs, int) and defs and not after:
            status, note = "REGRESSION", "new file, no symbols"
        regressions += status == "REGRESSION"
        print(f"| {path} | {before} | {after} | {shown} | {status} | {note} |")
    for path, defs in missing:
        print(f"| {path} | 0 | 0 | {defs} | REGRESSION | missing from graph |")
    regressions += len(missing)
    print(f"files: {len(rows) + len(missing)}, regressions: {regressions}")
    return 1 if regressions else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_uv-format
# @brief Format Python code with Ruff through `uvx`.
# @description
#   Runs Ruff formatting first and then fixes import ordering and selected
#   issues through Ruff's check mode.
# @example
#   uv-format

# @description Run Ruff formatting and autofix passes through `uvx`.
function uv_format() {
    uvx ruff format
    uvx ruff check --fix --extend-select I
}

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    uv_format
fi

<pre><code>#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file worktree-gc.sh
# @brief List the clean agent worktrees under .claude/worktrees/ whose work landed; quarantine them with --apply, delete old quarantined ones with --purge.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U16, a coordinator lever pre-authorized by
#   `Bash(scripts/orchestrator/worktree-gc.sh *)` (scripts/orchestrator/README.md,
#   "Pre-authorized levers"). The candidates are the worktrees of this checkout
#   (`git worktree list --porcelain -z`) under `<toplevel>/.claude/worktrees/`,
#   except the quarantine `<toplevel>/.claude/worktrees/.gc-quarantine/`; every
#   other worktree, the main one and the omp seats included, is never listed.
#   A candidate qualifies when its tree is clean (`git status --porcelain
#   --ignored=matching --untracked-files=all` prints nothing: `git worktree
#   remove` deletes ignored files without asking, so a tree holding one, an
#   `.env` say, is kept; and no index entry carries the `assume-unchanged` or
#   `skip-worktree` flag, `git ls-files -v` tag lowercase or `S`, since an edit
#   to such a file is invisible to `git status` and to the removal's own check)
#   and its work landed, the first of: its head is
#   reachable from `origin/main` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`); it landed by
#   content (every path `git diff --no-renames --name-only -z <merge-base>
#   <head>` names holds in `origin/main` the entry it holds in the head, mode
#   and object, or is absent from both: the case of a squash merge with no
#   later commit; no merge runs, so no configured merge driver or `merge=`
#   attribute can answer, and a git failure is an `error` row); or its head is
#   the `headRefOid` of a merged pull request of this repository (`gh pr list
#   --state merged --head <branch> --json number,headRefOid --limit 100`,
#   detached `--search <sha>`). A branch name
#   alone never counts: a commit pushed after a squash merge is not in main,
#   and `--head` also matches a fork's branch of the same name. A locked or
#   missing worktree is kept. The listing is read field by field on its NUL
#   separators, so a path cannot forge a record; a candidate whose path
#   contains a newline is an `error` row. Each candidate prints one row
#   `<verdict>\t<path>\t<ref>\t<reason>` (a newline in the path printed as
#   `\n`), verdict `gc` (qualifies), `keep` or `error`, then each quarantined
#   worktree a `quarantine` row with its age, then one `summary` row.
#
#   No check can be made atomic with a deletion, so taking a tree out of use
#   and deleting it are two runs. `--apply` deletes nothing: it renames each
#   qualifying tree with `git worktree move <path>
#   .gc-quarantine/<random>/<name>` (one rename on the same filesystem; git
#   refuses a locked tree), writes `<epoch> <classified head>` to
#   `gc-quarantined-at` in the tree's admin directory (`git rev-parse
#   --absolute-git-dir`, refused unless a plain directory directly under
#   `<common dir>/worktrees/`; the marker goes to a `mktemp` file there,
#   renamed onto its name, so a symlink planted at the name is replaced, never
#   written through), then checks the moved tree clean again (index flags
#   included) and its HEAD equal to the classified one. Both hold: a
#   `quarantined` row. Either fails (a file or commit made after the
#   classification moved with the tree), or the marker cannot be written: a
#   `held` row with the reason; the tree stays in the quarantine, is never
#   moved back and never deleted by this run. A refused move is a `failed`
#   row, exit 1. `--purge <days>` lists only the quarantine: each entry whose
#   marker is at least <days> days old (0: any age) is classified again by the
#   same rules (clean, ignored files included; HEAD read again and landed by
#   ancestry, content or a merged PR's exact head) and then removed with `git
#   worktree remove <path>`; an entry without a marker, younger, locked, or
#   no longer qualifying is kept, a refused removal is a `failed` row, exit 1.
#   Residual: purge, too, cannot check and remove atomically, so a file
#   written into the quarantined tree between its re-check and the removal is
#   lost; nothing has the quarantine path as its own, so that takes a process
#   still writing through its old working directory into the renamed tree
#   <days> days after the move. Nothing ever passes `--force`, and branch refs
#   stay. `git worktree prune` is never run: it would drop the admin data of
#   every worktree whose directory is missing, an unlocked omp seat included.
#   A `gh` error fails closed: the run moves and removes nothing and exits 1.
#   `origin/main` is read as it is; run `git fetch origin` first for a current
#   answer. Every `gh` call is bounded by WORKTREE_GC_GH_TIMEOUT seconds (perl
#   `alarm`, because `timeout` is not on every host). A path argument narrows
#   the listing and `--apply` to those worktrees and is refused unless it is
#   one of the candidates; `--purge` takes none.
# @arg $@ path Optional worktree paths under .claude/worktrees/ (not in the quarantine); default: all of them.
# @option --apply Move the qualifying worktrees into the quarantine (default: list only).
# @option --purge <days> Remove the quarantined worktrees quarantined at least <days> days ago that still qualify.
# @env WORKTREE_GC_GH_TIMEOUT Seconds per `gh` call (default 60).
# @stdout One TSV row per candidate and quarantined worktree, the move or removal rows, then `summary`.
# @exitcode 0 Listed (and quarantined or purged), including when nothing qualifies or a moved tree is held.
# @exitcode 1 A git or gh query failed, a path holds a newline, or a move or removal failed.
# @exitcode 2 Usage error, not in a git checkout, a path outside .claude/worktrees/ or in the quarantine, or a quarantine that is a symlink.
# @example
#   scripts/orchestrator/worktree-gc.sh
#   scripts/orchestrator/worktree-gc.sh --apply
#   scripts/orchestrator/worktree-gc.sh --purge 7
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

usage='usage: worktree-gc.sh [--apply] [<path>...] | --purge <days>'
apply=0 purge=''
paths=()
while (($#)); do
    case $1 in
    --apply) apply=1 ;;
    --purge)
        if (($# < 2)) || [[ ! $2 =~ ^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,4})$ ]]; then
            echo "${usage}" >&2
            exit 2
        fi
        purge=$2
        shift
        ;;
    --) ;;
    -*)
        echo "${usage}" >&2
        exit 2
        ;;
    *) paths+=("$1") ;;
    esac
    shift
done
if [[ -n ${purge} ]] && ((apply || ${#paths[@]})); then
    echo "${usage}" >&2
    exit 2
fi
gh_timeout=${WORKTREE_GC_GH_TIMEOUT:-60}
[[ ${gh_timeout} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || {
    echo 'worktree-gc: WORKTREE_GC_GH_TIMEOUT must be a positive integer' >&2
    exit 2
}

toplevel=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2> /dev/null) || {
    echo 'worktree-gc: not in a git checkout' >&2
    exit 2
}
toplevel=$(cd "${toplevel}" && pwd -P)
base=${toplevel}/.claude/worktrees
quarantine=${base}/.gc-quarantine
if ! common_dir=$(git -C "${toplevel}" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir) ||
    ! common_dir=$(cd "${common_dir}" && pwd -P); then
    echo 'worktree-gc: cannot resolve the git common directory' >&2
    exit 1
fi
git -C "${toplevel}" rev-parse --verify --quiet 'origin/main^{commit}' > /dev/null || {
    echo 'worktree-gc: origin/main is absent; run git fetch origin' >&2
    exit 1
}

# @description Print the physical form of a path, or the path itself when it no longer exists.
# @arg $1 path A path.
physical() {
    if [[ -d $1 ]]; then (cd "$1" && pwd -P); else printf '%s\n' "$1"; fi
}

# @description Succeed when a physical path lies strictly under .claude/worktrees/ of this checkout.
# @arg $1 path A physical path.
under_base() {
    [[ $1 == "${base}/"?* ]] # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
}

# @description Succeed when a physical path is the quarantine or lies under it.
# @arg $1 path A physical path.
in_quarantine() {
    [[ $1 == "${quarantine}" || $1 == "${quarantine}/"* ]] # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
}

# @description Print the admin directory of a worktree, refusing one outside `<common dir>/worktrees/`.
# @arg $1 path The worktree.
# @exitcode 1 git failed or the admin directory is elsewhere.
admin_dir() {
    local raw dir
    raw=$(git -C "$1" rev-parse --absolute-git-dir) && [[ ! -L ${raw} ]] && dir=$(cd "${raw}" && pwd -P) || return 1
    [[ ${dir} == "${common_dir}/worktrees/"?* && ${dir} != "${common_dir}/worktrees/"*/* ]] || return 1 # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
    printf '%s\n' "${dir}"
}

# @description Write the quarantine marker into an admin directory without following a link at its name: the content
#   goes to a fresh `mktemp` file beside it, which is renamed onto the name (a rename replaces a symlink there). A
#   directory at the name, or one a symlink there points at, is refused, since `mv` would move the file into it.
# @arg $1 path The admin directory, from admin_dir.
# @arg $2 string The marker line.
# @exitcode 1 The marker was not written.
write_marker() {
    local tmp
    [[ ! -d $1/${marker} ]] || return 1
    tmp=$(mktemp "$1/${marker}.XXXXXX") || return 1
    if printf '%s\n' "$2" > "${tmp}" && mv -f "${tmp}" "$1/${marker}"; then return 0; fi
    rm -f "${tmp}"
    return 1
}

# @description Run gh in the checkout, killed after WORKTREE_GC_GH_TIMEOUT seconds.
# @arg $@ string gh arguments.
bounded_gh() {
    (cd "${toplevel}" && perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV or die "exec gh: $!\n"' "${gh_timeout}" gh "$@")
}

selected=()
for path in "${paths[@]+"${paths[@]}"}"; do
    resolved=$(physical "${path}")
    under_base "${resolved}" || {
        echo "worktree-gc: refused: ${path} is outside ${base}/" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    ! in_quarantine "${resolved}" || {
        echo "worktree-gc: refused: ${path} is in the quarantine ${quarantine}/; --purge handles it" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    selected+=("${resolved}")
done

# Candidates and quarantined worktrees as parallel arrays: path, head, branch (empty when detached), state (`locked`,
# `missing`, `newline` or empty).
cand_path=() cand_head=() cand_branch=() cand_state=()
q_path=() q_head=() q_branch=() q_state=()
record() {
    [[ -n ${wt_path} ]] || return 0
    local resolved state=${wt_state}
    resolved=$(physical "${wt_path}")
    under_base "${resolved}" || return 0
    if [[ ${wt_path} == *$'\n'* ]]; then state=newline; fi # lint-comparisons: allow a newline-content test, not a path comparison
    if in_quarantine "${resolved}"; then
        ((${#selected[@]})) && return 0
        q_path+=("${resolved}") q_head+=("${wt_head}") q_branch+=("${wt_branch}") q_state+=("${state}")
        return 0
    fi
    if ((${#selected[@]})); then
        local wanted='' item
        for item in "${selected[@]}"; do [[ ${item} == "${resolved}" ]] && wanted=1; done # lint-comparisons: allow both operands are pwd -P forms from physical()
        [[ -n ${wanted} ]] || return 0
    fi
    cand_path+=("${resolved}") cand_head+=("${wt_head}") cand_branch+=("${wt_branch}") cand_state+=("${state}")
}
# The producer writes to a file, not a pipe or a process substitution, so its exit status is checked; the NUL-separated
# fields are read as they are (`read -d ''`), never turned into lines, so a newline inside a path stays in its field.
listing=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/worktree-gc.XXXXXX")
changed=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/worktree-gc.XXXXXX")
entries=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/worktree-gc.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -f "${listing}" "${changed}" "${entries}"' EXIT
git -C "${toplevel}" worktree list --porcelain -z > "${listing}" || {
    echo 'worktree-gc: git worktree list failed' >&2
    exit 1
}
wt_path='' wt_head='' wt_branch='' wt_state=''
while IFS= read -r -d '' field; do
    case ${field} in
    'worktree '*)
        record
        wt_path=${field#worktree } wt_head='' wt_branch='' wt_state=''
        ;;
    'HEAD '*) wt_head=${field#HEAD } ;;
    'branch refs/heads/'*) wt_branch=${field#branch refs/heads/} ;;
    locked | 'locked '*) wt_state=locked ;;
    prunable | 'prunable '*) [[ -n ${wt_state} ]] || wt_state=missing ;;
    esac
done < "${listing}"
record

for path in "${selected[@]+"${selected[@]}"}"; do
    found=''
    for item in "${cand_path[@]+"${cand_path[@]}"}"; do [[ ${item} == "${path}" ]] && found=1; done # lint-comparisons: allow both operands are pwd -P forms from physical()
    [[ -n ${found} ]] || {
        echo "worktree-gc: refused: ${path} is not a worktree of ${toplevel}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
done

# @description Succeed when the head landed in origin/main by content: every path `git diff` names between the merge
#   base and the head holds in origin/main the `git ls-tree -r` entry (mode, type, object) it holds in the head, or is
#   absent from both. Nothing here merges, so no merge driver, `merge=` attribute or `merge.*` setting takes part; the
#   diff is name-only and NUL-separated, renames off and submodules shown, and every pathspec literal.
# @arg $1 string The head sha.
# @exitcode 0 Landed by content (an empty change set included).
# @exitcode 1 Not landed, or the head shares no history with origin/main.
# @exitcode 2 A git call failed.
landed_by_content() {
    local head=$1 mb rc field in_head in_main
    local -a changed_paths=()
    mb=$(git -C "${toplevel}" merge-base origin/main "${head}") && rc=0 || rc=$?
    ((rc != 1)) || return 1
    if ((rc)) || [[ ! ${mb} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}([0-9a-f]{24})?$ ]]; then return 2; fi
    git -C "${toplevel}" diff --no-renames --no-relative --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-color \
        --ignore-submodules=none --name-only -z "${mb}" "${head}" -- > "${changed}" || return 2
    while IFS= read -r -d '' field; do changed_paths+=("${field}"); done < "${changed}"
    ((${#changed_paths[@]})) || return 0
    # Without -z the quoted listing has one line per entry, so it survives a command substitution; both sides are quoted alike.
    in_head=$(git -C "${toplevel}" -c core.quotePath=true --literal-pathspecs ls-tree -r --full-tree "${head}" \
        -- "${changed_paths[@]}") || return 2
    in_main=$(git -C "${toplevel}" -c core.quotePath=true --literal-pathspecs ls-tree -r --full-tree origin/main \
        -- "${changed_paths[@]}") || return 2
    [[ ${in_head} == "${in_main}" ]] || return 1
}

# @description Set `status` to the `git status --porcelain --ignored=matching --untracked-files=all` of a worktree,
#   and `flagged` to the number of its index entries marked `assume-unchanged` (`git ls-files -v` tag lowercase) or
#   `skip-worktree` (tag `S`), whose edits neither `git status` nor `git worktree remove` sees.
# @arg $1 path The worktree.
# @exitcode 1 git status or git ls-files failed.
tree_status() {
    local entry
    flagged=0
    status=$(git -C "$1" status --porcelain --ignored=matching --untracked-files=all) || return 1
    git -C "$1" ls-files -v -z > "${entries}" || return 1
    while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
        if [[ ${entry} == [[:lower:]S]' '* ]]; then flagged=$((flagged + 1)); fi
    done < "${entries}"
}

# @description Set `verdict` and `reason` for one candidate.
# @arg $1 path The worktree.
# @arg $2 string Its head sha.
# @arg $3 string Its branch, empty when detached.
# @arg $4 string Its state: `locked`, `missing`, `newline` or empty.
classify() {
    local path=$1 head=$2 branch=$3 state=$4 rc query prs number
    verdict=keep
    if [[ ${state} == newline ]]; then
        verdict=error reason='path contains a newline'
        return
    fi
    if [[ ${state} == locked ]]; then
        reason='locked'
        return
    fi
    if [[ ${state} == missing || ! -d ${path} ]]; then
        reason='missing (its admin data is left for the operator)'
        return
    fi
    if ! tree_status "${path}"; then
        verdict=error reason='git status failed'
        return
    fi
    if [[ -n ${status} ]] && grep -qv '^!! ' <<< "${status}"; then
        reason='dirty or untracked files'
        return
    fi
    if ((flagged)); then
        reason="${flagged} index entries marked assume-unchanged or skip-worktree (git status cannot see their edits)"
        return
    fi
    if [[ -n ${status} ]]; then
        reason='ignored files (git worktree remove would delete them)'
        return
    fi
    if [[ ! ${head} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}([0-9a-f]{24})?$ ]]; then
        verdict=error reason="unreadable head '${head}'"
        return
    fi
    if git -C "${toplevel}" merge-base --is-ancestor "${head}" origin/main 2> /dev/null; then
        verdict=gc reason="head ${head:0:12} is in origin/main"
        return
    fi
    landed_by_content "${head}" && rc=0 || rc=$?
    if ((rc > 1)); then
        verdict=error reason="comparing head ${head:0:12} with origin/main failed"
        return
    fi
    if ((rc == 0)); then
        verdict=gc reason="every path head ${head:0:12} changed holds the same entry in origin/main"
        return
    fi
    if [[ -n ${branch} ]]; then
        query=(--head "${branch}" --json 'number,headRefOid' --limit 100)
    else
        query=(--search "${head}" --json 'number,headRefOid')
    fi
    if ! prs=$(bounded_gh pr list --state merged "${query[@]}") ||
        ! number=$(jq -r --arg sha "${head}" 'map(select(.headRefOid == $sha))[0].number // empty' <<< "${prs}"); then
        verdict=error reason="gh pr list ${query[0]} ${query[1]:0:12} failed"
        return
    fi
    if [[ -n ${number} ]]; then
        verdict=gc reason="head ${head:0:12} is the head of merged PR #${number}"
    else
        reason="head ${head:0:12} is neither in origin/main nor the head of a merged PR"
    fi
}

marker='gc-quarantined-at'
now=$(date +%s)

# @description Set `quarantined_at` to the epoch the quarantine marker of a worktree records, empty without a readable one.
# @arg $1 path The quarantined worktree.
read_marker() {
    local dir line=''
    quarantined_at=''
    dir=$(admin_dir "$1") || return 0
    [[ -f ${dir}/${marker} && ! -L ${dir}/${marker} ]] || return 0
    IFS= read -r line < "${dir}/${marker}" || [[ -n ${line} ]] || return 0
    if [[ ${line} =~ ^([0-9]{1,12})\ [0-9a-f]{40}([0-9a-f]{24})?$ ]]; then quarantined_at=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}; fi
}

# @description Print an age in seconds as `<d>d <h>h`.
# @arg $1 number Seconds.
age() {
    printf '%dd %dh' $(($1 / 86400)) $(($1 % 86400 / 3600))
}

if [[ -n ${purge} ]]; then
    doomed=() errors=0 kept=0
    for ((i = 0; i < ${#q_path[@]}; i++)); do
        path=${q_path[i]} state=${q_state[i]} verdict=keep
        if [[ ${state} == newline ]]; then
            verdict=error reason='path contains a newline'
        elif [[ ${state} == locked ]]; then
            reason='locked'
        elif [[ ${state} == missing || ! -d ${path} ]]; then
            reason='missing (its admin data is left for the operator)'
        else
            read_marker "${path}"
            if [[ -z ${quarantined_at} ]]; then
                reason="no ${marker} marker in its admin directory"
            elif ((now - quarantined_at < purge * 86400)); then
                reason="quarantined $(age $((now - quarantined_at))) ago, younger than ${purge} days"
            elif ! head=$(git -C "${path}" rev-parse --verify --quiet 'HEAD^{commit}'); then
                verdict=error reason='cannot read HEAD'
            elif [[ ${head} != "${q_head[i]}" ]]; then
                reason="head moved to ${head:0:12} during the run"
            else
                # The same rules as a candidate's: clean (ignored files included) and landed by ancestry, content or a
                # merged PR's exact head.
                classify "${path}" "${head}" "${q_branch[i]}" "${state}"
            fi
        fi
        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "${verdict}" "${path//$'\n'/\\n}" "${q_branch[i]:-(detached ${q_head[i]:0:12})}" "${reason}"
        case ${verdict} in
        gc) doomed+=("${path}") ;;
        error) errors=$((errors + 1)) ;;
        *) kept=$((kept + 1)) ;;
        esac
    done
    if ((errors)); then
        printf 'summary\t%d qualify, %d kept, %d errors; nothing removed\n' "${#doomed[@]}" "${kept}" "${errors}"
        exit 1
    fi
    removed=0 failed=0
    for path in "${doomed[@]+"${doomed[@]}"}"; do
        in_quarantine "${path}" || {
            echo "worktree-gc: refused: ${path} is outside ${quarantine}/" >&2
            exit 2
        }
        # Residual: no check is atomic with the removal; the tree has sat renamed for at least the purge age.
        if git -C "${toplevel}" worktree remove "${path}"; then
            printf 'removed\t%s\n' "${path}"
            removed=$((removed + 1))
            slot=${path%/*}
            if [[ ${slot} != "${quarantine}" ]] && in_quarantine "${slot}"; then rmdir "${slot}" 2> /dev/null || true; fi # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        else
            printf 'failed\t%s\tgit worktree remove refused\n' "${path}"
            failed=$((failed + 1))
        fi
    done
    printf 'summary\t%d removed, %d failed, %d kept\n' "${removed}" "${failed}" "${kept}"
    ((! failed)) || exit 1
    exit 0
fi

gc=() errors=0 kept=0
for ((i = 0; i < ${#cand_path[@]}; i++)); do
    classify "${cand_path[i]}" "${cand_head[i]}" "${cand_branch[i]}" "${cand_state[i]}"
    shown=${cand_path[i]//$'\n'/\\n}
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "${verdict}" "${shown}" "${cand_branch[i]:-(detached ${cand_head[i]:0:12})}" "${reason}"
    case ${verdict} in
    gc) gc+=("${i}") ;;
    error) errors=$((errors + 1)) ;;
    *) kept=$((kept + 1)) ;;
    esac
done
for ((i = 0; i < ${#q_path[@]}; i++)); do
    read_marker "${q_path[i]}"
    if [[ -n ${quarantined_at} ]]; then
        reason="quarantined $(age $((now - quarantined_at))) ago"
    else
        reason="no ${marker} marker in its admin directory (--purge keeps it)"
    fi
    printf 'quarantine\t%s\t%s\t%s%s\n' "${q_path[i]//$'\n'/\\n}" "${q_branch[i]:-(detached ${q_head[i]:0:12})}" "${reason}" "${q_state[i]:+, ${q_state[i]}}"
done

if ((errors)); then
    printf 'summary\t%d qualify, %d kept, %d errors; nothing moved\n' "${#gc[@]}" "${kept}" "${errors}"
    exit 1
fi
if ((! apply)); then
    printf 'summary\t%d qualify, %d kept, %d in quarantine; dry run, rerun with --apply to quarantine\n' "${#gc[@]}" "${kept}" "${#q_path[@]}"
    exit 0
fi

if ((${#gc[@]})); then
    resolved=''
    if mkdir -p "${quarantine}" && [[ ! -L ${quarantine} ]]; then resolved=$(physical "${quarantine}"); fi
    [[ ${resolved} == "${quarantine}" ]] || { # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        echo "worktree-gc: refused: the quarantine ${quarantine} is not a plain directory" >&2
        exit 2
    }
fi
quarantined=0 held=0 failed=0
for i in "${gc[@]+"${gc[@]}"}"; do
    path=${cand_path[i]} head=${cand_head[i]}
    if ! under_base "${path}" || in_quarantine "${path}"; then
        echo "worktree-gc: refused: ${path} is outside ${base}/ or in the quarantine" >&2
        exit 2
    fi
    # A fresh directory per tree, so the destination never exists (git moves into an existing directory) and two trees
    # of the same name never meet.
    if ! slot=$(mktemp -d "${quarantine}/XXXXXXXX"); then
        printf 'failed\t%s\tcannot create a directory in the quarantine\n' "${path}"
        failed=$((failed + 1))
        continue
    fi
    dest=${slot}/${path##*/}
    # One rename: a process inside the tree keeps its working directory, now in the quarantine; nothing is deleted.
    if ! git -C "${toplevel}" worktree move "${path}" "${dest}"; then
        rmdir "${slot}" 2> /dev/null || true
        printf 'failed\t%s\tgit worktree move refused\n' "${path}"
        failed=$((failed + 1))
        continue
    fi
    # The classification may be minutes old (gh calls); whatever changed since moved with the tree and holds it.
    reason=''
    if ! dir=$(admin_dir "${dest}") || ! write_marker "${dir}" "${now} ${head}"; then
        reason="cannot write ${marker} in its admin directory"
    elif ! tree_status "${dest}"; then
        reason='git status failed after the move'
    elif [[ -n ${status} ]]; then
        reason='changed since the check: dirty, untracked or ignored files'
    elif ((flagged)); then
        reason="${flagged} index entries marked assume-unchanged or skip-worktree since the check"
    elif ! moved_head=$(git -C "${dest}" rev-parse --verify --quiet 'HEAD^{commit}'); then
        reason='cannot read HEAD after the move'
    elif [[ ${moved_head} != "${head}" ]]; then
        reason="head moved from ${head:0:12} to ${moved_head:0:12} since the check"
    fi
    if [[ -n ${reason} ]]; then
        printf 'held\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "${path}" "${dest}" "${reason}"
        held=$((held + 1))
    else
        printf 'quarantined\t%s\t%s\n' "${path}" "${dest}"
        quarantined=$((quarantined + 1))
    fi
done
printf 'summary\t%d quarantined, %d held, %d failed, %d kept\n' "${quarantined}" "${held}" "${failed}" "${kept}"
((! failed)) || exit 1

#!/usr/bin/env zsh

# @file home/dot_local/bin/server/cuda.sh
# @brief Export CUDA paths for server shells.
# @description
#   Sets `CUDA_HOME`, prepends the CUDA binaries to the shell path, and extends
#   `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` for CUDA libraries.
# @example
#   source ~/.local/bin/server/cuda.sh

export CUDA_HOME="/usr/local/cuda"

typeset -gU path
path=(
    $path
    ${CUDA_HOME}/bin(N-/)
)

export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$LD_LIBRARY_PATH:$CUDA_HOME/lib64"
