#
# @description Resolve path segments lexically as Node's path.resolve does, which npm applies to a bin link and to its
#   prefix before its ownership check (bin-links check-bin): an absolute segment restarts the path, empty and `.`
#   segments drop, and `..` drops its parent.
# @arg $@ path Segments, the first one absolute.
# @stdout The resolved path.
#
function normalize_node_path() {
    local segment part resolved=""
    local -a parts=()
    for segment in "$@"; do
        [ -z "${segment}" ] || [ -n "${segment%%/*}" ] || resolved="" # an absolute segment starts with its separator
        IFS=/ read -ra parts <<< "${segment}"
        for part in ${parts[@]+"${parts[@]}"}; do # empty for ""; bash before 4.4 calls "${parts[@]}" unbound then
            case "${part}" in
            "" | .) ;;
            ..) resolved="${resolved%/*}" ;;
            *) resolved="${resolved}/${part}" ;;
            esac
        done
    done
    printf '%s\n' "${resolved:-/}"
}

#
# @description Verify the pinned omp tarball before npm installs it.
# @exitcode 1 The download checksum or installed version differs from its pin.
#
function update_omp() (
    local installed download_dir tarball actual entry="${HOME}/.local/bin/omp" aside="" link resolved package_dir
    has_command npm || {
        printf 'Skipping omp: npm command not found.\n'
        return 0
    }
    section "omp"
    installed="$("${HOME}/.local/bin/omp" --version 2> /dev/null | awk 'NR == 1 { print $NF }')" || installed=none
    installed="${installed#omp/}"
    if [ "${installed}" = "${OMP_PIN_VERSION}" ]; then
        printf 'omp %s is already installed.\n' "${installed}"
        return 0
    fi
    download_dir="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/update-agent-assets.XXXXXX")" || return
    trap 'rm -rf "${download_dir}"' EXIT
    tarball="${download_dir}/omp-${OMP_PIN_VERSION}.tgz"
    curl -fsSL "${OMP_TARBALL_URL}" -o "${tarball}" || return
    actual="$(shasum -a 256 "${tarball}" | awk '{ print $1 }')" || return
    if [ "${actual}" != "${OMP_TARBALL_SHA256}" ]; then
        printf 'omp checksum mismatch: expected %s, got %s.\n' "${OMP_TARBALL_SHA256}" "${actual}" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    # npm refuses with EEXIST to replace a bin entry it does not own, so a standalone file or a link outside this
    # prefix's package (a mise or manual install, a dangling link included) moves to a kept path, and comes back when
    # the install fails; a directory stays for npm to judge.
    # npm resolves the link against the bin directory, and its prefix, before its ownership check (bin-links check-bin),
    # so both fold here too, and a target that leaves this prefix's package is not npm's own (the Bot's 4307029052).
    link="$(readlink "${entry}")" || link=""
    resolved="$(normalize_node_path "${entry%/*}" "${link}")" || return
    package_dir="$(normalize_node_path "${HOME}/.local/lib/node_modules/@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent")" || return
    if { [ -f "${entry}" ] || [ -L "${entry}" ]; } &&
        [[ "${resolved}" != "${package_dir}/"* ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are normalize_node_path forms
        aside="${HOME}/.local/share/agent-assets/omp/omp.previous"
        printf 'Moving %s to %s: npm does not own it%s.\n' "${entry}" "${aside}" "${link:+ (it points to ${link} and resolves to ${resolved})}"
        mkdir -p "${aside%/*}" && rm -rf "${aside}" && mv "${entry}" "${aside}" || return
    fi
    # Allow this reviewed pin before the default three-day cooldown expires.
    npm_config_min_release_age=0 npm install -g --prefix "${HOME}/.local" "${tarball}" &&
        installed="$("${entry}" --version 2> /dev/null | awk 'NR == 1 { print $NF }')" || installed=none
    installed="${installed#omp/}"
    if [ "${installed}" != "${OMP_PIN_VERSION}" ]; then
        [ -z "${aside}" ] || { rm -f "${entry}" && mv "${aside}" "${entry}" && printf 'Put the previous %s back.\n' "${entry}"; }
        printf 'omp version mismatch: expected %s, got %s.\n' "${OMP_PIN_VERSION}" "${installed}" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    manifest_record "update_omp" installer "${OMP_PIN_VERSION}" "${HOME}/.local/bin/omp" -- "npm_config_min_release_age=0 npm install -g --prefix ${HOME}/.local <verified-omp-tarball>"
)

#
# @description Verify the pinned platform wheel before uv installs hcom, and keep it where uv's receipt points.
# @exitcode 1 The download checksum or installed version differs from its pin.
#
function update_hcom() (
    local url expected installed download_dir wheel actual wheel_dir kernel machine platform
    platform="$(uname_platform)" || return 1
    read -r kernel machine <<< "${platform}"
    case "${kernel}-${machine}" in
    Darwin-arm64 | Darwin-aarch64) url="${HCOM_DARWIN_ARM64_URL}" expected="${HCOM_DARWIN_ARM64_SHA256}" ;;
    Darwin-x86_64 | Darwin-amd64) url="${HCOM_DARWIN_AMD64_URL}" expected="${HCOM_DARWIN_AMD64_SHA256}" ;;
    Linux-x86_64 | Linux-amd64) url="${HCOM_LINUX_AMD64_URL}" expected="${HCOM_LINUX_AMD64_SHA256}" ;;
    Linux-aarch64 | Linux-arm64) url="${HCOM_LINUX_ARM64_URL}" expected="${HCOM_LINUX_ARM64_SHA256}" ;;
    *)
        printf 'Skipping hcom: unsupported platform %s %s.\n' "${kernel}" "${machine}"
        return 0
        ;;
    esac
    has_command uv || {
        printf 'Skipping hcom: uv command not found.\n'
        return 0
    }
    section "hcom"
    # uv's receipt records the wheel's path as hcom's source and `uv tool upgrade` re-reads it, so the verified wheel
    # lives at a managed path that outlives the run.
    wheel_dir="${HOME}/.local/share/agent-assets/hcom"
    installed="$("${HOME}/.local/bin/hcom" --version 2> /dev/null | awk 'NR == 1 { print $NF }')" || installed=none
    # A pinned install without the retained wheel (one from before the wheel was kept) is reinstalled to repair it.
    if [ "${installed}" = "${HCOM_PIN_VERSION}" ] && [ -f "${wheel_dir}/${url##*/}" ]; then
        printf 'hcom %s is already installed.\n' "${installed}"
        return 0
    fi
    download_dir="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/update-agent-assets.XXXXXX")" || return
    trap 'rm -rf "${download_dir}"' EXIT
    wheel="${download_dir}/${url##*/}"
    curl -fsSL "${url}" -o "${wheel}" || return
    actual="$(shasum -a 256 "${wheel}" | awk '{ print $1 }')" || return
    if [ "${actual}" != "${expected}" ]; then
        printf 'hcom checksum mismatch: expected %s, got %s.\n' "${expected}" "${actual}" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    mkdir -p "${wheel_dir}" && mv -f "${wheel}" "${wheel_dir}/" || return
    wheel="${wheel_dir}/${url##*/}"
    # A failed install drops the retained wheel, so the next run retries instead of skipping on it (4303338055).
    uv tool install --force "${wheel}" || {
        rm -f "${wheel}"
        return 1
    }
    installed="$("${HOME}/.local/bin/hcom" --version 2> /dev/null | awk 'NR == 1 { print $NF }')" || installed=none
    if [ "${installed}" != "${HCOM_PIN_VERSION}" ]; then
        printf 'hcom version mismatch: expected %s, got %s.\n' "${HCOM_PIN_VERSION}" "${installed}" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    manifest_record "update_hcom" installer "${HCOM_PIN_VERSION}" "${HOME}/.local/bin/hcom" "${wheel}" -- "uv tool install --force <verified-hcom-wheel>"
)

#
# @description Print the inputs an installed pi-claude-bridge must match: the pinned tarball's sha256, then one
#   line per patch in application order, then bun.lock. The install writes these lines as the head of its RECEIPT.
# @stdout One `<file name> <sha256>` line per input.
# @exitcode 1 A patch or the lockfile is missing from home/dot_agents/assets/pi-claude-bridge.
#
function pi_claude_bridge_inputs() {
    local file sum
    printf 'pi-claude-bridge-%s.tgz %s\n' "${PI_CLAUDE_BRIDGE_PIN_VERSION}" "${PI_CLAUDE_BRIDGE_TARBALL_SHA256}"
    for file in "${PI_CLAUDE_BRIDGE_ASSET_DIR}"/patches/*.patch "${PI_CLAUDE_BRIDGE_ASSET_DIR}/bun.lock"; do
        [ -f "${file}" ] || {
            printf 'pi-claude-bridge asset file missing: %s\n' "${file}" >&2
            return 1
        }
        sum="$(shasum -a 256 "${file}")" || {
            printf 'shasum -a 256 could not hash %s; the pi-claude-bridge inputs are unknown\n' "${file}" >&2
            return 1
        }
        printf '%s %s\n' "${file##*/}" "${sum%% *}"
    done
}

#
# @description Install the pinned pi-claude-bridge tarball with this repository's patches and locked dependencies
#   as an omp extension directory, loaded with `omp -e <install dir>` (plan 025 decisions 30, 37, 38).
# @description
#   The tarball is verified against its reviewed sha256, the patches under
#   home/dot_agents/assets/pi-claude-bridge/patches apply in name order, Bun installs the dependency set the
#   committed bun.lock pins (peers excluded: omp's legacy pi compat layer provides them), and gap-check.ts refuses
#   a tree whose legacy pi imports omp's shims do not export, so an omp upgrade that drops one fails here instead
#   of in the first session. The staged tree replaces the install directory only after every check passes, and
#   a run whose RECEIPT already matches the pinned inputs changes nothing.
# @exitcode 1 A checksum, patch, dependency install or import check failed; the existing install is unchanged.
#
function update_pi_claude_bridge() (
    local install_dir="${HOME}/.local/lib/omp-extensions/pi-claude-bridge"
    local omp_dir="${HOME}/.local/lib/node_modules/@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent"
    local inputs receipt download_dir tarball actual staging="" patch_file previous
    has_command bun || {
        printf 'Skipping pi-claude-bridge: bun command not found.\n'
        return 0
    }
    [ -d "${omp_dir}" ] || {
        printf 'Skipping pi-claude-bridge: omp is not installed at %s.\n' "${omp_dir}"
        return 0
    }
    section "pi-claude-bridge"
    inputs="$(pi_claude_bridge_inputs)" || return
    # No readable RECEIPT is no match: the verified install runs again and writes it.
    receipt="$(sed -n '1,/^bun.lock /p' "${install_dir}/RECEIPT" 2> /dev/null)" || receipt=""
    if [ -d "${install_dir}/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk" ] &&
        [ "${receipt}" = "${inputs}" ]; then
        printf 'pi-claude-bridge %s is already installed.\n' "${PI_CLAUDE_BRIDGE_PIN_VERSION}"
    else
        download_dir="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/update-agent-assets.XXXXXX")" || return
        trap 'rm -rf "${download_dir}" ${staging:+"${staging}"}' EXIT
        tarball="${download_dir}/pi-claude-bridge-${PI_CLAUDE_BRIDGE_PIN_VERSION}.tgz"
        curl -fsSL "${PI_CLAUDE_BRIDGE_TARBALL_URL}" -o "${tarball}" || return
        actual="$(shasum -a 256 "${tarball}" | awk '{ print $1 }')" || return
        if [ "${actual}" != "${PI_CLAUDE_BRIDGE_TARBALL_SHA256}" ]; then
            printf 'pi-claude-bridge checksum mismatch: expected %s, got %s.\n' "${PI_CLAUDE_BRIDGE_TARBALL_SHA256}" "${actual}" >&2
            return 1
        fi
        # Staged beside the target so the final rename stays on one filesystem.
        mkdir -p "${install_dir%/*}" && staging="$(mktemp -d "${install_dir}.staging.XXXXXX")" || return
        tar xzf "${tarball}" -C "${staging}" --strip-components=1 || return
        for patch_file in "${PI_CLAUDE_BRIDGE_ASSET_DIR}"/patches/*.patch; do
            # -F0: GNU patch would apply a patch whose context drifted with fuzz and exit 0; Apple patch refuses either way.
            patch -p1 -s -F0 -d "${staging}" -i "${patch_file}" || {
                printf 'pi-claude-bridge patch %s did not apply.\n' "${patch_file##*/}" >&2
                return 1
            }
        done
        cp "${PI_CLAUDE_BRIDGE_ASSET_DIR}/bun.lock" "${staging}/bun.lock" || return
        (cd "${staging}" && bun install --production --omit=peer --frozen-lockfile) || return
        bun run "${PI_CLAUDE_BRIDGE_ASSET_DIR}/gap-check.ts" "${staging}/src" "${omp_dir}" || {
            printf 'pi-claude-bridge imports a name omp does not export (rows above); install refused.\n' >&2
            return 1
        }
        {
            printf '%s\n' "${inputs}"
            jq -r '"\(.name) \(.version)"' "${staging}"/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/*/package.json | LC_ALL=C sort
        } > "${staging}/RECEIPT" || return
        previous="${install_dir}.previous"
        rm -rf "${previous}"
        if [ -e "${install_dir}" ]; then
            mv "${install_dir}" "${previous}" || return
        fi
        mv "${staging}" "${install_dir}" || {
            [ ! -e "${previous}" ] || mv "${previous}" "${install_dir}"
            return 1
        }
        staging=""
        rm -rf "${previous}"
        printf 'pi-claude-bridge %s installed into %s.\n' "${PI_CLAUDE_BRIDGE_PIN_VERSION}" "${install_dir}"
        cat "${install_dir}/RECEIPT"
    fi
    manifest_record "update_pi_claude_bridge" installer "${PI_CLAUDE_BRIDGE_PIN_VERSION}" "${install_dir}" "${install_dir}/RECEIPT" "${install_dir}/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk" -- "curl -fsSL ${PI_CLAUDE_BRIDGE_TARBALL_URL}" "shasum -a 256 <tarball>" "patch -p1 -F0 -d <staging> -i <each home/dot_agents/assets/pi-claude-bridge/patches/*.patch in order>" "bun install --production --omit=peer --frozen-lockfile" "bun run gap-check.ts <staging>/src ${omp_dir}"
)

#
# @description Load the installed pi-claude-bridge in one omp session and fail on a load error.
# @description
#   `omp models` never evaluates extension modules, so the check is the session path: a one-prompt run under
#   `--no-extensions -e <install dir>` whose stderr and the omp log files it wrote must not contain `Failed to
#   load extension`, and which must reach the model (`PONG`, or `Not logged in` before the operator's /login).
#   Point HOME at a scratch directory to keep the session out of the real ~/.omp; under the real HOME a logged-in
#   host spends one short model turn.
# @exitcode 1 omp reported a load error or did not reach the model; omp's output is printed above the verdict.
#
function check_pi_claude_bridge() {
    local install_dir="${HOME}/.local/lib/omp-extensions/pi-claude-bridge" marker output failed_logs
    [ -d "${install_dir}" ] || {
        printf 'pi-claude-bridge is not installed at %s; run make update.\n' "${install_dir}" >&2
        return 1
    }
    marker="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/update-agent-assets.XXXXXX")" || return
    output="$(perl -e 'alarm 90; exec @ARGV' omp --no-extensions -e "${install_dir}" --no-session --model claude-bridge/claude-haiku-4-5 --max-time 60 -p "Reply with the single word PONG." 2>&1)" || true
    printf '%s\n' "${output}"
    # The stderr line is truncated to the display width; the log carries the full error.
    failed_logs="$(find "${HOME}/.omp/logs" -name 'omp.*.log' -newer "${marker}" -exec grep -l 'Failed to load extension' {} + 2> /dev/null || true)"
    rm -f "${marker}"
    if printf '%s\n' "${output}" | grep -q 'Failed to load extension' || [ -n "${failed_logs}" ]; then
        printf 'pi-claude-bridge did not load in omp%s.\n' "${failed_logs:+; omp log: ${failed_logs}}" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if ! printf '%s\n' "${output}" | grep -Eq 'PONG|Not logged in'; then
        printf 'pi-claude-bridge loaded but omp did not reach the model.\n' >&2
        return 1
    fi
    local version
    version="$(omp_version_label)"
    printf 'pi-claude-bridge loaded in %s.\n' "${version}"
}

#
# @description Print the version `omp --version` reports on its first line, or `unknown` when omp cannot report
#   one: the version only labels a success message, so its read failing changes no decision.
#
function omp_version_label() {
    local output
    if output="$(omp --version 2> /dev/null)"; then
        awk 'NR == 1 { print $NF }' <<< "${output}"
    else
        printf 'unknown\n'
    fi
}

#
# @description Confirm the pstack skills chezmoi places under ~/.agents/skills reach an omp seat.
# @description
#   No installer step runs for pstack: the two externals in home/.chezmoitemplates/chezmoiexternal.d/common.yaml.tmpl
#   deploy the pinned plugin's skills/* and docs/** (assets.pstack in the manifest) at every chezmoi apply. The check
#   fails when the poteto-mode skill or the Claude Code adapter its first paragraph links is missing, or when
#   `omp skill list`, run from an empty directory so no project skill tree takes part, does not name poteto-mode.
#   Without omp the file check alone decides.
# @exitcode 1 A file is missing or omp does not list the skill; omp's listing is printed above the verdict.
#
function check_pstack() {
    local file cwd listing count version
    for file in "${HOME}/.agents/skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md" "${HOME}/.agents/docs/harness/claude-code.md"; do
        [ -f "${file}" ] || {
            printf 'pstack: %s is missing; run make update.\n' "${file}" >&2
            return 1
        }
    done
    has_command omp || {
        printf 'pstack skills are in place; omp is not installed, so the seat listing is not checked.\n'
        return 0
    }
    cwd="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/update-agent-assets.XXXXXX")" || return
    listing="$(cd "${cwd}" && perl -e 'alarm 60; exec @ARGV' omp --no-session skill list --json 2> /dev/null)" || true
    rmdir "${cwd}"
    if ! printf '%s\n' "${listing}" | jq -e '.skills[] | select(.name == "poteto-mode")' > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        printf '%s\n' "${listing}" >&2
        printf 'pstack: omp skill list does not name poteto-mode.\n' >&2
        return 1
    fi
    count="$(jq '.skills | length' <<< "${listing}")" || return 1
    version="$(omp_version_label)"
    printf 'pstack skills reach %s: %s skills listed, poteto-mode among them.\n' "${version}" "${count}"
}

#
# @description Sync the vendored CompactionDB tree without deleting project runtime state.
#
function update_compactiondb() {
    local source_root version
    source_root="${DOTFILES_REPO_SOURCE_DIR}/vendor/compactiondb/"
    rsync -a --delete --exclude '.claude/contextdb/state/' --exclude '.claude/contextdb/spool/' --exclude '.claude/contextdb/health/' --exclude '.claude/contextdb/contextdb.sqlite3*' "${source_root}" "${HOME}/.agents/compactiondb/" || true
    version="$(awk '/^## / { print $2; exit }' "${source_root}CHANGELOG.md")" || {
        printf 'Cannot read the CompactionDB version from %sCHANGELOG.md.\n' "${source_root}" >&2
        return 1
    }
    manifest_record "update_compactiondb" rsync "${version}" "${HOME}/.agents/compactiondb" -- "rsync -a --delete --exclude .claude/contextdb/state/ --exclude .claude/contextdb/spool/ --exclude .claude/contextdb/health/ --exclude .claude/contextdb/contextdb.sqlite3* ${source_root} ${HOME}/.agents/compactiondb/"
}

#
# @description Install and refresh managed agent plugin assets.
# @arg $1 string Optional single step to run alone: update_pi_claude_bridge, check_pi_claude_bridge or check_pstack.
#
function main() {
    if [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; then
        case "$#:$1" in
        1:update_pi_claude_bridge | 1:check_pi_claude_bridge | 1:check_pstack)
            export PATH="${HOME}/.local/share/mise/shims:${PATH}"
            "$1"
            return
            ;;
        esac
        printf 'Usage: scripts/update-agent-assets.sh [update_pi_claude_bridge | check_pi_claude_bridge | check_pstack]\n' >&2
        exit 2
    fi

    export PATH="${HOME}/.local/share/mise/shims:${PATH}"
    remove_node_global_agent_cli_shadows
    ensure_mise_npm_agent_cli claude "npm:@anthropic-ai/claude-code"
    ensure_mise_npm_agent_cli codex "npm:@openai/codex"
    ensure_gh_extensions
    update_claude_superpowers
    update_claude_crit
    update_claude_ponytail
    update_claude_understand_anything
    update_codex_superpowers
    update_codex_crit
    update_codex_ponytail
    update_codex_understand_anything
    update_terminal_code
    update_terminal_browser
    update_omp
    update_pi_claude_bridge
    update_hcom
    update_compactiondb
    ensure_herdr_integrations
    manifest_prune_retired
    # After every plugin update above, so the trust hashes follow the plugin content of this run.
    refresh_codex_hook_trust
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
    main "$@"
fi
</code></pre>

The default mode updates user-level tooling and Homebrew-managed packages when those managers are available. Pass --system to include operating-system package upgrades such as apt. The network-only phases (Homebrew, mise self-update, uv tools, gh extensions) only warn when they fail, so an offline host still converges; installing the declared mise tools stays required, while a per-tool upgrade that fails only warns. <pre><code>#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file scripts/upgrade-tools.sh
# @brief Update installed tools to the latest safe versions; `make update` runs it after `chezmoi apply`.
# @description
#   Each manager's own safety features decide what the latest safe version is:
#   mise's minimum_release_age and verification settings in the applied
#   ~/.config/mise/config.toml, and a manager's own hold (an exact version in
#   that config, brew pin, uv tool install <pkg>==<version>, apt-mark hold).
#   The default mode updates user-level tooling and Homebrew-managed packages
#   when those managers are available. Pass `--system` to include
#   operating-system package upgrades such as apt. The network-only phases
#   (Homebrew, mise self-update, uv tools, gh extensions) only warn when they
#   fail, so an offline host still converges; installing the declared mise tools
#   stays required, while a per-tool upgrade that fails only warns. It edits no repository file, and exits 0 without changes
#   when CI=true.

set -Eeuo pipefail

# dirname is captured on its own line: inside the cd its status would be lost.
script_dir="$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" || {
    echo "upgrade-tools: dirname failed on ${BASH_SOURCE[0]}; the repository root is unknown" >&2
    exit 1
}
repo_root="$(cd "${script_dir}/.." && pwd)" || exit 1
# chezmoi applies home/dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl to ~/.config/mise whatever XDG_CONFIG_HOME
# says, so mise reads exactly that config: no inherited MISE_CONFIG_DIR, and the isolated Git
# config's XDG_CONFIG_HOME below cannot redirect it.
export MISE_CONFIG_DIR="${HOME}/.config/mise"
# No project config from this checkout upward joins the inventory, so only the host config's tools move.
export MISE_CEILING_PATHS="${repo_root}"

include_system=false
DEFAULT_FORBIDDEN_HOMEBREW_FORMULAE="node node@* python python@* python3 pip npm pnpm yarn claude"
required_failures=0
optional_warnings=0

#
# @description Print a section heading.
# @arg $1 string Heading text.
#
function section() {
    printf '\n==> %s\n' "$1"
}

#
# @description Return success when the current OS is macOS.
# @exitcode 1 Also exits the script when uname fails: a failed read is not "another OS".
#
function is_macos() {
    local kernel
    kernel="$(uname)" || {
        echo "uname failed; cannot tell whether this host is macOS" >&2
        exit 1
    }
    [ "${kernel}" = "Darwin" ]
}

#
# @description Return success when the current OS is Linux.
# @exitcode 1 Also exits the script when uname fails: a failed read is not "another OS".
#
function is_linux() {
    local kernel
    kernel="$(uname)" || {
        echo "uname failed; cannot tell whether this host is Linux" >&2
        exit 1
    }
    [ "${kernel}" = "Linux" ]
}

#
# @description Return success when a command is available.
# @arg $1 string Command name.
#
function has_command() {
    command -v "$1" > /dev/null 2>&1
}

#
# @description Run a required upgrade phase and record failure without stopping later phases.
# @arg $1 string Phase label.
# @arg $2 string Function name.
#
function run_required_phase() {
    local label="$1"
    shift

    if ! "$@"; then
        printf 'required failure: %s\n' "${label}" >&2
        ((required_failures += 1))
    fi
}

#
# @description Run an optional upgrade phase and record warning-only failure.
# @arg $1 string Phase label.
# @arg $2 string Function name.
#
function run_optional_phase() {
    local label="$1"
    shift

    if ! "$@"; then
        printf 'optional warning: %s failed\n' "${label}" >&2
        ((optional_warnings += 1))
    fi
}

#
# @description Return success when the named Homebrew formula is forbidden.
# @arg $1 string Formula name.
#
function is_forbidden_homebrew_formula() {
    local formula="$1"
    local forbidden_formula

    for forbidden_formula in ${DEFAULT_FORBIDDEN_HOMEBREW_FORMULAE} ${HOMEBREW_FORBIDDEN_FORMULAE:-}; do
        # shellcheck disable=SC2254 # Forbidden formula entries intentionally support glob patterns.
        case "${formula}" in
        ${forbidden_formula})
            return 0
            ;;
        esac
    done

    return 1
}

#
# @description Upgrade Homebrew packages on macOS when Homebrew is installed.
#
function upgrade_homebrew() {
    if ! is_macos; then
        return 0
    fi
    has_command brew || return 1

    section "Homebrew"
    if has_command gh; then
        # Homebrew verifies bottle build-provenance attestations through gh (HOMEBREW_VERIFY_ATTESTATIONS).
        local -x HOMEBREW_VERIFY_ATTESTATIONS=1
    else
        printf 'gh not found; Homebrew bottle attestation verification is skipped.\n'
    fi
    brew update || return

    local outdated_formula
    local outdated_formulae_output
    local outdated_formulae=()
    local upgrade_formulae=()
    outdated_formulae_output="$(brew outdated --formula --quiet)" || return
    if [ -n "${outdated_formulae_output}" ]; then
        while IFS= read -r outdated_formula; do
            outdated_formulae+=("${outdated_formula}")
        done <<< "${outdated_formulae_output}"
    fi

    if [ "${#outdated_formulae[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
        for outdated_formula in "${outdated_formulae[@]}"; do
            if is_forbidden_homebrew_formula "${outdated_formula}"; then
                printf 'Skipping forbidden Homebrew formula: %s\n' "${outdated_formula}"
                continue
            fi

            upgrade_formulae+=("${outdated_formula}")
        done
    fi

    if [ "${#upgrade_formulae[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
        # Homebrew asks for confirmation by default (brew upgrade --help); make update must not wait.
        HOMEBREW_NO_ASK=1 HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALLED_DEPENDENTS_CHECK=1 brew upgrade --formula "${upgrade_formulae[@]}" || return
    else
        printf 'No upgradeable Homebrew formulae after forbidden formula filtering.\n'
    fi

    local outdated_cask
    local outdated_casks_output
    local outdated_casks=()
    outdated_casks_output="$(brew outdated --cask --quiet)" || return
    if [ -n "${outdated_casks_output}" ]; then
        while IFS= read -r outdated_cask; do
            outdated_casks+=("${outdated_cask}")
        done <<< "${outdated_casks_output}"
    fi

    if [ "${#outdated_casks[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
        HOMEBREW_NO_ASK=1 HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALLED_DEPENDENTS_CHECK=1 brew upgrade --cask --skip-cask-deps "${outdated_casks[@]}" || return
    else
        printf 'No outdated Homebrew casks.\n'
    fi
}

#
# @description Upgrade standalone mise or skip package-manager-managed installations.
# @stdout Skip message when an official package-manager marker is present.
#
function upgrade_mise_self() {
    local mise_executable
    local mise_dir
    local mise_prefix

    has_command mise || return 1
    mise_executable="$(type -P mise)" || return 1
    mise_dir="$(dirname -- "${mise_executable}")" || return
    mise_prefix="$(cd "${mise_dir}/.." && pwd -P)" || return

    section "mise self-update"
    if [[ -f "${mise_prefix}/lib/mise-self-update-instructions.toml" ||
        -f "${mise_prefix}/lib/mise/mise-self-update-instructions.toml" ]]; then
        printf 'Skipping mise self-update: managed by package manager.\n'
        return 0
    fi

    # Plugin updates are branch moves the release-age cooldown does not cover.
    mise self-update --yes --no-plugins
}

#
# @description Run mise while hiding user-level Git config from package backend operations.
# @arg $@ string Mise command and arguments.
#
function run_mise_with_isolated_git_config() {
    local isolated_xdg_config_home
    local mise_config_dir
    local status

    mise_config_dir="${MISE_CONFIG_DIR}"
    isolated_xdg_config_home="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/mise-git-config.XXXXXX")"
    GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 \
        GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null \
        XDG_CONFIG_HOME="${isolated_xdg_config_home}" \
        MISE_CONFIG_DIR="${mise_config_dir}" \
        mise "$@"
    status="$?"
    rm -rf "${isolated_xdg_config_home}" 2> /dev/null || true
    return "${status}"
}

#
# @description Print mise tool names from the current configuration.
# @stdout One tool name per line.
#
function current_mise_tools() {
    run_mise_with_isolated_git_config ls --current --no-header | awk '{print $1}'
}

#
# @description Run a mise lifecycle command for each current tool; only upgrade is per tool.
# @arg $1 string Mise command name: upgrade.
# @exitcode 1 When the current tools cannot be listed.
# @exitcode 2 When the command failed for at least one tool.
#
function run_mise_tool_command() {
    local mise_command="$1"
    local mise_tool
    local mise_tools
    local failed=0

    if ! mise_tools="$(current_mise_tools)"; then
        printf 'warning: unable to list current mise tools for %s; continuing\n' "${mise_command}" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    while IFS= read -r mise_tool; do
        if [ -z "${mise_tool}" ]; then
            continue
        fi

        if [[ "${mise_tool}" == http:* ]]; then
            printf 'Skipping mise upgrade for pinned HTTP tool: %s.\n' "${mise_tool}"
            continue
        fi
        # ponytail: keep fd pinned until upstream publishes macOS x64 assets again.
        if [ "${mise_tool}" = "fd" ]; then
            printf 'Skipping mise upgrade for fd: newer releases lack a macOS x64 asset.\n'
            continue
        fi
        # A plain upgrade keeps the config's "latest" or exact request as written.
        if ! run_mise_with_isolated_git_config upgrade --yes "${mise_tool}"; then
            printf 'warning: mise %s failed for %s; continuing\n' "${mise_command}" "${mise_tool}" >&2
            failed=2
        fi
    done <<< "${mise_tools}"

    return "${failed}"
}

#
# @description Rebuild one npm: tool on the current node, keeping its working install until the new one succeeds.
#   mise install --force would delete the install before downloading its
#   replacement, so a rebuild without a network would leave the tool missing.
# @arg $1 string mise npm tool name, for example npm:ccusage.
#
function rebuild_mise_npm_tool() {
    local mise_tool="$1"
    local version install_dir backup

    version="$(run_mise_with_isolated_git_config current "${mise_tool}")" || return 1
    install_dir="$(run_mise_with_isolated_git_config where "${mise_tool}")" || return 1
    # Only an existing absolute install directory is moved or removed.
    [[ -n "${version}" && "${install_dir}" == /* ]] || return 1
    backup="${install_dir}.before-node-rebuild"
    # restore_interrupted_npm_rebuilds put any leftover backup back; never move an install into one.
    [[ -d "${install_dir}" && ! -e "${backup}" ]] || return 1
    mv "${install_dir}" "${backup}" || return 1
    # Until the new install succeeds, an interruption or exit puts the working install back.
    local restore
    restore="$(printf 'restore_npm_install %q %q' "${install_dir}" "${backup}")"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2064 # Expanded now on purpose: the paths are this function's locals.
    trap "${restore}; exit 130" INT
    # shellcheck disable=SC2064
    trap "${restore}; exit 143" TERM
    # shellcheck disable=SC2064
    trap "${restore}" EXIT
    if run_mise_with_isolated_git_config install --yes "${mise_tool}@${version}"; then
        trap - INT TERM EXIT
        # Renamed before it is deleted, so a backup that cannot be fully deleted is never restored over this
        # install; the dot keeps a leftover out of mise's installed versions.
        local discard="${install_dir%/*}/.${install_dir##*/}.discarded-after-rebuild"
        rm -rf "${discard}"
        mv "${backup}" "${discard}" || return 1
        rm -rf "${discard}" || printf 'warning: could not delete %s; nothing uses it\n' "${discard}" >&2
        return 0
    fi
    trap - INT TERM EXIT
    restore_npm_install "${install_dir}" "${backup}"
    return 1
}

#
# @description Put back every npm: install that a rebuild killed past its traps (SIGKILL, power loss) left
#   moved aside. It runs before any mise command, because mise cannot name an install that is not in place.
#
function restore_interrupted_npm_rebuilds() {
    local backup
    local failed=0
    # mise's own installs directory resolution: MISE_INSTALLS_DIR, then the data directory (MISE_DATA_DIR, then XDG_DATA_HOME).
    local installs="${MISE_INSTALLS_DIR:-${MISE_DATA_DIR:-${XDG_DATA_HOME:-${HOME}/.local/share}/mise}/installs}"
    for backup in "${installs}"/*/*.before-node-rebuild; do
        [ -d "${backup}" ] || continue
        restore_npm_install "${backup%.before-node-rebuild}" "${backup}" || failed=1
    done
    return "${failed}"
}

#
# @description Put a moved-aside npm: install back, replacing whatever a failed or interrupted install left.
# @arg $1 path The install directory.
# @arg $2 path The moved-aside working install.
#
function restore_npm_install() {
    [ -d "$2" ] || return 0
    # The backup moves only onto a path that is gone, so it is never buried inside a partial install that survives.
    if rm -rf "$1" && [ ! -e "$1" ] && mv "$2" "$1"; then
        return 0
    fi
    printf 'required failure: could not restore %s from %s\n' "$1" "$2" >&2
    ((required_failures += 1))
    return 1
}

#
# @description Rebuild the current npm: tools so they run on the current node.
#
function reinstall_mise_npm_tools() {
    local mise_tool
    local mise_tools
    local failed=0

    mise_tools="$(current_mise_tools)" || return 1
    while IFS= read -r mise_tool; do
        [[ "${mise_tool}" == npm:* ]] || continue
        if ! rebuild_mise_npm_tool "${mise_tool}"; then
            printf 'warning: rebuilding %s on the current node failed; its previous install stays; continuing\n' "${mise_tool}" >&2
            failed=1
        fi
    done <<< "${mise_tools}"

    return "${failed}"
}

#
# @description Install missing and upgrade outdated mise tools declared in the applied host config.
#
function upgrade_mise_tools() {
    has_command mise || return 1

    section "mise tools"
    local failed=0
    restore_interrupted_npm_rebuilds || failed=1
    mise trust --yes || failed=1
    # minimum_release_age in the config keeps freshly published releases out of both steps.
    # One bare install: it leaves installed tools alone offline, while a per-tool
    # install re-resolves "latest" over the network and fails without one.
    run_mise_with_isolated_git_config install --yes || failed=1
    # Upgrades need the network; an installed tool that cannot move yet is still converged.
    local upgrade_status=0
    run_mise_tool_command upgrade || upgrade_status=$?
    if [ "${upgrade_status}" -eq 2 ]; then
        printf 'optional warning: mise upgrade failed for at least one tool; its installed version stays\n' >&2
        ((optional_warnings += 1))
    elif [ "${upgrade_status}" -ne 0 ]; then
        failed=1
    fi
    # Neither the bare install nor the upgrades rebuild installed npm: tools, and node can also have moved
    # in an earlier run or under the installer, so a marker records the node they were last built on.
    local marker="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-${HOME}/.local/state}/dotfiles/npm-tools-node"
    local node_built="" node_now="" reinstalled=0
    if [ -r "${marker}" ]; then
        node_built="$(cat "${marker}")"
    fi
    node_now="$(run_mise_with_isolated_git_config current node 2> /dev/null)" || node_now=""
    if [ -n "${node_now}" ] && [ "${node_now}" != "${node_built}" ]; then
        if reinstall_mise_npm_tools; then
            reinstalled=1
        else
            printf 'optional warning: npm: tools were not all reinstalled on node %s\n' "${node_now}" >&2
            ((optional_warnings += 1))
        fi
        # A rebuild keeps or restores the previous install, so this final bare install only has to confirm
        # that every declared tool is present; it decides whether the phase converged.
        if ! run_mise_with_isolated_git_config install --yes; then
            failed=1
        elif [ "${reinstalled}" -eq 1 ]; then
            # Only a complete rebuild is recorded, so a failed one is retried by the next run.
            if ! { mkdir -p "$(dirname "${marker}")" && printf '%s\n' "${node_now}" > "${marker}"; }; then
                printf 'required: could not record the npm-tools node in %s\n' "${marker}" >&2
                failed=1
            fi
        fi
    fi
    return "${failed}"
}

#
# @description Print the manifest pin of an asset installed from a wheel (an assets.<name>.files URL ending in .whl), or nothing.
# @arg $1 string Asset name.
#
function manifest_wheel_pin() {
    # shortcut: reads the unquoted block style of home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml line by line, not as YAML; use a parser if assets: gains quotes or flow style.
    awk -v name="$1" '
        /^[^ #]/ { in_assets = ($0 ~ /^assets:/) }
        in_assets && /^  [^ #]/ { asset = $1; sub(/:$/, "", asset) }
        in_assets && asset == name && /^    pin:/ { pin = $2 }
        in_assets && asset == name && /\.whl$/ { wheel = 1 }
        END { if (wheel) print pin }
    ' "${repo_root}/home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml"
}

#
# @description Upgrade uv tool installations when uv is available, except the ones the manifest pins from a wheel.
#
function upgrade_uv_tools() {
    local tools tool pin failed=0
    has_command uv || return 1

    section "uv tools"
    # Plain text even where FORCE_COLOR or CLICOLOR_FORCE is set (herdr-agents panes): uv colours tool names there.
    tools="$(uv tool list --color never)" || return
    # Tool lines read "<name> v<version>"; their entry points follow as "- <command>".
    for tool in $(printf '%s\n' "${tools}" | awk '/^[^- ]/ { print $1 }'); do
        pin="$(manifest_wheel_pin "${tool}")" || return
        if [ -n "${pin}" ]; then
            # uv's receipt names the local wheel, so an index upgrade has nothing to move; update-agent-assets.sh does.
            printf 'skip: %s (manifest pins %s from a wheel)\n' "${tool}" "${pin}"
        else
            uv tool upgrade "${tool}" || failed=1
        fi
    done
    return "${failed}"
}

#
# @description Upgrade GitHub CLI extensions when gh is available.
#
function upgrade_gh_extensions() {
    if ! has_command gh; then
        return 0
    fi

    section "GitHub CLI extensions"
    gh extension upgrade --all
}

#
# @description Upgrade apt packages only when system upgrades are requested.
#
function upgrade_apt_packages() {
    if ! ${include_system} || ! is_linux; then
        return 0
    fi
    has_command apt-get || return 1

    section "apt"
    sudo --preserve-env=http_proxy,https_proxy,no_proxy apt-get update || return
    sudo --preserve-env=http_proxy,https_proxy,no_proxy apt-get upgrade -y
}

#
# @description Parse command-line options.
# @arg $@ string Command-line arguments.
#
function parse_args() {
    while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
        case "$1" in
        --system)
            include_system=true
            ;;
        -h | --help)
            cat << 'USAGE'
Usage: scripts/upgrade-tools.sh [--system]

Update installed tools to the latest safe versions; make update runs it.

Options:
  --system  Include operating-system package upgrades such as apt.
USAGE
            exit 0
            ;;
        *)
            printf 'Unknown option: %s\n' "$1" >&2
            exit 2
            ;;
        esac
        shift
    done
}

#
# @description Update installed tools through each manager.
# @arg $@ string Command-line arguments.
#
function main() {
    parse_args "$@"
    # A CI runner's tools belong to its image, not to this machine's update.
    if [ "${CI:-false}" = true ]; then
        printf 'CI=true: skipping installed-tool updates.\n'
        return 0
    fi

    # Network-only phases warn and continue, so make update still converges offline.
    run_optional_phase "Homebrew" upgrade_homebrew
    run_optional_phase "mise self-update" upgrade_mise_self
    run_required_phase "mise inventory/install/upgrade" upgrade_mise_tools
    run_optional_phase "uv tool upgrade" upgrade_uv_tools
    run_optional_phase "GitHub CLI extension upgrade" upgrade_gh_extensions
    run_required_phase "apt system upgrade" upgrade_apt_packages

    printf '\nUpgrade summary: required failures: %d; optional warnings: %d\n' \
        "${required_failures}" "${optional_warnings}"
    [ "${required_failures}" -eq 0 ]
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
    main "$@"
fi
</code></pre>

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file scripts/usage-snapshot.sh
# @brief Capture one daily ccusage snapshot for usage reviews.
# @description
#   Stores weekly and daily ccusage JSON in the repository worklog. Existing
#   snapshots are left unchanged, and unavailable or failing ccusage commands
#   warn without failing scheduled lifecycle runs.

set -Eeuo pipefail

# dirname is captured on its own line: inside the cd its status would be lost.
script_dir="$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" || {
    echo "usage-snapshot: dirname failed on ${BASH_SOURCE[0]}; the repository root is unknown" >&2
    exit 1
}
repo_root="$(cd "${script_dir}/.." && pwd)" || exit 1
usage_dir="${repo_root}/.agents/worklog/claude/usage"
snapshot_date="$(date +%Y%m%d)"
snapshot_path="${usage_dir}/${snapshot_date}.json"

if [[ -e "${snapshot_path}" ]]; then
    printf 'Usage snapshot already exists: %s\n' "${snapshot_path}"
    exit 0
fi

if ! command -v ccusage > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf 'WARN: ccusage is unavailable; usage snapshot skipped.\n' >&2
    exit 0
fi

if ! weekly_json="$(ccusage weekly --json)"; then
    printf 'WARN: ccusage weekly failed; usage snapshot skipped.\n' >&2
    exit 0
fi
if ! daily_json="$(ccusage daily --json)"; then
    printf 'WARN: ccusage daily failed; usage snapshot skipped.\n' >&2
    exit 0
fi

mkdir -p "${usage_dir}"
captured_at="$(date '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z')"
temporary_path="${snapshot_path}.tmp.$$"
trap 'rm -f "${temporary_path}"' EXIT
printf '{"captured_at":"%s","weekly":%s,"daily":%s}\n' \
    "${captured_at}" "${weekly_json}" "${daily_json}" > "${temporary_path}"
if ln "${temporary_path}" "${snapshot_path}" 2> /dev/null; then
    rm -f "${temporary_path}"
    trap - EXIT
elif [[ -e "${snapshot_path}" ]]; then
    printf 'Usage snapshot already exists: %s\n' "${snapshot_path}"
    exit 0
else
    printf 'WARN: unable to publish usage snapshot: %s\n' "${snapshot_path}" >&2
    exit 0
fi

printf 'Usage snapshot captured: %s\n' "${snapshot_path}"

This check parses each file with shfmt (shfmt -ln bash --to-json) and reports every command substitution ($(…) or backquotes) that opens inside another one, as file:line: … at the line where the inner one opens; capture the inner result first, or split a path in the shell (${path%/*}, ${path##*/}). The rule does not look at the command name: matching names lost four audit rounds to spellings bash resolves at run time ($'\544irname', command -p dirname, exec -a x dirname, /usr/bin/dirname), and SC2312 already refuses the other commands in this shape, so the linted groups held no nested substitution when the rule was set (regime-cutover U38b). A heredoc body whose delimiter has any quoted or escaped part is literal and skipped, as bash reads it (shfmt expands the body of a partly quoted delimiter such as <<'E'OF). The files are parsed as bash: make shellcheck passes only bash scripts, and bash also parses the repository's POSIX scripts. A file shfmt cannot parse is refused, never read as clean; that includes a heredoc delimiter with ANSI-C escapes (<<$'\x45OF'), which shfmt 3.14.1 and ShellCheck 0.11.0 both fail to terminate.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file masked-dirname-check.sh
# @brief Refuse a command substitution nested inside another one, the shape SC2312 lets through for dirname and basename.
# @description
#   ShellCheck's SC2312 (check-extra-masked-returns) exempts dirname and basename, so the U31 shape
#   `dir=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd -P)` passes it although the inner status is
#   lost. This check parses each file with shfmt (`shfmt -ln bash --to-json`) and reports every
#   command substitution (`$(…)` or backquotes) that opens inside another one, as `file:line: …` at
#   the line where the inner one opens; capture the inner result first, or split a path in the shell
#   (`${path%/*}`, `${path##*/}`). The rule does not look at the command name: matching names lost
#   four audit rounds to spellings bash resolves at run time (`$'\544irname'`, `command -p dirname`,
#   `exec -a x dirname`, `/usr/bin/dirname`), and SC2312 already refuses the other commands in this
#   shape, so the linted groups held no nested substitution when the rule was set (regime-cutover
#   U38b). A heredoc body whose delimiter has any quoted or escaped part is literal and skipped, as
#   bash reads it (shfmt expands the body of a partly quoted delimiter such as `<<'E'OF`).
#   The files are parsed as bash: `make shellcheck` passes only bash scripts, and bash also parses
#   the repository's POSIX scripts. A file shfmt cannot parse is refused, never read as clean; that
#   includes a heredoc delimiter with ANSI-C escapes (`<<$'\x45OF'`), which shfmt 3.14.1 and
#   ShellCheck 0.11.0 both fail to terminate.
# @arg $@ path The files to check (the ShellCheck groups of `make shellcheck`).
# @env SHFMT The shfmt to run (default `shfmt` on PATH; CI puts the mise-pinned 3.14.1 there).
# @exitcode 0 No command substitution nested inside another.
# @exitcode 1 At least one finding, each printed as `file:line: …`.
# @exitcode 2 No file given, a listed file cannot be read or parsed, or shfmt or python3 is missing:
#   the list is refused, never read as clean.
# @example
#   scripts/ci/masked-dirname-check.sh scripts/orchestrator/hcom-seat
set -euo pipefail

shfmt=${SHFMT:-shfmt}

if (($# == 0)); then
    echo "masked-dirname-check: no file to check; an empty list is refused" >&2
    exit 2
fi

for tool in "${shfmt}" python3; do
    if ! command -v "${tool}" > /dev/null; then
        echo "masked-dirname-check: ${tool} not found; the list is refused" >&2
        exit 2
    fi
done

for file in "$@"; do
    if [[ ! -f ${file} || ! -r ${file} ]]; then
        echo "masked-dirname-check: cannot read ${file}; the list is refused" >&2
        exit 2
    fi
done

# Reads shfmt's typed JSON on stdin; argv[1] names the file. Exits 1 when it prints a finding.
walk=$(
    cat << 'PY'
import json
import sys

MESSAGE = "a command substitution inside another one loses its status; capture it first, or split a path in the shell"


def quoted(word):
    """Whether any part of the word is quoted or escaped."""
    return any(
        part.get("Type") in ("SglQuoted", "DblQuoted") or (part.get("Type") == "Lit" and "\\" in part["Value"])
        for part in word.get("Parts") or []
    )


findings = set()


def walk(node, depth):
    if isinstance(node, list):
        for item in node:
            walk(item, depth)
        return
    if not isinstance(node, dict):
        return
    if node.get("Type") == "CmdSubst":
        if depth:
            findings.add(node["Pos"]["Line"])
        depth += 1
    elif node.get("Hdoc") and quoted(node["Word"]):
        # shfmt 3.14.1 parses the body of a partly quoted delimiter (`<<'E'OF`, `<<E"O"F`) as expanded text;
        # bash makes the body literal once any part of the delimiter is quoted.
        node = {key: value for key, value in node.items() if key != "Hdoc"}
    for value in node.values():
        walk(value, depth)


walk(json.load(sys.stdin), 0)
for line in sorted(findings):
    print(f"{sys.argv[1]}:{line}: {MESSAGE}")
sys.exit(1 if findings else 0)
PY
)

status=0
for file in "$@"; do
    if ! tree=$("${shfmt}" -ln bash --to-json < "${file}"); then
        echo "masked-dirname-check: shfmt cannot parse ${file}; the list is refused" >&2
        exit 2
    fi
    python3 -c "${walk}" "${file}" <<< "${tree}" || {
        code=$?
        if ((code != 1)); then
            echo "masked-dirname-check: cannot walk the syntax tree of ${file} (python3 exit ${code}); the list is refused" >&2
            exit 2
        fi
        status=1
    }
done
exit "${status}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file scripts/lib/asset-manifest.sh
# @brief Record installed agent assets in a private atomic JSON manifest.

#
# @description Return the installed version of a Claude Code plugin, or `unknown` when the plugin
#   list cannot be read or does not name it: the manifest records what it could not read as such.
# @arg $1 string Fully qualified Claude Code plugin ID.
#
function manifest_claude_plugin_version() {
    local plugin_id="$1"
    local listing version

    if listing="$(claude plugin list --json 2> /dev/null)" &&
        version="$(jq -er --arg id "${plugin_id}" 'first(.[] | select(.id == $id) | .version)' <<< "${listing}" 2> /dev/null)"; then
        printf '%s\n' "${version}"
    else
        printf 'unknown\n'
    fi
}

#
# @description Return the installed version of a Codex plugin, or `unknown` when the plugin list
#   cannot be read or does not name it.
# @arg $1 string Fully qualified Codex plugin ID.
#
function manifest_codex_plugin_version() {
    local plugin_id="$1"
    local listing version

    if listing="$(codex plugin list --json 2> /dev/null)" &&
        version="$(jq -er --arg id "${plugin_id}" 'first(.installed[] | select(.pluginId == $id) | .version)' <<< "${listing}" 2> /dev/null)"; then
        printf '%s\n' "${version}"
    else
        printf 'unknown\n'
    fi
}

#
# @description Return the installed Homebrew formula version, or `unknown` when brew cannot list it
#   (a formula that is not installed makes `brew list --versions` fail).
# @arg $1 string Homebrew formula name.
#
function manifest_brew_formula_version() {
    local formula="$1"
    local listing version=""

    if listing="$(brew list --versions "${formula}" 2> /dev/null)"; then
        version="$(awk -v formula="${formula}" '$1 == formula { print $2; exit }' <<< "${listing}")" || version=""
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "${version:-unknown}"
}

#
# @description Atomically replace one step in the installed asset manifest.
# @arg $1 string Install step name.
# @arg $2 string Asset kind.
# @arg $3 string Installed source version.
# @arg $@ string Absolute paths followed by an optional `--` and command lines.
#
function _manifest_record() {
    [ "$#" -ge 3 ] || return 1

    local step="$1"
    local kind="$2"
    local source_version="$3"
    local manifest_directory manifest_path temporary_path paths_json commands_json installed_at path
    local -a paths=()
    local -a commands=()
    shift 3

    case "${kind}" in
    plugin | rsync | brew | installer | integration) ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
    esac
    [ -n "${step}" ] && [ -n "${source_version}" ] && [ -n "${HOME:-}" ] || return 1

    while [ "$#" -gt 0 ] && [ "$1" != "--" ]; do
        paths+=("$1")
        shift
    done
    if [ "${1:-}" = "--" ]; then
        shift
        commands=("$@")
    fi
    for path in "${paths[@]}"; do
        [[ "${path}" == /* ]] || return 1
    done

    paths_json="$(jq -cn --args '$ARGS.positional' "${paths[@]}")" || return 1
    commands_json="$(jq -cn --args '$ARGS.positional' "${commands[@]}")" || return 1
    installed_at="$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')" || return 1
    manifest_directory="${HOME}/.agents"
    manifest_path="${manifest_directory}/.installed-manifest.json"
    mkdir -p "${manifest_directory}" || return 1
    temporary_path="$(mktemp "${manifest_path}.tmp.XXXXXX")" || return 1
    chmod 600 "${temporary_path}" || {
        rm -f "${temporary_path}"
        return 1
    }

    local -a jq_arguments=(
        --arg step "${step}"
        --arg installed_at "${installed_at}"
        --arg kind "${kind}"
        --argjson paths "${paths_json}"
        --argjson commands "${commands_json}"
        --arg source_version "${source_version}"
    )
    # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # jq expands these jq variables; the shell must not expand them.
    local jq_filter='
        if type != "object" or ((.steps // {}) | type) != "object" then error("invalid manifest") else . end
        | .version = 1
        | .steps = (.steps // {})
        | .steps[$step] = {
            installed_at: $installed_at,
            kind: $kind,
            paths: $paths,
            commands: $commands,
            source_version: $source_version
        }
    '

    if [ -f "${manifest_path}" ]; then
        jq "${jq_arguments[@]}" "${jq_filter}" "${manifest_path}" > "${temporary_path}" || {
            rm -f "${temporary_path}"
            return 1
        }
    else
        printf '{"version":1,"steps":{}}\n' | jq "${jq_arguments[@]}" "${jq_filter}" > "${temporary_path}" || {
            rm -f "${temporary_path}"
            return 1
        }
    fi
    mv "${temporary_path}" "${manifest_path}" || {
        rm -f "${temporary_path}"
        return 1
    }
}

#
# @description Record one install step without propagating manifest failures.
# @arg $1 string Install step name.
# @arg $2 string Asset kind.
# @arg $3 string Installed source version.
# @arg $@ string Absolute paths followed by an optional `--` and command lines.
# @stderr Prints one warning line when recording fails.
#
function manifest_record() {
    local step="${1:-unknown}"

    if ! _manifest_record "$@" 2> /dev/null; then
        printf 'warning: failed to record asset manifest step %s\n' "${step}" >&2
    fi
    return 0
}

#
# @description Drop manifest records of install steps that no longer exist, so a retired step does
#   not leave a permanent doctor failure. A step exists when its name, before any `:` identity
#   suffix, is a function defined in the calling shell. An absent manifest is left absent.
# @stdout Prints one line per pruned step.
#
function _manifest_prune_retired() {
    local manifest_path temporary_path step steps retired_json
    local -a retired=()

    [ -n "${HOME:-}" ] || return 1
    manifest_path="${HOME}/.agents/.installed-manifest.json"
    [ -f "${manifest_path}" ] || return 0

    steps="$(jq -r 'if type != "object" or ((.steps // {}) | type) != "object" then error("invalid manifest") else (.steps // {}) | keys[] end' "${manifest_path}")" || return 1
    while IFS= read -r step; do
        [ -z "${step}" ] || declare -F "${step%%:*}" > /dev/null || retired+=("${step}")
    done <<< "${steps}"
    [ "${#retired[@]}" -gt 0 ] || return 0

    retired_json="$(jq -cn --args '$ARGS.positional' "${retired[@]}")" || return 1
    temporary_path="$(mktemp "${manifest_path}.tmp.XXXXXX")" || return 1
    chmod 600 "${temporary_path}" || {
        rm -f "${temporary_path}"
        return 1
    }
    # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # jq expands $retired; the shell must not expand it.
    jq --argjson retired "${retired_json}" '.steps |= with_entries(select(.key as $k | $retired | index($k) | not))' "${manifest_path}" > "${temporary_path}" || {
        rm -f "${temporary_path}"
        return 1
    }
    mv "${temporary_path}" "${manifest_path}" || {
        rm -f "${temporary_path}"
        return 1
    }
    for step in "${retired[@]}"; do
        printf 'Pruned retired asset manifest step %s.\n' "${step}"
    done
}

#
# @description Prune retired manifest steps without propagating manifest failures.
# @stdout Prints one line per pruned step.
# @stderr Prints one warning line when pruning fails.
#
function manifest_prune_retired() {
    if ! _manifest_prune_retired 2> /dev/null; then
        printf 'warning: failed to prune retired asset manifest steps\n' >&2
    fi
    return 0
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# shellcheck shell=bash

# @file scripts/lib/github-release.sh
# @brief Resolve the newest GitHub release that has cooled down.
# @description
#   Sourced by the installers that take a GitHub release and by `make docker`.
#   setup.sh runs before the repository exists, so it carries a copy of the
#   functions below; tests/unit/test_github_release.py keeps the copies equal.
#   Only curl or wget and awk are needed, so a fresh machine can run it.

# Releases younger than this stay out: the same 72 hours as minimum_release_age
# in home/dot_mise/config.toml. Change both together.
GITHUB_RELEASE_MIN_AGE_HOURS=72
# gh releases before this forward credentials to TUF mirror hosts during attestation checks
# (GHSA-8xvp-7hj6-mcj9), so an older gh is not used for them.
GITHUB_ATTESTATION_MIN_GH="2.93.0"
# A release tag is a version: the only shape installers, setup.sh and `make docker` accept, so an
# API answer can never smuggle shell syntax or a path into a URL or a command line.
GITHUB_RELEASE_TAG_PATTERN='^v?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*([-.+][0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$'

#
# @description Succeed when GITHUB_SERVER_URL or GH_HOST names a GitHub host other than github.com,
#   as in a GitHub Enterprise Server job: the environment's GITHUB_TOKEN and GH_TOKEN then belong
#   to that host and must never reach github.com.
#
function github_enterprise_context() {
    [ "${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}" != https://github.com ] || [ "${GH_HOST:-github.com}" != github.com ]
}

#
# @description Run gh for github.com, without an Enterprise host's environment tokens.
# @arg $@ string gh's arguments.
#
function github_dotcom_gh() {
    if github_enterprise_context; then
        env -u GITHUB_TOKEN -u GH_TOKEN gh "$@"
    else
        gh "$@"
    fi
}

#
# @description Print the first page of a repository's releases as the GitHub API returns them.
#   GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN or gh's github.com token authenticate the request when one is available.
#   An xtrace the caller turned on (DOTFILES_DEBUG) is off while the credential is handled, and
#   restored afterwards on every path, so a trace never shows it.
# @arg $1 string owner/repo
#
function github_release_list() {
    local status=0 xtrace=""
    case $- in *x*)
        xtrace=1
        set +x
        ;;
    esac
    github_release_fetch "$1" || status=$?
    [ -z "${xtrace}" ] || set -x
    return "${status}"
}

#
# @description The request behind github_release_list; call github_release_list, which keeps it out of a trace.
# @arg $1 string owner/repo
#
function github_release_fetch() {
    local url="https://api.github.com/repos/$1/releases?per_page=30" bearer=""
    # An environment token counts only off an Enterprise host; there it belongs to that host.
    github_enterprise_context || bearer="${GITHUB_TOKEN:-${GH_TOKEN:-}}"
    if [ -z "${bearer}" ] && command -v gh > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        # github.com only: GH_HOST or an Enterprise default host must not send its credential here.
        bearer="$(github_dotcom_gh auth token --hostname github.com 2> /dev/null)" || bearer=""
    fi
    if command -v curl > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        if [ -n "${bearer}" ]; then
            # The credential goes through curl's config on stdin, never the command line.
            printf 'header = "Authorization: Bearer %s"\n' "${bearer}" |
                curl -fsSL -K - -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' "${url}"
        else
            curl -fsSL -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' "${url}"
        fi
    elif [ -n "${bearer}" ]; then
        # wget reads the credential from a private wgetrc (mktemp creates it 0600), never the command line.
        # A subshell whose EXIT trap removes it, with signals turned into exits, so an interruption
        # cannot strand the credential.
        (
            wgetrc="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/github-release.XXXXXX")" || exit 1
            trap 'rm -f "${wgetrc}"' EXIT
            trap 'exit 1' HUP INT TERM
            printf 'header = Authorization: Bearer %s\n' "${bearer}" > "${wgetrc}" || exit 1
            wget --config="${wgetrc}" -qO - --header='Accept: application/vnd.github+json' "${url}"
        )
    else
        wget -qO - --header='Accept: application/vnd.github+json' "${url}"
    fi
}

#
# @description Print the tag of the newest release of a GitHub repository that is neither
#   a draft nor a prerelease and was published at least GITHUB_RELEASE_MIN_AGE_HOURS ago.
# @arg $1 string owner/repo
# @stdout The release tag.
# @exitcode 1 When the release list cannot be fetched, no release qualifies, or the tag is not
#   a version (GITHUB_RELEASE_TAG_PATTERN).
#
function github_release_tag() {
    local cutoff list tag
    cutoff=$(($(date -u +%s) - GITHUB_RELEASE_MIN_AGE_HOURS * 3600))
    cutoff="$(date -u -d "@${cutoff}" +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ 2> /dev/null ||
        date -u -r "${cutoff}" +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" || return 1
    # Fetched whole before parsing, so a failed or truncated download never yields a tag.
    list="$(github_release_list "$1")" || return 1
    # The API pretty-prints each release's own fields at four spaces; nested objects sit deeper.
    tag="$(printf '%s\n' "${list}" | awk -v cutoff="${cutoff}" '
        /^  \{/ { tag = ""; draft = ""; prerelease = ""; published = "" }
        /^    "tag_name": "/ { tag = $0; sub(/^    "tag_name": "/, "", tag); sub(/",?$/, "", tag) }
        /^    "draft": / { draft = ($0 ~ /: false,?$/) ? "no" : "yes" }
        /^    "prerelease": / { prerelease = ($0 ~ /: false,?$/) ? "no" : "yes" }
        /^    "published_at": "/ { published = $0; sub(/^    "published_at": "/, "", published); sub(/",?$/, "", published) }
        /^  \}/ {
            if (tag != "" && draft == "no" && prerelease == "no" && published != "" && published <= cutoff && published > newest) {
                newest = published
                chosen = tag
            }
        }
        END { if (chosen == "") exit 1; print chosen }
    ')" || return 1
    if ! [[ "${tag}" =~ ${GITHUB_RELEASE_TAG_PATTERN} ]]; then
        printf 'unexpected release tag %s for %s\n' "${tag}" "$1" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "${tag}"
}

#
# @description Succeed when a gh at least GITHUB_ATTESTATION_MIN_GH, authenticated to
#   github.com, can verify GitHub release attestations. mise's gh shim comes first, so an
#   older system gh earlier on PATH (Ubuntu's apt gh predates 2.93.0) never hides it.
#
function github_attestation_ready() {
    local PATH="${HOME}/.local/share/mise/shims:${PATH}" version version_output
    command -v gh > /dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    if ! version_output="$(github_dotcom_gh --version 2> /dev/null)"; then
        printf 'gh --version failed, so gh is not used for attestations.\n' >&2
        return 1
    fi
    read -r _ _ version _ <<< "${version_output}"
    # Only a stable X.Y.Z counts: a prerelease such as 2.93.0-rc.1 sorts below the 2.93.0 fix.
    if ! [[ "${version}" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]] ||
        ! printf '%s\n%s\n' "${GITHUB_ATTESTATION_MIN_GH}" "${version}" | awk -F. '
        NR == 1 { split($0, minimum, ".") }
        NR == 2 {
            for (i = 1; i <= 3; i++) {
                if ($i + 0 > minimum[i] + 0) exit 0
                if ($i + 0 < minimum[i] + 0) exit 1
            }
            exit 0
        }'; then
        printf 'gh %s is not a stable release at or after %s (GHSA-8xvp-7hj6-mcj9), so it is not used for attestations.\n' \
            "${version:-unknown}" "${GITHUB_ATTESTATION_MIN_GH}" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    github_dotcom_gh auth status --hostname github.com > /dev/null 2>&1
}

#
# @description Verify a downloaded asset against its GitHub release attestation, which is
#   signed by GitHub for an immutable release and lists every asset's digest.
# @arg $1 string owner/repo
# @arg $2 string The release tag.
# @arg $3 path The downloaded asset.
# @exitcode 0 The attestation verified the asset.
# @exitcode 1 The attestation did not verify the asset.
# @exitcode 2 gh is absent or not authenticated, so nothing was verified.
#
function github_release_attestation() {
    # The same gh github_attestation_ready checked: mise's shim first.
    local PATH="${HOME}/.local/share/mise/shims:${PATH}"
    github_attestation_ready || return 2
    # gh prints its verification report on stdout; it goes to stderr so callers get only the status.
    github_dotcom_gh release verify-asset "$2" "$3" --repo "github.com/$1" 1>&2 || return 1
}

#
# @description Download a release asset and its checksum file, check the checksum and the asset's
#   GitHub release attestation now (no deferral), and print the asset's sha256, so a build without
#   gh can check the asset against it (`make docker` passes it to the Dockerfile). Needs curl.
# @arg $1 string owner/repo
# @arg $2 string The release tag.
# @arg $3 string The asset name.
# @arg $4 string The name of the release's checksum file.
# @stdout The verified asset's sha256.
# @exitcode 1 A download, the checksum or the attestation failed.
# @exitcode 2 No gh 2.93.0 or newer is authenticated to github.com, so nothing was downloaded.
#
function github_release_verified_sha256() (
    local actual base="https://github.com/$1/releases/download/$2" dir expected sum
    github_attestation_ready || return 2
    dir="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/github-release.XXXXXX")" || return 1
    trap 'rm -rf "${dir}"' EXIT
    curl -fsSL "${base}/$3" -o "${dir}/$3" || return 1
    curl -fsSL "${base}/$4" -o "${dir}/$4" || return 1
    expected="$(awk -v name="$3" '$2 == name { print $1; exit }' "${dir}/$4")"
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        sum="$(sha256sum "${dir}/$3")" || {
            printf 'sha256sum could not hash %s\n' "$3" >&2
            return 1
        }
    else
        sum="$(shasum -a 256 "${dir}/$3")" || {
            printf 'shasum -a 256 could not hash %s\n' "$3" >&2
            return 1
        }
    fi
    actual="${sum%% *}"
    if [ -z "${expected}" ] || [ "${actual}" != "${expected}" ]; then
        printf 'Checksum mismatch for %s\n' "$3" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    github_release_attestation "$1" "$2" "${dir}/$3" || return 1
    printf '%s\n' "${actual}"
)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file bus-history.sh
# @brief Print a team's hcom bus history as TSV rows the records can paste.
# @description
#   Plan 025 W2b (C-1). Reads `hcom events --type message --thread <team> --full
#   --last <limit> [--after <since>]` (`hcom events --help`; hcom 0.7.30 and 0.7.31,
#   measured 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-24; at v0.7.30 src/commands/events.rs:33 last,
#   :39 full; `--last` is `ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT n`, events.rs:185, so the newest
#   rows) and prints one row per message,
#   ascending by id: `id<TAB>at<TAB>from<TAB>to<TAB>kind<TAB>body`. `at` is hcom's
#   `ts` as printed, `to` the delivered_to names joined with commas (`-` when
#   none), `kind` the first word of the text, and `body` the text with backslash,
#   tab, CR and LF escaped as `\\`, `\t`, `\r` and `\n`, so every row is one line
#   of five tabs. `--kind` keeps only the rows whose kind equals it. Never writes:
#   the store `$HCOM_DIR/hcom.db` must already exist, because `hcom events`
#   creates one on first use (observed with 0.7.30 and 0.7.31).
# @arg $1 string Team, the hcom thread (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`).
# @option --limit <n> Newest rows to read (default 200, a positive integer).
# @option --since <ts> Only rows after this time, hcom's `--after` (`YYYY-MM-DD[THH:MM:SS[Z]]`).
# @option --kind <kind> Only rows of this kind, the first word of the line (e.g. RESULT).
# @env HCOM_DIR The private hcom store directory; default: the store derived from the checkout (regime-env).
# @stdout TSV rows `id<TAB>at<TAB>from<TAB>to<TAB>kind<TAB>body`, possibly none.
# @exitcode 0 Printed.
# @exitcode 1 Usage error, store absent, or hcom failed (its error on stderr).
# @example
#   HCOM_DIR=/path/to/.hcom scripts/orchestrator/bus-history.sh dotfiles --limit 50 --kind RESULT
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
# @set LEVER_DIR The physical directory of this file, where the sourced regime-env helper sits (U33).
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    # shellcheck disable=SC2034 # read by the levers that source regime-env from this directory
    LEVER_DIR=${dir}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

usage='usage: bus-history.sh <team> [--limit <n>] [--since <ts>] [--kind <kind>]'
(($# >= 1)) || {
    echo "${usage}" >&2
    exit 1
}
team=$1
shift
limit=200 since='' kind=''
while (($#)); do
    (($# >= 2)) || {
        echo "${usage}" >&2
        exit 1
    }
    case $1 in
    --limit) limit=$2 ;;
    --since) since=$2 ;;
    --kind) kind=$2 ;;
    *)
        echo "${usage}" >&2
        exit 1
        ;;
    esac
    shift 2
done
[[ ${team} =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$ ]] || {
    echo "bus-history: team '${team}' is outside ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}\$" >&2
    exit 1
}
[[ ${limit} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || {
    echo 'bus-history: --limit must be a positive integer' >&2
    exit 1
}
# The store is HCOM_DIR when set, else the one derived from this checkout (regime-env, regime-cutover U33); a
# derived store that does not exist yet is refused like an explicit one, because `hcom events` would create it.
[[ -r ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env ]] || {
    echo "bus-history: refused: regime-env unreadable beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env" >&2
    exit 1
}
# shellcheck source=scripts/orchestrator/regime-env
. "${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env"
regime_env bus-history || exit 1
[[ -n ${HCOM_DIR:-} && -f ${HCOM_DIR:-}/hcom.db ]] || {
    echo "bus-history: store absent: \${HCOM_DIR}/hcom.db (HCOM_DIR=${HCOM_DIR:-unset})" >&2
    exit 1
}

query=(events --type message --thread "${team}" --full --last "${limit}")
[[ -z ${since} ]] || query+=(--after "${since}")
rows=$(hcom "${query[@]}") || exit 1
jq -rn --arg kind "${kind}" '
  def kind_of: [splits("[ \t]+") | select(. != "")][0] // "-";
  def escaped: gsub("\\\\"; "\\\\") | gsub("\t"; "\\t") | gsub("\r"; "\\r") | gsub("\n"; "\\n");
  [inputs | select(.type == "message")] | sort_by(.id)[]
  | select($kind == "" or (.data.text | kind_of) == $kind)
  | [(.id | tostring), .ts, (.data.from // "-"),
     ((.data.delivered_to // []) | if length == 0 then "-" else join(",") end),
     (.data.text | kind_of), (.data.text | escaped)]
  | join("\t")' <<< "${rows}"

docs.text: Plan 024 P1-3 (T133). Reads the run with gh run view <run-id> --json, the log of each job whose conclusion is failure (--log-failed), timed_out or cancelled (--log), and the signatures of .github/flakes.yaml (a list of {id, job, log_regex, note}; job and log_regex are extended regular expressions, matched with grep -E against the job name and its log). A job with no log matches nothing. A pull-request run must belong to exactly one pull request whose current head is the run's headSha, checked before the logs are read and again right before the rerun: a superseded head's rerun would re-enter pr-<N> and cancel the newest head's run. When every such job matches a signature, the run is reserved by an atomic mkdir(2) of .orchestration/validation/ci-reruns.lock.d/<run-id> (through python3's os.mkdir), one <utc>\t<run-id>\t<headSha>\t<job>\t<signature id> row per job is appended to .orchestration/validation/ci-reruns.tsv, and only then gh run rerun <run-id> --failed runs. The reservation stays after success, failure or interruption, so a run is rerun at most once, and it blocks only its own run. All of these live in the checkout this script lives in (git rev-parse --show-toplevel there). Before reading anything, uv, python3, gh, jq, git and mkdir are resolved as mise which answers them under env -i from / (else command -v). Each answer is followed through every link to its physical file, which must be an executable regular file and no shim: neither a file named mise in any letter case nor the mise binary itself (same device and inode; a mise shim is a link to it), nor a file in a directory named shims in any letter case, as found or as resolved. An answer (captured with its own trailing newlines), link or directory whose path holds a control character is refused too; otherwise the script exits 1. Only the checked physical file is ever run: all but python3 are linked by it into a private directory, created under TMPDIR when it is absolute with no ':' or control character, else wherever mktemp puts it with TMPDIR unset, then used only by its physical path, which must have no ':' either (else exit 1) and be this user's with mode 0700 (removed on exit and on HUP, INT or TERM), and PATH becomes those links then /usr/bin:/bin. python3 is always started by its physical path, never a link (CPython reads a pyvenv.cfg beside and above the path it starts by), as python3 -I and as uv's --python for uv run --no-config --no-project under env -i from the root, so no checkout's .python-version, .venv or executable and no inherited UV_, VIRTUAL_ENV or PYTHON variable picks the interpreter (security:4fe2438:1). Before PATH is pinned, every other command (mktemp, env, find, ln and the EXIT trap's rm) runs by its absolute system path; mise, the resolver itself, is the one program found through PATH.
